model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [c-Fos+Alexa Fluor 647, NeuN+Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole adult mouse brain clearing due to its excellent preservation of fluorescent proteins and immunolabeling signals, rapid clearing speed, and compatibility with light-sheet microscopy. It is particularly suitable for mapping activated neurons using c-Fos as a marker. The use of c-Fos (Alexa Fluor 647) allows identification of behaviorally activated neurons, NeuN (Alexa Fluor 488) labels all neurons for comprehensive mapping, and DAPI provides nuclear counterstaining to aid in anatomical registration and segmentation.  

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Preprocessing  
1.1 Incubation with methanol series (20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100%) in PBS-T (0.2% Triton X-100), each step for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 5 days total)  
1.2 Incubation with chilled 100% methanol for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 1 day)  
1.3 Incubation with chilled 1:1 methanol:benzyl ether (BEM) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 1 day)  
1.4 Incubation with 100% BEM for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 1 day)  

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Incubation with primary antibody solution: c-Fos (1:1000), NeuN (1:1000) in 100% BEM with 6% (wt/vol) dextran sulfate, 0.3 M NaCl, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 7 days)  
2.2 Wash with 100% BEM, 5 times, 2 hours each. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 10 hours total)  
2.3 Incubation with secondary antibody solution: Alexa Fluor 647 anti-rabbit, Alexa Fluor 488 anti-mouse (1:500 each) in 100% BEM with 6% dextran sulfate, 0.3 M NaCl. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 7 days)  
2.4 Wash with 100% BEM, 5 times, 2 hours each. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 10 hours total)  

3 Nuclear Staining  
3.1 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 in 100% BEM) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 1 day)  
3.2 Wash with 100% BEM, 3 times, 1 hour each. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 3 hours total)  

4 Tissue Optical Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (100% dibenzyl ether, DBE) without shaking. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
5.1 Incubation with fresh 100% DBE for RI matching and final clearing. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Store sample in 100% DBE at RT in the dark until imaging.  
6.2 Mount brain in custom chamber filled with DBE for light-sheet or confocal imaging.

The selected labeling strategy enables comprehensive visualization of neuronal somata (NeuN), axons/dendrites (β-III Tubulin), and nuclear architecture (DAPI), which aligns with the goal of generating a 3D morphological atlas of neurons and fiber tracts.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling (if not already performed)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization solution (0.3% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 10% FBS in PBS) for 3 days. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-NeuN (1:500) and anti-β-III Tubulin (1:1000) in labeling solution (0.3% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 5% FBS in PBS) for 7 days. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 168 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100 (PBT), 3 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488 anti-mouse (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 647 anti-rabbit (1:500) in labeling solution for 5 days. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 120 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBT, 3 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  
1.6 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000) in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.7 Wash with PBS, 2 × 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour total)

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol, 2 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 5% H₂O₂ in methanol (1:5 dilution of 30% H₂O₂ in methanol) at 4 °C for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% methanol, 2 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)

4.1 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

6.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (DBE) for 2 hours prior to imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

7.1 Mount brain in DBE within a custom chamber or imaging cuvette.  
7.2 Store in DBE at RT in the dark for up to several weeks.

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [c-Fos, Npas4]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is highly suitable for whole adult mouse brain clearing, offering excellent tissue penetration, rapid processing, and strong preservation of fluorescence signals from endogenous reporters and immunolabeled immediate early gene (IEG) proteins like c-Fos and Npas4. It is particularly effective for 3D imaging and spatial mapping of sparse neuronal activation patterns across the whole brain. The methanol-based delipidation minimizes tissue swelling and maintains structural integrity, while the refractive index matching ensures high-resolution imaging deep within the tissue. This method is compatible with commonly used fluorophores (e.g., Alexa Fluor, GFP, tdTomato) and avoids the need for additional labeling beyond the two IEGs of interest.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Optical Clearing  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (v/v) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (v/v) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (v/v) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with chilled 100% methanol (freshly prepared) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 1:2 (vol/vol) H2O2:methanol solution (1 volume of 30% H2O2 in 2 volumes of methanol) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Replace with fresh H2O2:methanol solution (1:2) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Wash with 100% methanol (3×, 1 hour each) (Temperature: 4 °C)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (v/v) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (v/v) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (v/v) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with PBS (3×, 1 hour each) (Temperature: 4 °C)  

4 Immunolabeling  
4.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% donkey serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-c-Fos (1:1000) and anti-Npas4 (1:500) in labeling buffer (1% donkey serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
4.3 Wash with PBS + 0.1% Triton X-100 (5×, 24 hours each) (Temperature: 4 °C)  
4.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488 anti-rabbit (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 647 anti-mouse (1:500) in labeling buffer (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
4.5 Wash with PBS + 0.1% Triton X-100 (5×, 24 hours each) (Temperature: 4 °C)  

5 Dehydration  
5.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (v/v) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (v/v) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (v/v) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 1 hour)  
5.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (v/v) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 1 hour)  
5.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (3×, 1 hour each) (Temperature: 4 °C)  

6 Delipidation and Clearing  
6.1 Incubation with freshly prepared dichloromethane (DCM) and methanol (1:1 vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
6.2 Replace with fresh DCM:methanol (1:1) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
6.3 Incubation with 100% DCM (2×, 1 hour each) (Temperature: RT)  

7 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
7.1 Incubation with dibenzyl ether (DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
7.2 Replace with fresh DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

8 Imaging and Storage  
8.1 Mount brain in DBE-filled imaging chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy  
8.2 Store in DBE at RT in the dark for long-term preservation

**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1)+Alexa Fluor 488, GAP43+Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for large, fixed nervous tissue like spinal cords due to its excellent preservation of fluorescent signals, rapid clearing, and compatibility with multiple antibody labeling. It uses organic solvents to remove lipids, enabling deep penetration and high-resolution 3D imaging with light-sheet or confocal microscopy. β-III Tubulin labels all axons, while GAP43 highlights regenerating axons, allowing distinction between preserved and newly regrown fibers. This dual labeling strategy enables precise 3D reconstruction and analysis of axonal continuity and directionality around the injury site.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling (if not already performed)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization solution (10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-β-III Tubulin (1:1000) and anti-GAP43 (1:500) in labeling solution (1% DMSO, 3% donkey serum, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 7 days. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 7 days)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBST), 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit (or species-matched) at 1:500 dilution in labeling solution for 4 days. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 4 days)  
1.5 Wash with PBST, 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.6 Incubation with chilled 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1:20 dilution of 30% H₂O₂ in methanol) overnight. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Wash with 100% methanol, 3 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

4 Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 1:1 DCM:BABB (benzyl alcohol:benzyl benzoate, 1:1 vol/vol) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 100% BABB for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
5.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (BABB containing 0.5% (wt/vol) N-phenyl-1-naphthylamine if needed for auto-fluorescence suppression) for at least 24 hours before imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

6.1 Store sample in BABB at RT in the dark until imaging.  
6.2 Mount sample in a custom chamber with BABB to match RI of the objective (e.g., glycerol or BABB-matched immersion objectives).  
6.3 Perform 3D imaging using light-sheet or confocal microscopy optimized for Alexa Fluor 488 and Alexa Fluor 647 channels.

2.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP, mCherry]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is highly suitable for large, fixed tissue samples like rat spinal cords due to its excellent optical clearing, preservation of fluorescent proteins (e.g., GFP and mCherry), and compatibility with deep imaging using light-sheet or confocal microscopes. It is fast compared to aqueous-based methods and supports high-resolution 3D imaging of long-range neural fibers. The dual labeling with GFP and mCherry allows for clear distinction between mature (mCherry-labeled) and regenerating (GFP-labeled) axons, enabling precise spatial mapping of fiber trajectories across the injury site.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Permeabilization and Blocking  
1.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 5% H₂O₂ in methanol at 4 °C to quench endogenous peroxidases. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with 70% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with blocking solution (0.3% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 0.1% BSA in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Primary Antibody Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: chicken anti-GFP (1:1000) and rabbit anti-mCherry (1:1000) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  

3 Washing  
3.1 Wash with 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS (PBST) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Repeat wash step 3.1 for a total of 3 times.  

4 Secondary Antibody Labeling  
4.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-chicken (1:1000) and Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-rabbit (1:1000) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  

5 Washing  
5.1 Wash with PBST for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Repeat wash step 5.1 for a total of 3 times.  

6 Dehydration  
6.1 Incubation with 50% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Incubation with 70% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.3 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.4 Repeat step 6.3 with fresh 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

7 Delipidation and Clearing  
7.1 Incubation with freshly prepared dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.2 Incubation with DCM containing 0.2% (vol/vol) TDE (2,2’-thiodiethanol) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.3 Incubation with DCM containing 3% (vol/vol) TDE for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.4 Incubation with DCM containing 5% (vol/vol) TDE for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.5 Incubation with DCM containing 10% (vol/vol) TDE for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.6 Incubation with DCM containing 20% (vol/vol) TDE for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.7 Incubation with DCM containing 30% (vol/vol) TDE for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.8 Incubation with DCM containing 40% (vol/vol) TDE for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.9 Incubation with DCM containing 50% (vol/vol) TDE for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

8 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
8.1 Incubation with dibenzyl ether (DBE) for RI matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Replace with fresh DBE and incubate until full clearing is achieved (typically 3–6 hours). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3–6 hours)  

9 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
9.1 Store sample in DBE at 4 °C in the dark until imaging. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: up to 2 weeks)  
9.2 Prior to imaging, equilibrate the sample in fresh DBE for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1), GFAP]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for spinal cord clearing due to its excellent preservation of fluorescence, compatibility with immunolabeling, and ability to clear large, fixed tissues without the need for electrophoretic steps that can damage fragile samples. It is particularly suitable for 3D mapping of neural fibers due to its high optical homogeneity and minimal tissue distortion. β-III Tubulin labels both mature and regenerating axons, making it ideal for tracing long-distance fiber continuity, while GFAP labels astrocytes and glial scar borders, which is critical for identifying the injury core and assessing axonal interactions with the scar environment.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling (if not already performed)
1.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization solution: 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-β-III Tubulin (1:1000) + anti-GFAP (1:1000) in labeling buffer (0.2% Triton X-100, 5% DMSO in PBS) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 (3 × 24 hours at RT)
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488 anti-mouse + Alexa Fluor 647 anti-rabbit (1:1000) in labeling buffer (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)
1.5 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 (3 × 24 hours at RT)

2 Dehydration
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (2 changes) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)

3 Bleaching (optional for autofluorescence reduction)
3.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H2O2 in methanol (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)
3.2 Rinse with 100% methanol (2 × 30 min at RT)
3.3 Incubation with fresh 5% H2O2 in methanol (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)

4 Rehydration
4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.5 Incubation with PBS (3 × 1 hour at RT)

5 Delipidation (Clearing)
5.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (200 mM dibasic sodium phosphate, 15% (wt/vol) N-butyldiethanolamine, 20% (vol/vol) DMSO, pH 8.5) (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 72–96 hours or until tissue becomes translucent)
5.2 Replace with fresh iDISCO+ solution and continue incubation until full clearing is achieved (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 48–72 hours)

6 Refractive Index (RI) Matching
6.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS (pH 7.4) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
6.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
6.3 Incubation with 100% glycerol (2 changes) (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours total)

7 Mounting and Imaging Preparation
7.1 Transfer tissue into a glass-bottom imaging dish or custom chamber with 100% glycerol
7.2 Ensure tissue is fully submerged and oriented for light-sheet or confocal imaging
7.3 Store at 4 °C in 100% glycerol if imaging is not immediate (fluorescence is stable for weeks)

**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP, DiD]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is ideal for large, whole-organ CNS samples due to its high tissue penetration, excellent preservation of fluorescent proteins (like GFP), and compatibility with lipophilic tracers such as DiD. It enables rapid and deep clearing of tissues up to several centimeters in size, making it suitable for tracing long-range projections from cortex to spinal cord. The method is compatible with light-sheet microscopy and allows for long-term storage and repeated imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Washing and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 and 5% DMSO for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Fluorescent Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with DiD (1:200 dilution in PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100 and 5% DMSO) for retrograde labeling of long-range projections. (Temperature: RT, Time: 72 hours)  
2.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 (3× 1 hour each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol overnight. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

4 Delipidation and Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with freshly prepared dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with DCM for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with DCM containing 5% Tween-20 for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Rehydration and Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
5.1 Incubation with 80% DCM in methanol for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with 60% DCM in methanol for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.3 Incubation with 40% DCM in methanol for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.4 Incubation with 20% DCM in methanol for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.6 Incubation with BABB (1:2 benzyl alcohol : benzyl benzoate) for RI matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Optional Long-Term Storage and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Incubation with fresh BABB for 12 hours prior to imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
6.2 Mount sample in BABB-filled imaging chamber with support structure to prevent mechanical deformation. (Temperature: RT, Time: N/A)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (e.g., from Thy1-GFP mouse), MBP (Myelin Basic Protein) antibody + Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated secondary]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for large, intact CNS samples due to its excellent optical clearing, compatibility with endogenous and immunolabeled fluorescence, and ability to preserve fine axonal structures over long distances. It is particularly suitable for 3D imaging of long-range projections in whole CNS tissue. The dual labeling strategy with GFP-labeled cortical projection neurons and MBP immunostaining allows for clear distinction between specific long-range projections and the general axonal scaffold, enabling precise mapping of fiber trajectories, branching, and termination patterns across the brain-spinal cord axis.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling (if not already performed)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization solution: 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-MBP (1:500 dilution) in iDISCO+ antibody solution (1% DMSO, 3% donkey serum, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 7 days)  
1.3 Wash with iDISCO+ wash buffer (0.2% Triton X-100, 0.05% Tween-20 in PBS) 6 times over 48 hours at 4 °C.  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) in iDISCO+ antibody solution. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 7 days)  
1.5 Wash with iDISCO+ wash buffer 6 times over 48 hours at 4 °C.  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 5% H₂O₂ in methanol (1:20 dilution of 30% H₂O₂ in methanol). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 1:1 (vol/vol) DCM:MeOH. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (1:2 benzyl alcohol:benzyl benzoate, BABB). (Temperature: RT, Time: 48–72 hours or until fully transparent)  

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
5.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution: dibenzyl ether (DBE). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24–48 hours)  

6 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Mount sample in custom chamber or imaging cuvette with DBE.  
6.2 Image using light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) or high-penetration confocal microscopy.  

7 Storage (if needed)  
7.1 Store cleared sample in DBE at 4 °C in the dark. (Time: up to several months without significant signal loss)

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-MBP (1:500 dilution) in PBST (0.2% Triton X-100) with 5% DMSO and 3% donkey serum. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 72 hours)

2.3 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse/rabbit IgG (1:1000) in PBST with 5% DMSO. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 72 hours)

3.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 6 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 6 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 6 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
3.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 6 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 2 × 6 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours total)

4.1 Incubation with freshly prepared dichloromethane (DCM) and methanol (2:1 vol/vol) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% dichloromethane (DCM) for 6 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)

6.2 Seal chamber with vacuum grease and parafilm to prevent evaporation.  
6.3 Store at RT in the dark until imaging.  
6.4 Image using light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) or high-penetration confocal microscopy with appropriate filters for GFP and Alexa Fluor 647.

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP, MBP]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for large, whole-organ CNS samples due to its excellent tissue preservation, compatibility with endogenous fluorescent proteins (like GFP), and efficient clearing of lipids without causing significant shrinkage. It also allows for high-resolution 3D imaging across long distances (e.g., cortex to spinal cord), which is essential for tracing long-range projections. The MBP antibody labels the global axonal network, providing a spatial reference for the specific GFP-labeled projection. iDISCO+ includes a bleaching step to reduce autofluorescence and improve signal-to-noise, while preserving fluorescence intensity better than pure methanol-based protocols.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Bleaching  
1.1 Incubation with chilled 5% H₂O₂ in methanol (1:5 dilution of 30% H₂O₂ in methanol) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Repeat step 1.1 with fresh solution (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Rehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS (vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS (vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS (vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS (vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.5 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Blocking and Antibody Labeling  
3.1 Incubation with blocking solution (0.3% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 5% donkey serum in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-MBP (1:500 dilution in blocking solution) (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 7 days)  
3.3 Wash with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, 5× 24 hours)  
3.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:1000 in blocking solution) (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 7 days)  
3.5 Wash with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, 5× 24 hours)  

4 Delipidation (Clearing)  
4.1 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with 1:1 methanol:dichloromethane (vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with 100% dichloromethane (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
4.4 Incubation with 100% dichloromethane (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
5.1 Incubation with 1:2 benzyl alcohol:benzyl benzoate (BABB) (vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% BABB (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  

6 Final Sample Stabilization and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Mount sample in custom chamber with 100% BABB to maintain RI matching  
6.2 Store in light-protected container at RT until imaging  
6.3 Image using light-sheet or two-photon microscopy with appropriate filters for GFP and Alexa Fluor 647

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [6E10 (Alexa Fluor 488), Congo red (Alexa Fluor 647)]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole mouse brain clearing, offering excellent preservation of fluorescent signals, deep penetration, and compatibility with multiple immunolabeling strategies. It is fast compared to hydrogel-based methods and avoids the need for electrophoretic equipment. The methanol-based delipidation is effective for lipid removal while maintaining antigenicity and fluorescent protein stability. 6E10 is a well-established N-terminal Aβ antibody that labels diffuse and fibrillar plaques, while Congo red is a classical amyloid dye with high specificity for β-sheet structures. Using both labels allows spatial cross-validation of Aβ pathology in 3D across cortical and hippocampal regions. Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 are spectrally distinct, photostable, and compatible with iDISCO+ clearing and light-sheet imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling  
1.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization solution (10% DMSO, 5% donkey serum, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody 6E10 (1:500 dilution in labeling buffer: 3% DMSO, 0.2% Triton X-100, 1% BSA in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 (3 × 24 hours). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 3 × 24 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody (Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG, 1:1000 in labeling buffer) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 (3 × 24 hours). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 3 × 24 hours)  
1.6 Incubation with Congo red (0.2% in PBS) containing Alexa Fluor 647 NHS ester (1:1000) for 48 hours to label fibrillar amyloid. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.7 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 (3 × 24 hours). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 3 × 24 hours)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.6 Incubation with 100% methanol for additional 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 5% H₂O₂ in methanol (1:5 dilution of 30% H₂O₂ in methanol) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM) for 4 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with DCM for additional 4 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 1:1 DCM:methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% methanol for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.3 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.4 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.5 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.6 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.7 Incubation with PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
5.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (DBE:Tween 20, 2:1 vol/vol) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with fresh iDISCO+ clearing solution for additional 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Transfer brain into a glass-bottom imaging dish.  
6.2 Cover brain with a small volume of fresh iDISCO+ clearing solution.  
6.3 Seal dish with parafilm to prevent evaporation during imaging.  
6.4 Image using light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) or two-photon confocal system optimized for cleared tissue.  

7 Storage (if not imaging immediately)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [6E10 (Alexa Fluor 488), Congo red (Alexa Fluor 594)]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole mouse brain clearing, offering excellent preservation of fluorescent signals, fast processing, and compatibility with immunolabeling. It is particularly suitable for 3D quantitative imaging of amyloid-β pathology in AD models. The dual labeling with 6E10 (specific for amyloid-β) and Congo red (binds to amyloid fibrils) ensures high-confidence identification of amyloid plaques, minimizing false positives due to autofluorescence or non-specific particles. Both dyes are compatible with iDISCO+ protocols and emit in spectrally distinct channels.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling and Staining  
1.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization solution (0.3% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 5% donkey serum in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody 6E10 (1:1000 in blocking solution) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100 (3 × 24 hours). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 3 × 24 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody (Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG, 1:500 in blocking solution) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100 (3 × 24 hours). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 3 × 24 hours)  
1.6 Incubation with Congo red (0.2% in PBS containing 50% ethanol, pH 8.0) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.7 Wash with PBS containing 50% ethanol (3 × 6 hours). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 6 hours)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 2 hours (2 changes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 2 hours)  

3 Delipidation and Clearing  
3.1 Incubation with freshly prepared dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with DCM containing 5% H2O2 for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with fresh DCM for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.6 Incubation with PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
5.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ RI matching solution (DBE/Toluene, 1:2 vol/vol) for 3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with iDISCO+ final RI matching solution (DBE/Toluene, 1:1 vol/vol) for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

6 Sample Preservation and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Mount brain in a custom chamber filled with DBE/Toluene (1:1) for light-sheet or confocal imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: N/A)  
6.2 Store unused samples in 1:2 DBE/Toluene at 4 °C for up to 2 weeks. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: up to 2 weeks)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [6E10+Alexa Fluor 488, 4G8+Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole mouse brain clearing with excellent preservation of fluorescent signals, especially for immunolabeled targets. It is fast, scalable, and compatible with multiple fluorophores, making it suitable for dual labeling of Aβ plaques with two distinct antibodies (6E10 and 4G8) for cross-validated 3D mapping. The methanol-based dehydration and DBE-based refractive index (RI) matching provide high tissue transparency and optical homogeneity, enabling deep imaging of cortical and hippocampal regions. Dual labeling with spectrally distinct Alexa Fluor dyes ensures reliable detection and quantification of Aβ pathology across the entire brain.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: 6E10 (1:500) + 4G8 (1:500) in labeling buffer (1% DMSO, 3% donkey serum, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBST), 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:1000) + Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse IgG2a (1:1000) in labeling buffer for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBST, 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.6 Incubation with chilled 100% methanol for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Bleaching (optional for autofluorescence reduction)  
3.1 Incubation with 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Wash with 100% methanol, 3 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

4 Delipidation and Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with 1:1 (vol/vol) methanol:Dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% DCM for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 1:1 (vol/vol) DCM:DBE for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 100% DBE for 3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
4.5 Incubation with fresh 100% DBE for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  

5 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Transfer brain into a glass-bottom imaging dish or custom chamber.  
5.2 Add fresh 100% DBE to submerge the brain.  
5.3 Seal the dish to prevent evaporation.  
5.4 Store at 4 °C until imaging. (Time: up to 1 week)  
5.5 Image using light-sheet or high-penetration confocal microscopy with 488 nm and 640 nm excitation lasers.

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD31+Alexa Fluor 647, GFAP+Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole tissue clearing of fixed mouse brain samples, offering excellent preservation of fluorescent signals (including Alexa Fluor dyes), rapid delipidation, and compatibility with immunolabeled antigens. It is particularly suitable for 3D imaging of vascular networks and tumor morphology. CD31 labels endothelial cells for visualization of the entire vasculature, while GFAP labels astrocytes and reactive gliosis, enabling delineation of tumor boundaries and invasion patterns. This combination allows for high-resolution 3D mapping of tumor-vascular interactions.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling (if not already performed)  
1.1 Incubate tissue in blocking solution (10% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubate with primary antibodies: rat anti-CD31 (1:200) and rabbit anti-GFAP (1:500) in 3% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with 0.1% Tween-20 in PBS (PBST), 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
1.4 Incubate with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated goat anti-rat and Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated goat anti-rabbit (both at 1:500) in 3% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBST, 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubate in 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubate in 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubate in 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubate in 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubate in 100% methanol, 2 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubate in freshly prepared 5% H₂O₂ in methanol (1:5 dilution of 30% H₂O₂ in methanol) at 4 °C for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Incubate in 100% dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubate in 1:1 DCM:DBE for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubate in 100% dibenzyl ether (DBE) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
4.1 Incubate in 50% glycerol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.2 Incubate in 80% glycerol in PBS overnight. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.3 Incubate in 100% glycerol for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Transfer sample to a glass-bottom imaging dish or chambered coverslip.  
5.2 Immerse in 100% glycerol for imaging.  
5.3 Seal chamber with silicone grease or imaging-compatible adhesive coverslip.  

6 Optional Long-Term Storage  
6.1 Store cleared and labeled sample in 100% glycerol at 4 °C in the dark. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: indefinite)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD31+Alexa Fluor 647, Claudin-5+Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole organs or large tissue blocks like mouse brain, offering excellent optical clearing, lipid removal, and preservation of fluorescent signals. It is particularly suitable for 3D imaging of vascular networks and barrier structures. The methanol-based protocol preserves endogenous fluorescence and allows high-resolution imaging deep into the tissue. CD31 labels all endothelial cells for visualization of the full vascular network, while Claudin-5 labels tight junctions to assess blood-brain barrier integrity. This dual labeling enables spatial comparison of vascular architecture and barrier disruption between tumor and non-tumor regions.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling Completion and Washing  
1.1 Wash tissue block 3× 1 hour each with PBS containing 0.2% Tween-20 (PBSTw) at RT to remove excess antibodies.  
1.2 Incubate in PBSTw overnight at 4 °C to ensure complete removal of unbound antibodies.

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubate tissue in 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour at RT.  
2.2 Transfer to 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour at RT.  
2.3 Move to 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour at RT.  
2.4 Incubate in 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour at RT.  
2.5 Transfer to 100% methanol for 2 hours at RT (repeat once with fresh methanol).

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubate tissue in freshly prepared 66% dichloromethane (DCM)/33% methanol solution for 2 hours at RT.  
3.2 Replace with fresh solution and incubate overnight at RT.  
3.3 Repeat step 3.1 for 2 more cycles (total 3 cycles of 2 hours each) to ensure complete delipidation.

4 Bleaching (Optional for Autofluorescence Reduction)  
4.1 Incubate in chilled 5% H2O2 in methanol at 4 °C for 12–16 hours.  
4.2 Wash with 100% methanol until bubbles stop (2–3 washes, 30 min each at RT).

5 Rehydration  
5.1 Incubate in 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour at RT.  
5.2 Transfer to 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour at RT.  
5.3 Move to 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour at RT.  
5.4 Incubate in 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour at RT.  
5.5 Wash 3× 1 hour each with PBSTw at RT.

6 Mounting and Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
6.1 Incubate tissue in iDISCO+ RI matching solution (DBE:Tween-20 = 2:1 vol/vol) for 12–24 hours at RT.  
6.2 Replace with fresh RI matching solution and incubate until tissue becomes fully transparent (typically 12–24 hours more).  
6.3 Store or image in the same RI matching solution to maintain optical clarity and fluorescence.

7 Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Mount tissue in a custom imaging chamber or glass-bottom dish using DBE-based mounting medium.  
7.2 Seal chamber with vacuum grease or silicone to prevent evaporation during long-term imaging.  
7.3 Perform light-sheet or high-penetration confocal imaging to capture 3D vascular architecture and Claudin-5 signal.

**Chosen Method:** ScaleS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD31+Alexa Fluor 647, Claudin-5+Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** ScaleS is a sucrose-based, non-detergent tissue clearing method that provides excellent structural preservation, especially for fine vasculature and tight junction proteins like Claudin-5. It is particularly suitable for fixed tissues with preserved fluorescence (e.g., Alexa Fluor dyes), and it avoids the mechanical stress and swelling associated with detergent-based methods like CUBIC. This ensures minimal distortion of tumor architecture, vascular continuity, and perivascular tumor invasion patterns. The selected labeling strategy targets both vascular structure (CD31) and blood-brain barrier integrity (Claudin-5), aligning with the scientific goals.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preprocessing  
1.1 Incubation with 10% (wt/vol) sucrose in PBS for cryoprotection. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 20% (wt/vol) sucrose in PBS for full equilibration. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: rat anti-CD31 (1:200) and rabbit anti-Claudin-5 (1:100) in labeling buffer (3% NGS, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
2.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100 (3 × 24 hours at RT)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated goat anti-rat IgG and Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated goat anti-rabbit IgG (both at 1:500). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
2.5 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100 (3 × 24 hours at RT)  

3 ScaleS Clearing  
3.1 Incubation with ScaleS-1 solution (4 M urea, 10% (wt/vol) glycerol, 25% (wt/vol) sucrose in 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, pH 8.5). (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with ScaleS-2 solution (4 M urea, 20% (wt/vol) glycerol, 50% (wt/vol) sucrose in 0.1% Triton X-100, pH 8.5). (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with ScaleS-3 solution (4 M urea, 30% (wt/vol) glycerol, 60% (wt/vol) sucrose in 0.1% Triton X-100, pH 8.5). (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 72 hours)  

4 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
4.1 Incubation with ScaleS-4 solution (4 M urea, 40% (wt/vol) glycerol, 70% (wt/vol) sucrose in 0.1% Triton X-100, pH 8.5). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with ScaleS-5 solution (4 M urea, 50% (wt/vol) glycerol, 80% (wt/vol) sucrose in 0.1% Triton X-100, pH 8.5). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Transfer tissue into a custom imaging chamber with ScaleS-5 solution for light-sheet or deep-tissue confocal imaging.  
5.2 Optional: For long-term storage, incubate in ScaleS-Storage solution (4 M urea, 50% (wt/vol) glycerol, 80% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.02% NaN3, pH 8.5). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: indefinite)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is ideal for whole-organ clearing of fixed tissues, especially for preserving endogenous fluorescent proteins like GFP over long periods. It achieves high transparency and optical homogeneity, which is critical for 3D imaging of sparse, weakly fluorescent neurons. The use of endogenous GFP combined with Alexa Fluor 647-labeled MAP2 enhances signal contrast for neuronal soma and dendrites, enabling detailed morphological analysis. uDISCO also allows for long-term storage and re-imaging without significant signal loss, aligning perfectly with the scientific goal.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preprocessing  
1.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) SDS in PBS for delipidation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS for 3 × 1 hour to remove SDS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody: Rabbit anti-MAP2 (1:1000 dilution) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
2.3 Wash with PBS + 0.1% Triton X-100 for 5 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 hours total)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Goat anti-Rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500 dilution) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
2.5 Wash with PBS + 0.1% Triton X-100 for 5 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 hours total)  

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 2 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)  

4 Delipidation  
4.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane:methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% dichloromethane for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Repeat step 4.2 until tissue becomes transparent. (Temperature: RT, Time: variable, typically 1–2 hours)  

5 Rehydration  
5.1 Incubation with 1:1 (vol/vol) dichloromethane:methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.4 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.5 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.6 Incubation with PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

6 RI Matching  
6.1 Incubation with uDISCO RI matching solution (1:1 vol/vol benzyl alcohol:benzyl benzoate, BABB) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Incubation with 100% BABB for 2 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)  

7 Long-Term Storage and Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Store sample in 100% BABB at 4 ℃ in the dark. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: up to several months)  
7.2 Prior to imaging, equilibrate sample in fresh BABB for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.3 Mount sample in custom chamber with BABB immersion and image using light-sheet or confocal microscopy. (Temperature: RT, Time: variable)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP, MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is ideal for large tissue volumes (up to 5 mm thickness), offers excellent fluorescence preservation (critical for weak endogenous signals like sparse GFP-labeled neurons), and enables long-term storage (up to 1 year) without signal degradation. It is compatible with both endogenous fluorescent proteins (e.g., GFP) and immunolabeled markers (e.g., MAP2). The use of MAP2 as a neuronal dendritic marker complements sparse GFP labeling, enabling detailed dendritic morphology and local circuit analysis. Alexa Fluor 647 is a bright, photostable dye suitable for long-term imaging and compatible with uDISCO.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling (if not already performed)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: Rabbit anti-MAP2 (1:500 dilution) in labeling buffer (1% DMSO, 1% serum, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 (3 × 24 hours at 4 °C)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:1000 dilution) in labeling buffer. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 (3 × 24 hours at 4 °C)

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.6 Incubation with chilled 100% methanol. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1:20 dilution of 30% H₂O₂ in methanol). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Replace with fresh 5% H₂O₂ in methanol. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
3.3 Wash with 100% methanol (3 × 2 hours at RT)

4 Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with 1:1 mixture of dichloromethane (DCM) and methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with DCM containing 0.001% (wt/vol) Sudan Black B (to reduce background autofluorescence). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (100% BABB: 1 part benzyl alcohol, 2 parts benzyl benzoate). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24–48 hours or until fully transparent)

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
5.1 Incubation with 100% BABB containing 0.0005% (wt/vol) Sudan Black B. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Transfer to fresh 100% BABB. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

6 Long-Term Storage and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Store sample in 100% BABB at RT in the dark. (Duration: up to 6 months)  
6.2 Prior to imaging, equilibrate sample in fresh BABB for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT)  
6.3 Mount in custom chamber with BABB immersion and image using light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Chosen Method:** ScaleS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), F-Actin+Phalloidin]  
**Justification:** ScaleS is a sorbitol-based aqueous clearing method that is highly compatible with endogenous fluorescent proteins like GFP and preserves weak fluorescence signals over long periods. It is ideal for 3 mm thick samples and allows for long-term storage without significant signal loss. Phalloidin labeling of F-actin provides a compatible and stable marker for neuronal morphology, including dendritic branches and spines. Unlike organic-solvent-based methods, ScaleS maintains tissue integrity and avoids excessive background increase, making it ideal for long-term archival and re-imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preprocessing  
1.1 Incubation with ScaleS-0 solution (0.1 M PBS, pH 7.4, 0.1% Triton X-100) for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS for 12 hours to enhance permeabilization. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

2 Fluorescent Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with Phalloidin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 568 (1:200 dilution in PBS with 0.3% Triton X-100 and 5% normal goat serum) for neuronal morphology labeling. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100 (3 × 1 hour). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)

3 ScaleS Clearing  
3.1 Incubation with ScaleS-1 solution (30% w/v sucrose, 25% w/v D-sorbitol, 10% (w/v) polyvinyl alcohol, 10% (w/v) polyvinylpyrrolidone, pH 9.5) for 48 hours. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with ScaleS-2 solution (40% w/v sucrose, 35% w/v D-sorbitol, 10% (w/v) polyvinyl alcohol, 10% (w/v) polyvinylpyrrolidone, pH 9.5) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)

4 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
4.1 Incubation with ScaleS-3 solution (45% w/v sucrose, 45% w/v D-sorbitol, 10% (w/v) polyvinyl alcohol, 10% (w/v) polyvinylpyrrolidone, pH 9.5) for RI matching (final RI ~1.46). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)

5 Long-Term Storage Preparation  
5.1 Transfer tissue into fresh ScaleS-3 solution supplemented with 0.02% sodium azide for long-term preservation. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: ongoing)  
5.2 Store samples in the dark at 4 °C for up to 6 months with periodic solution changes every 2 months.

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Equilibrate cleared tissue in fresh ScaleS-3 solution for 12 hours before imaging. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
6.2 Mount tissue in a chamber filled with ScaleS-3 solution for light-sheet or confocal imaging.

1 Immunolabeling

1.4 Incubate with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:1000) and DAPI (1:10,000) in labeling buffer for 72 hours. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100 (6× 1 hour each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubate in 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubate in 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubate in 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubate in 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.4 Incubate in 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

The method is scalable, rapid compared to aqueous clearing methods, and compatible with light-sheet and confocal imaging. NeuN labels mature neurons specifically in the nucleus, while DAPI provides nuclear counterstaining, enhancing cell identification and spatial mapping reliability across cortical layers and perilesional zones.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling (if not already performed)

1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:1000 dilution in labeling buffer) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100 (3 × 24 hours) (Temperature: RT)  
1.6 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 dilution in PBS) for nuclear labeling (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.7 Final wash with PBS (3 × 24 hours) (Temperature: RT)

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS (vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS (vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS (vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS (vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (3 × 1 hour) (Temperature: RT)

3.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 5% H₂O₂ in methanol (1:20 dilution of 30% H₂O₂ in methanol) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% dichloromethane (DCM) (Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 1:1 dichloromethane: methanol (vol/vol) (Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 100% dichloromethane (Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Repeat steps 3.2–3.4 for a total of 3 cycles (Temperature: RT)

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 1:1 dichloromethane:methanol (vol/vol) (Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS (vol/vol) (Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS (vol/vol) (Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS (vol/vol) (Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS (vol/vol) (Time: 1 hour)  
4.6 Incubation with PBS (3 × 1 hour) (Temperature: RT)

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
5.1 Incubation with 30% glycerol in PBS (wt/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with 50% glycerol in PBS (wt/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.3 Incubation with 80% glycerol in PBS (wt/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.4 Incubation with 100% glycerol (RI matching solution) (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)

6 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Mount sample in 100% glycerol in a custom imaging chamber with spacers to accommodate 5 mm thickness  
6.2 Seal chamber with vacuum grease or silicone to prevent evaporation  
6.3 Store at 4 °C in the dark until imaging  
6.4 Image using light-sheet or high-penetration confocal microscopy with appropriate filters for Alexa Fluor 647 and DAPI

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [NeuN+Alexa Fluor 647, MAP2+Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is highly suitable for thick human brain tissue due to its efficient delipidation and excellent preservation of fluorescent signals, especially for antibody-based labeling. It enables deep penetration of antibodies and dyes in large tissue volumes (up to several mm), which is critical for the 3 mm human cortical slices. The combination of NeuN (specific nuclear marker for mature neurons) and MAP2 (dendritic marker for neuronal soma and processes) provides dual-confirmation for mature neuron identification, enhancing reliability of 3D localization and density analysis. Alexa Fluor dyes are highly compatible with iDISCO+ clearing and RI matching, and are spectrally separable for multiplex imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling Enhancement  
1.1 Incubation with 0.2 M glycine in PBS for antigen retrieval. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS for permeabilization. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with blocking solution (10% DMSO, 5% donkey serum in PBS) to reduce nonspecific binding. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with primary antibodies: NeuN (1:500) and MAP2 (1:1000) in labeling buffer (1% DMSO, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 7 days)  
1.5 Wash with PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100 (PBST), 6 × 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 3 days total)  
1.6 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse IgG and Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:1000 each) in labeling buffer. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 7 days)  
1.7 Wash with PBST, 6 × 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 3 days total)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 66% dichloromethane (DCM), 33% methanol (vol/vol) for lipid removal. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Replace with fresh delipidation solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.3 Repeat step 3.2 until tissue becomes translucent (typically 2–3 cycles).  

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Tissue Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (200 mM dibasic sodium phosphate, 15% w/v N-butyldiethanolamine, 50% DMSO, pH 8.5). (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
5.2 Replace with fresh clearing solution. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 48 hours)  

6 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
6.1 Incubation with RI matching solution (DBE, Sigma D151050-100ML) for optical clearing. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Replace with fresh DBE. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Mounting and Imaging  
7.1 Mount tissue in a glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber using DBE.  
7.2 Store at 4 °C in the dark until imaging.  
7.3 Perform 3D imaging using light-sheet or high-penetration confocal microscopy with 488 nm and 647 nm excitation lasers.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling Enhancement  
1.1 Incubation with 0.2 M HCl for 30 minutes to enhance antibody penetration. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.2 Wash with PBS for 1 hour, 3 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
1.3 Incubation with blocking solution (10% DMSO, 5% donkey serum in PBS-Triton 0.3%) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-NeuN (1:500) and anti-MAP2 (1:200) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 7 days)  
1.5 Wash with PBS-Triton 0.3% for 12 hours, 3 times. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours per wash)  
1.6 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse and Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 7 days)  
1.7 Wash with PBS-Triton 0.3% for 12 hours, 3 times. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours per wash)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour, repeated once. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 2)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 66% dichloromethane (DCM), 33% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% DCM for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 100% DCM for 1 hour, repeated 3 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 3)  

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 66% methanol, 33% PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with PBS for 1 hour, repeated 3 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 3)

5.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ RI matching solution (DBE, Sigma D8267) for 3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (endogenous), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 594]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for rapid optical clearing of fixed thick brain sections (up to 1 mm), with excellent preservation of endogenous fluorescent proteins like GFP and compatibility with immunolabeling. It uses a methanol-based dehydration and delipidation protocol that is fast, scalable, and suitable for high-resolution imaging of dendritic spines. The combination of endogenous GFP-labeled sparse neurons and MAP2 immunostaining provides clear delineation of dendritic morphology and spine distribution. Alexa Fluor 594 is highly photostable and compatible with iDISCO+ clearing steps.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling (if not already labeled)  
1.1 Incubate slices in blocking/permeabilization solution: 0.3% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 5% donkey serum in PBS for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubate with primary antibody: Rabbit anti-MAP2 (1:500) in labeling solution (0.3% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 3% donkey serum in PBS) for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.3 Wash 3× 1 hour each with PBS + 0.3% Triton X-100. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  
1.4 Incubate with secondary antibody: Donkey anti-Rabbit Alexa Fluor 594 (1:500) in labeling solution for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.5 Wash 3× 1 hour each with PBS + 0.3% Triton X-100. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubate slices in 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Transfer to 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Transfer to 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Transfer to 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Transfer to 100% methanol twice, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubate slices in freshly prepared dichloromethane (DCM)/methanol (2:1 vol/vol) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Replace with fresh DCM/methanol (1:2 vol/vol) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Transfer to 100% DCM for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubate in DCM/methanol (1:2 vol/vol) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Transfer to 80% methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.3 Transfer to 60% methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.4 Transfer to 40% methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.5 Transfer to 20% methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.6 Wash 2× in PBS + 0.3% Triton X-100 for 30 minutes each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes each)  

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
5.1 Incubate slices in iDISCO+ RI-matching solution (DBE/Tween-20, 99:1 vol/vol) for 1–3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1–3 hours)  
5.2 Replace with fresh RI-matching solution if needed for longer clarity. (Temperature: RT, Time: optional 1–3 hours)  

6 Mounting and Imaging  
6.1 Mount slices in custom chamber or glass-bottom dish with RI-matching solution.  
6.2 Image using confocal or light-sheet microscopy with appropriate filters for GFP and Alexa Fluor 594.  

7 Optional Long-Term Storage  
7.1 Store cleared slices in iDISCO+ storage solution (DBE/Tween-20, 99:1) at 4 °C in the dark. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: up to several weeks)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ 是一种快速、高效的有机溶剂透明化方法，特别适用于500 μm左右的中等厚度脑切片。它在24小时内即可完成透明化，对内源性荧光（如GFP）的保留效果优异，同时兼容抗体标记（如MAP2），可清晰显示树突主干和分支结构。结合Alexa Fluor 568标记的次级抗体，可实现高对比度的树突结构可视化，满足树突棘密度分析和归一化长度测量的需求。

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preprocessing  
1.1 将固定好的500 μm小鼠脑切片置于PBS中漂洗3次，每次1小时（Temperature: RT, Time: 1小时 × 3）  
1.2 在4% PFA（PBS配制）中后固定1小时（Temperature: RT, Time: 1小时）  
1.3 PBS漂洗3次，每次30分钟（Temperature: RT, Time: 30分钟 × 3）

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 在封闭液（0.3% Triton X-100, 5% Normal Goat Serum in PBS）中封闭1小时（Temperature: RT, Time: 1小时）  
2.2 加入兔抗MAP2一抗（1:500稀释于封闭液中）于4℃孵育12小时（Temperature: 4℃, Time: 12小时）  
2.3 PBS + 0.1% Triton X-100漂洗3次，每次1小时（Temperature: RT, Time: 1小时 × 3）  
2.4 加入Alexa Fluor 568标记的山羊抗兔二抗（1:500稀释）于RT避光孵育6小时（Temperature: RT, Time: 6小时）  
2.5 PBS漂洗3次，每次1小时（Temperature: RT, Time: 1小时 × 3）

3 Dehydration  
3.1 梯度甲醇（30%, 50%, 70%, 80%, 100%）脱水，每步30分钟（Temperature: RT, Time: 30分钟/步）  
3.2 100%甲醇再脱水一次，1小时（Temperature: RT, Time: 1小时）

4 Delipidation  
4.1 转入Dichloromethane (DCM)中脱脂30分钟（Temperature: RT, Time: 30分钟）  
4.2 更换新鲜DCM，继续脱脂30分钟（Temperature: RT, Time: 30分钟）

5 Rehydration  
5.1 梯度甲醇（80%, 70%, 50%, 30%）复水，每步30分钟（Temperature: RT, Time: 30分钟/步）  
5.2 PBS漂洗3次，每次30分钟（Temperature: RT, Time: 30分钟 × 3）

6 Tissue Optical Clearing  
6.1 转入iDISCO+透明液（20% DMSO, 20% N-Benzyl Alcohol, 60% Methanol）中透明处理，避光震荡孵育6小时（Temperature: RT, Time: 6小时）

7 Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 透明完成后，PBS漂洗3次，每次30分钟（Temperature: RT, Time: 30分钟 × 3）  
7.2 转入DBE（Dibenzyl Ether）中进行折射率匹配，避光静置孵育3小时（Temperature: RT, Time: 3小时）

8 Imaging and Storage  
8.1 将样本置于载玻片上，用DBE封片，4℃避光保存待成像  
8.2 使用共聚焦或光片显微镜进行高分辨率成像，用于树突棘密度分析与树突骨架结构重建

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (endogenous, labeling pyramidal neurons), Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 568 (labeling F-actin in dendritic spines)]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for rapid optical clearing of fixed, thick brain sections (up to 1 mm), with excellent preservation of endogenous fluorescence (e.g., GFP) and compatibility with immunolabeling. It is methanol-based and fast, enabling full clearing and refractive index (RI) matching within 24 hours. Phalloidin labels F-actin, a core structural component of dendritic spines, and when conjugated to Alexa Fluor 568, provides high-contrast, specific labeling ideal for spine detection. This dual labeling strategy enables clear visualization of both the neuronal morphology (via GFP) and spine structure (via Phalloidin), facilitating accurate spine density quantification along defined dendritic segments.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling Enhancement and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with methanol at –20 °C for 3 hours to enhance antibody penetration and preserve fluorescence. (Temperature: –20 °C, Time: 3 hours)  
1.2 Wash with 50% methanol in PBS (vol/vol) for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100 (PBST) for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

2 Staining  
2.1 Incubation with Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 568 (1:100 dilution in PBST) for 2 hours to label F-actin in dendritic spines. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Wash with PBST (3 × 30 minutes) to remove unbound dye. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1.5 hours total)  

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 50% methanol in PBS (vol/vol) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 70% methanol in PBS (vol/vol) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 100% methanol overnight (or for 8 hours) to fully dehydrate the tissue. (Temperature: RT, Time: 8 hours)  

4 Bleaching (Optional for Autofluorescence Reduction)  
4.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H2O2 in methanol for 4 hours (if high autofluorescence is expected). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 4 hours)  
4.2 Wash with 100% methanol (2 × 1 hour) to remove residual H2O2. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)  

5 Delipidation and Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour to initiate delipidation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with DCM for an additional 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.3 Incubation with DCM containing 0.001% (vol/vol) Sudan Black B for 1 hour to reduce autofluorescence (optional). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

6 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
6.1 Incubation with dibenzyl ether (DBE) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Incubation with fresh DBE for 2 hours to complete RI matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

7 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Mount the cleared 500 μm brain slice in a glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber using DBE as the mounting medium.  
7.2 Seal the chamber with vacuum grease to prevent evaporation during imaging.  
7.3 Image using a high-resolution confocal or light-sheet microscope equipped with a water- or oil-immersion objective (e.g., 25× or 40×, NA ≥ 1.0) optimized for cleared tissue.

**Chosen Method:** SeeDB2  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP, MAP2]  
**Justification:** SeeDB2 is a fast, aqueous-based optical clearing method that preserves endogenous fluorescence (e.g., GFP) and is compatible with immunolabeled structures. It is ideal for 300–500 μm thick brain slices and achieves high-resolution imaging of fine neuronal structures like dendritic spines within a single day. Using GFP for sparse labeling of neurons and MAP2 for dendritic backbone labeling allows for clear segmentation and spine detection in 3D. SeeDB2 minimizes tissue shrinkage compared to TDE and provides superior refractive index (RI) matching for high-resolution imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Pre-Treatment  
1.1 Incubation with 0.1 M PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in phosphate buffer) for permeabilization. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.2 Blocking with 10% normal goat serum (NGS) in PBST for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with primary antibody: chicken anti-GFP (1:1000) and mouse anti-MAP2 (1:500) in PBST + 3% NGS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
1.4 Wash with PBST (3 × 30 minutes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1.5 hours total)  
1.5 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488 goat anti-chicken (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 568 goat anti-mouse (1:500) in PBST + 3% NGS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
1.6 Wash with PBST (3 × 30 minutes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1.5 hours total)  

2 SeeDB2 Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with Solution A (50% (w/v) fructose, 10% (w/v) glycerol in 0.1 M PBST) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with Solution B (70% (w/v) fructose, 20% (w/v) glycerol in 0.1 M PBST) for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with Solution C (80% (w/v) fructose, 30% (w/v) glycerol in 0.1 M PBST) for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with Solution D (90% (w/v) fructose, 40% (w/v) glycerol in 0.1 M PBST) for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.5 Incubation with Solution E (90% (w/v) fructose, 50% (w/v) glycerol in 0.1 M PBST) for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Mounting and Refractive Index Matching  
3.1 Mount sample in Solution E in a glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging recommended)  
3.2 Optional: Seal chamber with vacuum grease to prevent evaporation during long-term imaging.  

4 Imaging  
4.1 Image using a high-resolution confocal or two-photon microscope with a water-immersion objective (e.g., 25×/1.05 NA).  
4.2 Use 488 nm laser for GFP and 561 nm for MAP2 (Alexa Fluor 568), and collect z-stacks at 0.3–0.5 μm step size for optimal spine resolution.

5.1 Transfer sample to fresh Solution E in a sealed container. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: up to 1 week without significant signal loss)
