**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1)+Alexa Fluor 488, NeuroTrace 500 (or equivalent Nissl stain), DiI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole-mount mouse embryos due to its excellent preservation of fluorescent proteins and immunolabeling, rapid clearing speed, and compatibility with lipophilic tracers like DiI. It enables high-resolution 3D imaging across large volumes such as the entire E12.5 embryo. The dual labeling strategy targets both neuronal architecture (β-III Tubulin) and cell body labeling (NeuroTrace 500), while DiI labels long-range projections, enabling full reconstruction of cranial and spinal nerve pathways.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling (if not already performed)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: mouse anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, 1:1000) in blocking solution for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS + 0.1% Tween-20 (PBST) 5 times, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated goat anti-mouse IgG (1:500) in blocking solution for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBST 5 times, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 hours total)  

2 Nuclear and Cell Body Staining  
2.1 Incubation with NeuroTrace 500 (1:200 in PBST) for 24 hours to label neuronal cell bodies. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Wash with PBST 3 times, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

3 Lipophilic Tracer Labeling (Optional, if retrograde labeling of specific nerves is desired)  
3.1 Apply DiI crystals to cut peripheral nerve ends or stereotactically inject DiI solution (1% in DMSO) into target regions (e.g., cranial nerves or dorsal root ganglia).  
3.2 Incubate for 7–10 days to allow DiI diffusion. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 7–10 days)  
3.3 Wash with PBST 3 times, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

4 Dehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour (×2 changes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)  

5 Delipidation  
5.1 Incubation with freshly prepared dichloromethane:methanol (2:1 vol/vol) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with fresh dichloromethane for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Repeat step 5.2 for full delipidation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

6 Rehydration  
6.1 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 15 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 15 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
6.3 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 15 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
6.4 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 15 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
6.5 Incubation with PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

7 Tissue Clearing  
7.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (DBE:Tween 20, 2:1 vol/vol) for 24–48 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24–48 hours)  
7.2 Replace with fresh iDISCO+ solution and incubate until fully transparent (typically 1–2 more days). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2–3 days total)  

8 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
8.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (e.g., BABB: benzyl alcohol:benzyl benzoate, 1:2 vol/vol) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Replace with fresh BABB and incubate for another 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

9 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
9.1 Mount embryo in a custom chamber or glass-bottom dish with BABB.  
9.2 Seal with silicone grease or nail polish to prevent evaporation.  
9.3 Store at 4 °C in the dark until imaging. (Time: up to 2 weeks)  

10 Light-Sheet or Confocal Imaging  
10.1 Image using a light-sheet microscope with appropriate filters:  
- Alexa Fluor 488 (β-III Tubulin): Excitation 488 nm, Emission 500–550 nm  
- NeuroTrace 500: Excitation 500 nm, Emission 520–560 nm  
- DiI: Excitation 550 nm, Emission 570–620 nm  
10.2 Use cleared embryo in BABB with matched RI (≈1.56) for optimal imaging depth and resolution.

The dual labeling strategy using β-III Tubulin (a pan-neuronal marker) and NeuroTrace (a fluorescent Nissl stain) allows for high-contrast visualization of both neuronal cell bodies and their extending axons, enabling reliable tracing of early projection paths from central to peripheral regions. This combination enhances signal-to-noise and facilitates 3D reconstruction of complex neural architectures.

1 Immunolabeling (if not already performed)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 5% (wt/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)

1.3 Three washes with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBT), 1 hour each. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG at 1:1000 in labeling buffer for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.5 Three washes with PBT, 2 hours each. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 3 × 2 hours)  
1.6 Incubation with NeuroTrace 500/525 Green (1:200 dilution in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% DCM for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 100% DCM for another 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) DCM in methanol for 15 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
4.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.3 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.4 Incubation with 15% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.5 Incubation with PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

5.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (20% (wt/vol) DMSO, 30% (vol/vol) benzyl alcohol, 50% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether) for 24–48 hours or until fully transparent. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24–48 hours)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1)+Alexa Fluor 488, Neurofilament H (NF-H)+Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole-mount immunolabeling and clearing of small embryos (8–10 mm), offering excellent preservation of fluorescence, deep penetration, and compatibility with multiple fluorophores. It enables high-resolution imaging of both early (TUJ1) and mature (NF-H) axonal structures. The methanol-based dehydration and delipidation steps reduce background and improve signal-to-noise ratio, especially when combined with bleaching and extended washing. This method supports high-resolution light-sheet or confocal imaging of continuous neural projections across the entire embryo.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling (Post-Washing)
1.1 Incubate embryo in blocking solution (10% normal goat serum, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubate with primary antibodies: β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, 1:1000) and Neurofilament H (NF-H, 1:500) in 2% normal goat serum, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash 5 times with 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS, 24 hours each. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 5 × 24 hours)  
1.4 Incubate with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit in 2% normal goat serum, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.5 Wash 5 times with 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS, 24 hours each. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 5 × 24 hours)

2 Bleaching
2.1 Incubate in chilled 5% H₂O₂ in methanol (1:5 vol/vol) for bleaching endogenous autofluorescence. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)

3 Dehydration
3.1 Incubate in 20% MeOH in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubate in 40% MeOH in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubate in 60% MeOH in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubate in 80% MeOH in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubate in 100% MeOH twice, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)

4 Delipidation
4.1 Incubate in 66% dichloromethane (DCM)/33% MeOH for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubate in 100% DCM for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Repeat step 4.2 until tissue becomes visibly transparent. (Temperature: RT, Time: up to 3 hours total)

5 Rehydration
5.1 Incubate in 66% MeOH/33% PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubate in 40% MeOH in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubate in 20% MeOH in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.4 Incubate in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

6 Refractive Index (RI) Matching
6.1 Incubate in iDISCO+ RI-matching solution (DBE/Toluene, 1:1 vol/vol) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Replace with fresh RI-matching solution and incubate for another 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

7 Storage and Imaging Preparation
7.1 Transfer embryo to a glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber.  
7.2 Cover with RI-matching solution (DBE/Toluene, 1:1) during imaging to minimize light scattering and maintain transparency.  
7.3 Store in sealed container with RI-matching solution at RT for up to 1 week or at 4 °C for longer storage.

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Bruchpilot (BRP/nc82)+Alexa Fluor 555, Synapsin+Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for small, fixed whole-mount tissues like Drosophila brains due to its rapid clearing, excellent preservation of fluorescent proteins and immunolabels, and compatibility with light-sheet microscopy. It is methanol-based, which effectively removes lipids while maintaining structural integrity. The dual labeling with Bruchpilot (a marker for active zone) and Synapsin (a presynaptic vesicle-associated protein) allows for clear distinction between synaptic active zones and vesicle pools, enabling detailed 3D mapping of synaptic architecture across brain regions.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling (if not already performed)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Bruchpilot (nc82, 1:100) and anti-Synapsin (1:200) in 2% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS (5× 2 hours each). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 10 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 555-conjugated anti-mouse and Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit (1:500 each) in 2% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.5 Wash with 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS (5× 2 hours each). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 10 hours total)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 50% methanol in PBS (vol/vol) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 70% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 100% methanol for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Bleaching  
3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 70% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 50% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

5 Delipidation and Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (20% DMSO, 20% N,N-dimethylformamide in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Replace with fresh iDISCO+ solution and incubate for another 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
6.1 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) in iDISCO+ solution for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with 100% DBE for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Mounting and Imaging  
7.1 Mount sample in 100% DBE in a glass-bottom dish or custom chamber suitable for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.  
7.2 Store at RT in the dark until imaging.  
7.3 Image using light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) or high-resolution confocal microscopy with appropriate filters for Alexa Fluor 488 and Alexa Fluor 555.

**Chosen Method:** FlyClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Bruchpilot (BRP/nc82)+Alexa Fluor 568, Synapsin+Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FlyClear is specifically optimized for Drosophila brain tissue, effectively clearing chitinous structures (e.g., cuticle) while preserving synaptic structures and fluorescent signals. It is compatible with immunolabeling and allows high-resolution 3D imaging. The selected labeling strategy targets Bruchpilot (a core component of the active zone) and Synapsin (a presynaptic vesicle-associated protein), enabling dual-channel visualization of distinct presynaptic domains. Alexa Fluor 488 and 568 provide spectrally separable signals with good photostability, ideal for light-sheet or confocal imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling (if not already performed)  
1.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: Bruchpilot (nc82, 1:50) and Synapsin (1:100) in PBST (0.3% Triton X-100) at 4 °C for 72 hours  
1.2 Wash with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100) for 6 × 1 hour at RT  
1.3 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-mouse and Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit in PBST at 1:500 dilution at 4 °C for 72 hours  
1.4 Wash with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100) for 6 × 1 hour at RT  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 2 hours (Temperature: RT)  

3 Delipidation & Clearing  
3.1 Incubation with 1:2 mixture of benzyl alcohol:benzyl benzoate (BABB) for 2 hours (Temperature: RT)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% BABB for 12 hours (Temperature: RT)  

4 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
4.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.56 RI, e.g., dibenzyl ether) for 6 hours (Temperature: RT)  
4.2 Replace with fresh RI-matching solution and incubate for 12 hours (Temperature: RT)  

5 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Transfer sample to a glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber  
5.2 Immerse in RI-matching solution during imaging to prevent evaporation and maintain optical clarity  
5.3 Perform dual-channel 3D imaging using confocal or light-sheet microscopy (Alexa Fluor 488: excitation ~488 nm, emission ~525 nm; Alexa Fluor 568: excitation ~561 nm, emission ~600 nm)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** FlyClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Bruchpilot (BRP/nc82)+Alexa Fluor 568, Synapsin+Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FlyClear is specifically optimized for Drosophila tissues, offering excellent preservation of fluorescence while enabling rapid and effective optical clearing of small, chitinous tissues like the fly head. It is compatible with commonly used Alexa Fluor dyes and allows high-resolution imaging of synaptic structures. The dual labeling with Bruchpilot (a presynaptic active zone marker) and Synapsin (a presynaptic vesicle-associated protein) enables precise mapping of synaptic structures, synaptic clusters, and their spatial relationships across different brain regions.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling Completion  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Bruchpilot (nc82) and anti-Synapsin diluted 1:100 in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.3 Wash with 0.1% PBST (PBS + 0.1% Triton X-100) 5 times, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-mouse and Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.5 Wash with 0.1% PBST 5 times, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour)

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.6 Replace with fresh 100% methanol and incubate for an additional 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3 Delipidation and Clearing  
3.1 Incubation with 1:2 benzyl alcohol:benzyl benzoate (BABB) solution for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 1:1 BABB solution for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with 2:1 BABB solution overnight. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.4 Incubation with 100% BABB for 6 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
3.5 Replace with fresh 100% BABB and incubate for an additional 6 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)

4 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
4.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.56 RI, e.g., dibenzyl ether) for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.2 Replace with fresh RI-matching solution and incubate overnight. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)

5 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Transfer sample to a glass-bottom imaging dish or chambered coverslip.  
5.2 Mount in RI-matching solution to prevent drying and minimize spherical aberration.  
5.3 Seal the sample with vacuum grease or imaging sealant if long-term imaging is required.  
5.4 Store at 4 °C in the dark until imaging. (Time: up to 1 week)  
5.5 Image using confocal or light-sheet microscopy with appropriate filters for Alexa Fluor 488 and Alexa Fluor 568.

**Chosen Method:** FlyClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Bruchpilot (BRP/nc82), Synapsin]  
**Justification:** FlyClear is specifically optimized for Drosophila tissues, particularly those with chitinous structures like the cuticle, and effectively clears both soft and rigid tissues while preserving fine neural structures. It is compatible with immunolabeling and allows for high-resolution 3D imaging. Bruchpilot (BRP/nc82) labels the active zone of presynaptic sites, while Synapsin labels the presynaptic vesicle clusters, enabling dual-channel distinction of synaptic functional domains. These markers are well-established for synaptic mapping in Drosophila and are compatible with FlyClear’s immunolabeling workflow.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal goat serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: mouse anti-Bruchpilot (nc82, 1:100) and rabbit anti-Synapsin (1:200) in labeling buffer (1% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS (5× 24 hours). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 5× 24 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated goat anti-mouse and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated goat anti-rabbit (1:500 each) in labeling buffer for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.5 Wash with 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS (5× 24 hours). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 5× 24 hours)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with FlyClear Solution I (20% sucrose, 2.5% glycerol, 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with FlyClear Solution II (40% sucrose, 5% glycerol, 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with FlyClear Solution III (60% sucrose, 10% glycerol, 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with FlyClear Final Solution (80% sucrose, 20% glycerol, 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS, RI ~1.45) for 48–72 hours until full clearing is achieved. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48–72 hours)  

3 Mounting and Refractive Index Matching  
3.1 Transfer sample to a refractive index (RI)-matched imaging chamber using FlyClear Final Solution or 80% Histodenz in PBS (RI ~1.47) for light-sheet or confocal imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate)  
3.2 Store samples at 4 °C in FlyClear Final Solution if imaging is delayed. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: up to 2 weeks)

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Osx (Osterix), Osteocalcin]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for hard tissues such as bone, enabling deep optical clearing while preserving endogenous fluorescence and antigenicity. It is ideal for postnatal mouse calvarial samples and allows high-resolution 3D imaging of bone suture regions. Osx (Osterix) labels pre-osteoblasts and early osteoblasts, while Osteocalcin labels mature osteoblasts, enabling distinction between differentiation stages. These markers are well-established for osteogenic lineage tracing and are compatible with BoneClear’s immunolabeling workflow.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Osx (1:200) and anti-Osteocalcin (1:500) in labeling buffer (1% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100 (3 × 1 hour). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488 anti-rabbit (anti-Osx) and Alexa Fluor 647 anti-mouse (anti-Osteocalcin) at 1:500 dilution in labeling buffer for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100 (5 × 2 hours). (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 2 hours)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 2 hours (2 changes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 1:1 DCM:methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 100% DCM for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Tissue Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with BoneClear solution A (urea, glycerol, Triton X-100, pH 8.5) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with BoneClear solution B (higher urea and glycerol concentration, pH 9.0) for 48 hours. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 48 hours)  

6 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
6.1 Incubation with RI matching solution (80% glycerol, 20% PBS) for 6 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with 100% glycerol for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

7 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Mount sample in 100% glycerol in an imaging chamber with spacers to prevent compression.  
7.2 Seal chamber with coverslip using silicone grease.  
7.3 Store at 4 °C in the dark until imaging.  
7.4 Image using light-sheet or confocal microscopy with glycerol-immersion objectives.

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Osx (Osterix), GFP]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for hard tissues such as bone, offering excellent preservation of immunofluorescence signals and compatibility with GFP. It enables deep penetration and clearing of mineralized tissues while maintaining structural integrity and minimizing tissue deformation, which is critical for 3D spatial analysis of osteogenic lineage cells. Osx (Osterix) is a key transcription factor expressed in pre-osteoblasts and early osteoblasts, making it ideal for identifying early osteogenic populations, while GFP can be used to label mature osteoblasts or used as a reporter in transgenic models. This dual labeling allows for precise spatial mapping of osteogenic differentiation stages across the suture mesenchyme, bone front, and calvarial plate.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling (if not already performed)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-Osx (1:200 dilution) in labeling buffer (1% BSA, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100 (3 × 1 hour). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500 dilution) in labeling buffer for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100 (3 × 1 hour). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) methanol:dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% DCM for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Mineralization Removal  
4.1 Incubation with 0.5 M EDTA in PBS (pH 7.4) for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
4.2 Wash with PBS (3 × 1 hour). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  

5 Lipid Removal and Initial Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with BoneClear Solution A (8 M urea, 2% Triton X-100, 0.1 M PBS, pH 7.4) for 48 hours. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
5.2 Replace with fresh BoneClear Solution A and incubate for another 48 hours. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 48 hours)  

6 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
6.1 Incubation with BoneClear Solution B (8 M urea, 50% glycerol, 2% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with BoneClear Solution C (8 M urea, 80% glycerol, 2% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 48 hours. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
6.3 Incubation with BoneClear Solution D (8 M urea, 90% glycerol, 2% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 72 hours)  

7 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Mount sample in a chamber filled with BoneClear Solution D.  
7.2 Image using light-sheet or high-penetration confocal microscopy (excitation/emission: Osx-Alexa Fluor 594 at ~590/617 nm, GFP at ~488/509 nm).  

8 Optional Long-Term Storage  
8.1 Store in BoneClear Solution D at 4 °C in the dark. (Time: up to 6 months)

**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for hard tissues like bone, offering excellent optical clearing while preserving endogenous fluorescence and antigenicity. It is particularly suitable for postnatal mouse calvarial sutures due to its ability to decalcify and clear dense mineralized tissue without compromising structural integrity. The dual labeling with Osx (a marker for pre-osteoblasts and early osteoblasts) and CD31 (an endothelial cell marker) enables precise mapping of osteogenic lineage cells in relation to vascular structures, which is critical for analyzing bone suture microenvironment and local angiogenesis. This combination allows for high-resolution 3D imaging of cellular distribution across the suture midline, ossification front, and bone plate edge.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Decalcification and Softening  
1.1 Incubation with 10% (wt/vol) EDTA in PBS (pH 7.4) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.2 Replace solution with fresh 10% EDTA in PBS. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  

2 Permeabilization  
2.1 Incubation with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
2.2 Wash with PBS (3×, 1 hour each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

3 Blocking  
3.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  

4 Primary Antibody Incubation  
4.1 Incubate with primary antibodies: anti-Osx (1:200), anti-CD31 (1:100) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
4.2 Wash with PBS + 0.1% Triton X-100 (5×, 2 hours each). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 10 hours total)  

5 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
5.1 Incubate with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rat IgG (both at 1:500) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
5.2 Wash with PBS + 0.1% Triton X-100 (5×, 2 hours each). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 10 hours total)  

6 Nuclear Staining  
6.1 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 in PBS) for nuclear labeling. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
6.2 Wash with PBS (3×, 1 hour each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

7 Tissue Clearing  
7.1 Incubation with BoneClear Solution I (8 M urea, 25% (vol/vol) glycerol, 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS, pH 7.0). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
7.2 Replace with BoneClear Solution II (8 M urea, 50% (vol/vol) glycerol, 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS, pH 7.0). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
7.3 Incubation with BoneClear Solution III (8 M urea, 75% (vol/vol) glycerol, 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS, pH 7.0). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

8 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
8.1 Incubation with RI matching solution (8 M urea, 80% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS, pH 7.0). (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  

9 Final Storage and Imaging Preparation  
9.1 Mount sample in RI-matched chamber using 80% glycerol solution.  
9.2 Store at 4 °C in the dark until imaging. (Time: up to 2 weeks)  
9.3 Image using light-sheet or confocal microscopy with appropriate filter sets for Alexa Fluor 488, Alexa Fluor 647, and DAPI.

2.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Osterix (1:200), anti-Osteocalcin (1:500) in labeling buffer (1% serum, 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
2.3 Wash with PBS + 0.1% Triton X-100 for 5 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 hours total)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488 anti-rabbit (Osterix), Alexa Fluor 647 anti-mouse (Osteocalcin), both at 1:500. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
2.5 Wash with PBS + 0.1% Triton X-100 for 5 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 hours total)

2.7 Final wash with PBS for 3 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH (Tyrosine Hydroxylase)+Alexa Fluor 488, CD31+Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for bone tissue optical clearing, enabling deep penetration and preservation of fluorescent signals in mineralized tissues. It allows for simultaneous visualization of neural and vascular structures in intact bones like mouse femurs. The selected labeling strategy targets tyrosine hydroxylase (a marker for sympathetic nerve fibers) and CD31 (a marker for endothelial cells in blood vessels), enabling 3D mapping of their spatial relationships. Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 are bright, photostable fluorophores compatible with BoneClear’s clearing conditions.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling Completion  
1.1 Incubate femurs in blocking solution (10% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubate with primary antibodies: anti-TH (1:500) and anti-CD31 (1:200) in labeling buffer (1% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash 3× with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  
1.4 Incubate with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rat (1:1000 each) in labeling buffer for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.5 Wash 3× with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubate in 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubate in 40% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.3 Incubate in 60% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.4 Incubate in 80% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.5 Incubate in 100% methanol for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubate in 1:2 (vol/vol) methanol:dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubate in 100% DCM for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Clearing  
4.1 Incubate in 1:1 (vol/vol) DCM:BoneClear solution (100% BoneClear solution contains 80% ethyl cinnamate, 20% benzyl alcohol) for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.2 Incubate in 100% BoneClear solution for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
5.1 Transfer femurs to RI-matching solution (80% ethyl cinnamate, 20% benzyl alcohol, RI ≈ 1.52) and incubate for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

6 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Mount femurs in a custom chamber filled with RI-matching solution.  
6.2 Seal chamber with silicone grease and coverslip.  
6.3 Proceed to light-sheet or confocal microscopy for 3D imaging of TH+ sympathetic fibers and CD31+ vascular structures.  

7 Storage (if needed)  
7.1 Store samples in 100% BoneClear solution at 4 °C for up to 2 weeks. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: up to 2 weeks)

Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 are spectrally distinct, photostable, and compatible with BoneClear’s clearing conditions, enabling multiplexed imaging and precise spatial co-localization analysis.

1 Immunolabeling Completion  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-TH (1:500) and anti-CD31 (1:200) in labeling buffer (1% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100 (3 × 1 hour). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rat (1:1000 each) in labeling buffer for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100 (5 × 1 hour). (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 hours total)

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 1:2 v/v methanol:dichloromethane (DCM) for 6 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% DCM for 6 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with 2:1 v/v DCM:clearing solution (BoneClear solution: 100 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.5, 10% glycerol, 20% N-methylglucamine, 20% sorbitol, 30% ethylene glycol) for 6 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)

4 Tissue Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with 100% BoneClear solution for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with fresh 100% BoneClear solution for an additional 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
5.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (80% glycerol, 10% sorbitol, 10% N-methylglucamine in PBS, RI ~1.46) for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with fresh RI-matching solution for an additional 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

6.2 Seal chamber with silicone grease or imaging-compatible adhesive to prevent evaporation.  
6.3 Store at 4 °C in the dark until imaging. (Time: up to 2 weeks)  
6.4 Image using light-sheet fluorescence microscopy or high-penetration confocal microscopy.  
6.5 Perform 3D reconstruction and spatial analysis using Imaris, Fiji, or similar software to quantify nerve-vascular proximity, overlap, and regional enrichment.

TH is a specific marker for sympathetic nerve fibers, and CD31 labels endothelial cells of blood vessels. The combination allows precise spatial mapping of nerve-vascular interactions in the bone marrow microenvironment.

**Protocol Steps:**

1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)

1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% Tween-20 (PBST), 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rat (1:1000 each) in labeling buffer for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBST, 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol, 2 × 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours total)

**Chosen Method:** ScaleS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH (酪氨酸羟化酶)+Alexa Fluor 488, CD31+Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** ScaleS is a sucrose-based tissue clearing method specifically optimized for hard tissues like bone, offering excellent preservation of tissue architecture and fluorescence while minimizing brittleness. It avoids harsh organic solvents like叔丁醇 (tert-butanol), which cause tissue fragility, and instead uses graded sucrose solutions for delipidation and refractive index (RI) matching. This makes it ideal for preserving the structural integrity of whole mouse femurs and the spatial continuity of the bone marrow cavity. The labeling strategy targets TH for sympathetic nerve fibers and CD31 for endothelial cells, enabling visualization of vascular networks and their perivascular regions. Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 are compatible with RI-matched imaging and are preserved well under ScaleS conditions.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling Completion  
1.1 Incubate sample in blocking solution (10% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubate with primary antibodies: anti-TH (1:500) and anti-CD31 (1:200) in antibody dilution buffer (2% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% Tween-20 (PBST) 5 times over 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours total)  
1.4 Incubate with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rat (1:500 each) in antibody dilution buffer for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBST 5 times over 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours total)

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubate in 20% (wt/vol) sucrose in PBS for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubate in 30% (wt/vol) sucrose in PBS for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)

3 Delipidation and Clearing  
3.1 Incubate in 20% (wt/vol) sucrose + 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Incubate in ScaleS-CL solution (40% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol, 30% (vol/vol) glycerol, 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
3.3 Incubate in ScaleS-CL solution with 0.1% SDS for 48 hours to enhance delipidation. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
3.4 Wash in ScaleS-CL without SDS for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)

4 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
4.1 Incubate in ScaleS-RI solution (45% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol, 30% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
4.2 Replace with fresh ScaleS-RI solution and incubate for another 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)

5 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Transfer sample to a glass-bottom imaging dish or chambered coverslip.  
5.2 Fill chamber with fresh ScaleS-RI solution to maintain RI matching during imaging.  
5.3 Seal chamber with parafilm or silicone grease to prevent evaporation during imaging.  
5.4 Store at 4 °C in ScaleS-RI solution for up to 2 weeks before imaging.

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically designed for deep optical clearing of bone-embedded tissues such as the mouse cochlea. It effectively decalcifies and clears dense bony structures while preserving fine cellular morphology and fluorescent signals. Phalloidin labels F-actin, which is highly enriched in stereocilia of hair cells, enabling clear identification of both inner and outer hair cells. DAPI labels nuclei, allowing for segmentation and orientation. These small molecule dyes are stable, do not require antibody penetration, and are compatible with BoneClear’s decalcification and clearing steps.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Cochlear Dissection and Initial Washing  
1.1 Wash fixed cochlea in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Post-wash in PBS with 0.1% Triton X-100 for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 F-Actin Staining  
2.1 Incubate in Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 647 (1:100 dilution in PBS with 0.1% Triton X-100) for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Wash in PBS with 0.1% Triton X-100 (3 × 1 hour). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

3 Nuclear Staining  
3.1 Incubate in DAPI (1 μg/mL in PBS with 0.1% Triton X-100) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Wash in PBS with 0.1% Triton X-100 (3 × 1 hour). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

4 Decalcification and Clearing  
4.1 Incubate in BoneClear Solution A (10% EDTA, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24–48 hours (duration depends on age and calcification level of cochlea). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24–48 hours)  
4.2 Replace with fresh Solution A every 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours per change)  
4.3 Incubate in BoneClear Solution B (50% glycerol, 50% ethylene glycol, 1% Triton X-100) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.4 Transfer to BoneClear Solution C (80% glycerol, 20% ethylene glycol, 1% Triton X-100) for 24–48 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24–48 hours)  

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
5.1 Incubate in final RI matching solution (100% glycerol or DBE-based solution if deeper imaging is required) for at least 24 hours before imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Imaging and Storage  
6.1 Store in RI matching solution at 4 °C in the dark until imaging.

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488, Myosin VIIa (primary antibody) + Alexa Fluor 594 secondary, DAPI]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically designed for clearing dense calcified tissues like bone-embedded organs (e.g., the cochlea), enabling deep 3D imaging while preserving fine structures such as F-actin and stereocilia. It is compatible with immunolabeling and small fluorescent dyes like phalloidin. Phalloidin directly labels F-actin, which is essential for visualizing stereocilia bundles, while Myosin VIIa is a specific marker for hair cells. DAPI is used for nuclear counterstain to support hair cell identification and positional mapping. This combination ensures high-resolution, multichannel imaging of hair cell identity and cytoskeletal structure in the intact cochlea.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling (if not already performed)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody (rabbit anti-Myosin VIIa, 1:500 dilution in blocking solution) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% Tween-20 (PBST), 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody (Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated goat anti-rabbit IgG, 1:1000 in PBST) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBST, 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  

2 F-actin Staining  
2.1 Incubation with Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488 (1:100 dilution in PBST) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Wash with PBST, 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  

3 Nuclear Staining  
3.1 Incubation with DAPI (1 μg/mL in PBST) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Wash with PBST, 3 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

4 Dehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Delipidation and Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with 1:2 benzyl alcohol:benzyl benzoate (BABB) for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with 1:1 BABB for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
5.3 Incubation with 2:1 BABB for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.4 Incubation with 100% BABB for 24–48 hours until fully cleared. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  

6 Mounting and Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with dibenzyl ether (DBE) for refractive index matching for at least 24 hours before imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Imaging  
7.1 Perform 3D imaging using light-sheet or high-penetration confocal microscopy in DBE-immersion. (Temperature: RT, Time: variable)

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI, Myosin VIIa]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically designed for optical clearing of calcified and dense tissues such as bone-embedded organs, making it ideal for the mouse cochlea, which is deeply embedded in the dense auditory bulla. It preserves fine structures and fluorescent signals effectively, especially F-actin labeling, which is critical for analyzing stereocilia integrity. Phalloidin labels F-actin-rich stereocilia with high specificity and brightness, DAPI labels nuclei for cellular identification and spatial orientation, and Myosin VIIa is a specific marker for hair cells, enabling precise quantification and localization. These markers together allow for 3D mapping of hair cell loss and stereocilia disruption along the cochlear spiral.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling Completion  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-Myosin VIIa (1:500 dilution in blocking solution) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100 (3 × 2 hours). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:1000) and Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 647 (1:200) in blocking solution for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100 (3 × 2 hours). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
1.6 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 in PBS) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 2 hours (×2 changes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours total)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 1:2 (vol/vol) benzyl alcohol:benzyl benzoate (BABB) for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% BABB for 12 hours (×2 changes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours total)  

4 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
4.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.56 RI, e.g., dibenzyl ether) for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with fresh RI-matching solution for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

5 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Transfer sample into a glass-bottom imaging dish using fine forceps to avoid damaging the cochlear structure.  
5.2 Add RI-matching solution to fully submerge the sample and cover with a coverslip.  
5.3 Store at 4 °C in the dark until imaging. (Time: up to 2 weeks)  
5.4 Image using light-sheet or high-resolution confocal microscopy with multi-channel detection for Alexa Fluor 594 (Myosin VIIa), Alexa Fluor 647 (Phalloidin), and DAPI.  

6 Optional Long-Term Storage  
6.1 For long-term storage (>2 weeks), replace RI-matching solution with fresh solution every 7 days. (Temperature: 4 °C)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor, Myosin VIIa, DAPI]  
**Justification:** Ce3D is a fast, effective, and fluorescence-preserving clearing method particularly suitable for dense, calcified tissues like the cochlea. It enables deep penetration while maintaining structural and fluorescent integrity, which is critical for high-resolution imaging of F-actin (via phalloidin) and hair cell identity (via Myosin VIIa). Phalloidin labels F-actin in stereocilia with high specificity and brightness, and Myosin VIIa is a well-established marker for both inner and outer hair cells. DAPI is retained for nuclear counterstain and spatial orientation. This labeling strategy is compatible with Ce3D’s mild conditions and avoids the need for immunolabeling, reducing processing time and preserving signal integrity.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling (if applicable)  
1.1 Wash tissue in PBS with 0.3% Triton X-100 (PBST) for 3 × 1 hour at RT.  
1.2 Incubate with Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor (1:100 dilution) and anti-Myosin VIIa (1:200 dilution) in PBST with 5% normal goat serum (NGS) for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.3 Wash in PBST 3 × 2 hours at RT.  
1.4 Incubate with secondary antibody (if needed) and DAPI (1:10,000) in PBST with 5% NGS for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.5 Wash in PBST 3 × 2 hours at RT.  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubate in 20% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubate in 40% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.3 Incubate in 60% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.4 Incubate in 80% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.5 Incubate in 100% methanol for 2 × 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubate in 1:2 methanol/dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubate in 100% DCM for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubate in 100% DCM with 5% H2O2 for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubate in 1:2 DCM/methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubate in 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubate in 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubate in 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubate in 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.6 Incubate in 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.7 Incubate in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Tissue Clearing  
5.1 Incubate in Ce3D solution (80% Histodenz, 1.45 M sucrose, 2.5% PVP in PBS) for 24–48 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24–48 hours)  

6 Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubate in Ce3D-RIMS (88% Histodenz, 1.45 M sucrose, 2.5% PVP in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Mounting and Imaging  
7.1 Transfer sample to a glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber.  
7.2 Add Ce3D-RIMS solution to prevent drying and match RI during imaging.  
7.3 Image using light-sheet or high-penetration confocal microscopy for 3D reconstruction and hair cell quantification.

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [IB4-Alexa Fluor 647, TH (Tyrosine Hydroxylase)+Alexa Fluor 555, DAPI]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically designed for optical clearing of mineralized tissues such as teeth and bones, effectively preserving both enamel and dentin structures while enabling deep imaging. It uses a decalcification-based approach followed by refractive index matching, which is ideal for small, hard tissues like mouse molars. The labeling strategy uses IB4-Alexa Fluor 647 to label all nerve fibers (pan-nerve labeling), TH (Tyrosine Hydroxylase) to specifically label sympathetic nerve fibers, and DAPI for nuclear counterstain. This combination allows for 3D visualization and differentiation of total and sympathetic nerve fibers within the pulp cavity without the need for additional antibody labeling, as IB4 and TH are well-established markers for this purpose.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Decalcification and Delipidation  
1.1 Incubation with 10% (wt/vol) EDTA in PBS (pH 7.4) for decalcification. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.2 Replace solution with fresh 10% (wt/vol) EDTA in PBS. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  

2 Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody: TH (Tyrosine Hydroxylase) rabbit monoclonal (1:500 dilution) + IB4-Alexa Fluor 647 (1:200 dilution) in labeling buffer (3% normal goat serum, 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
2.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100 (3 × 1 hour each). (Temperature: RT)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 555-conjugated goat anti-rabbit IgG (1:1000 dilution) in labeling buffer. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
2.5 Wash with PBS (3 × 1 hour each). (Temperature: RT)  
2.6 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 dilution in PBS) for nuclear staining. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.7 Final wash with PBS (3 × 30 minutes). (Temperature: RT)  

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Delipidation  
4.1 Incubation with 100% dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Replace with fresh 100% DCM and incubate for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
5.1 Incubation with 1:1 mixture of benzyl alcohol and benzyl benzoate (BABB) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% BABB for RI matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

6 Mounting and Imaging  
6.1 Mount sample in a glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber using 100% BABB.  
6.2 Image using a confocal or light-sheet microscope equipped with appropriate filters for DAPI, Alexa Fluor 555, and Alexa Fluor 647.

**Chosen Method:** ClearT2  
**Chosen Labeling:** [DiD]  
**Justification:** ClearT2 is a mild, aqueous-based optical clearing method that preserves fine tissue architecture and is particularly suitable for small, calcified tissues like teeth. It maintains the spatial relationships of enamel, dentin, and pulp cavity while enabling deep imaging. DiD, a lipophilic carbocyanine dye, is ideal for tracing neural pathways due to its ability to diffuse along lipid membranes and label entire neuronal processes without the need for immunostaining. This direct labeling approach is sufficient for mapping the gross trajectory, branching, and terminal fields of pulp innervation without molecular specificity.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Labeling  
1.1 Incubation with DiD (1 mg/mL in DMSO, diluted 1:1000 in PBS) via root apex immersion for retrograde labeling. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.2 Post-labeling wash in PBS to remove excess dye. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)

2 Fixation and Permeabilization  
2.1 Post-fixation with 4% PFA in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Wash in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)  
2.3 Incubation with 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS for permeabilization. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

3 Clearing (ClearT2 Protocol)  
3.1 Incubation with ClearT2 Solution I (20% glycerol, 2.5% acrylamide, 0.1% VA-044 in PBS) to initiate hydrogel formation. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with ClearT2 Solution II (40% glycerol, 5% acrylamide, 0.2% VA-044 in PBS) for polymerization. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with ClearT2 Solution III (80% glycerol, 10% acrylamide, 0.2% VA-044 in PBS) for full tissue clearing. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 48–72 hours)

4 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
4.1 Gradual transition into RI matching solution (80% glycerol in PBS, RI ~1.45–1.47) to minimize light scattering. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Final incubation in 100% glycerol for optimal optical clearing. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24–48 hours)

5 Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Mount sample in 100% glycerol within a custom chamber to maintain orientation and immersion.  
5.2 Seal chamber to prevent evaporation during long-term imaging.  
5.3 Proceed to light-sheet or high-resolution confocal microscopy for 3D reconstruction of labeled nerve fibers.

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [DAPI, Phalloidin, β-III Tubulin+Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for hard tissues such as teeth and bones, enabling effective decalcification and optical clearing while preserving fine cellular and subcellular structures. It allows for deep penetration of labeling agents and maintains fluorescence of both endogenous and exogenous fluorophores. DAPI labels nuclei for general tissue architecture, Phalloidin highlights F-actin for soft tissue morphology, and β-III Tubulin labels neuronal processes, making it ideal for mapping neural architecture in the tooth pulp. This combination ensures visualization of the 3D spatial relationships between the pulp cavity, soft tissue boundaries, and innervation patterns.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling Completion and Washing  
1.1 Incubate sample in 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS (PBST) for permeabilization. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Wash 3× in PBS for 30 minutes each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min × 3)  
1.3 Incubate with β-III Tubulin primary antibody (1:500 dilution in PBST) at 4 °C. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.4 Wash 3× in PBS for 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 h × 3)  
1.5 Incubate with Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated secondary antibody (1:1000 dilution in PBST) and Phalloidin-488 (1:200 dilution) at 4 °C. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.6 Wash 3× in PBS for 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 h × 3)  
1.7 Incubate with DAPI (1:10,000 dilution in PBS) for nuclear staining. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.8 Wash 3× in PBS for 30 minutes each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min × 3)  

2 Decalcification  
2.1 Incubate sample in 10% EDTA (pH 7.4) at 4 °C. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours, change solution every 24 hrs)  
2.2 Rinse in PBS until EDTA is fully removed. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 min washes)  

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubate in ascending methanol series: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% (each for 1 hour at RT). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)  
3.2 Equilibrate in 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Delipidation  
4.1 Incubate in dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Repeat DCM incubation for another hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Rehydration  
5.1 Incubate in descending methanol series: 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% (each for 1 hour at RT). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)  
5.2 Transfer to PBS and equilibrate for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

6 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
6.1 Incubate in BoneClear RI-matching solution (e.g., 50% glycerol in PBS) for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
6.2 Transfer to 80% glycerol in PBS and incubate overnight. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
6.3 Incubate in 100% glycerol for final RI matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Mount sample in a glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber using 100% glycerol.  
7.2 Seal sample chamber to prevent evaporation during imaging.  
7.3 Proceed to imaging using light-sheet or confocal microscopy optimized for Alexa Fluor 647, FITC (Phalloidin), and DAPI.

**Chosen Method:** ScaleS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [DAPI, Phalloidin, IB4 (凝集素)]  
**Justification:** ScaleS is a urea-based, slow but highly compatible tissue clearing method that preserves tissue morphology and endogenous fluorescence. It is ideal for small, mineralized tissues like mouse molars, where structural preservation of enamel and dentin is critical. DAPI labels nuclei for general tissue architecture, Phalloidin highlights F-actin in soft tissue structures (e.g., pulp stroma), and IB4 labels endothelial cells and some nerve-associated structures, providing contrast for 3D mapping of pulp innervation without requiring immunolabeling. These dyes are small, fixable, and compatible with ScaleS chemistry.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Pre-labeling (if not already done)  
1.1 Incubation with DAPI (1:1000 in PBS) for nuclear staining. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with Phalloidin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 or 594 (1:200 in PBS with 0.3% Triton X-100) for F-actin labeling. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with IB4 conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:200 in PBS with 0.3% Triton X-100) for labeling of nerve-associated vasculature and glial structures. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
1.4 Wash with PBS with 0.3% Triton X-100 (3 × 1 hour) to remove unbound dye. (Temperature: RT)

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) ethanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) ethanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) ethanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) ethanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% ethanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.6 Repeat 100% ethanol incubation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

3 Clearing (ScaleS protocol)  
3.1 Incubation with ScaleS1 solution (4 M urea, 10% glycerol, 10% DMSO in PBS) for delipidation and clearing. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
3.2 Replace with fresh ScaleS1 solution. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)

4 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
4.1 Incubation with ScaleS2 solution (4 M urea, 20% glycerol, 20% DMSO in PBS, RI ~1.44) for RI matching. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Replace with fresh ScaleS2 solution. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

5 Final Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Optional: Incubation with ScaleS3 solution (4 M urea, 30% glycerol, 30% DMSO in PBS, RI ~1.46) for long-term storage and optimal RI matching. (Temperature: RT or 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Mount sample in a chamber filled with ScaleS3 or similar RI-matched solution for light-sheet or confocal imaging.  
5.3 Image using a high-resolution confocal or light-sheet microscope with appropriate excitation and emission filters for DAPI, Alexa Fluor 488/594 (Phalloidin), and Alexa Fluor 647 (IB4).

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [DiD, DAPI]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for hard tissue-soft tissue composite samples like bone and cartilage-containing vertebral segments. It achieves high transparency while preserving fluorescence and maintaining structural integrity, which is critical for resolving fine peripheral nerve structures across mineralized and soft tissue interfaces. DiD is a lipophilic tracer ideal for long-range axonal tracing without the need for immunolabeling, and DAPI provides nuclear counterstain to delineate tissue architecture. These dyes are compatible with BoneClear’s clearing chemistry and RI matching, enabling high-resolution 3D imaging of nerve trajectories and their spatial relationships with bone foramina, cartilage boundaries, and paravertebral muscles.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Labeling  
1.1 Incubation with DiD labeling solution (1:200 dilution of DiD in PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100) for retrograde labeling of peripheral nerves. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100 (3 × 1 hour) to remove excess dye. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  
1.3 Incubation with DAPI (1 μg/mL in PBS) for nuclear staining. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.4 Wash with PBS (3 × 30 minutes) to remove unbound DAPI. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1.5 hours total)

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for partial dehydration. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% dichloromethane (DCM) for delipidation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
3.2 Replace with fresh 100% DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.5 Incubation with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

5 BoneDecalcification (optional but recommended for better optical penetration in vertebral bone)  
5.1 Incubation with 10% EDTA in PBS (pH 7.4) for decalcification. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
5.2 Replace with fresh 10% EDTA solution. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
5.3 Wash with PBS (3 × 1 hour). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)

6 Clearing  
6.1 Incubation with BoneClear Solution A (urea 8 M, glycerol 25%, Triton X-100 1%, in PBS) for initial clearing. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Replace with fresh BoneClear Solution A. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.3 Incubation with BoneClear Solution B (urea 8 M, glycerol 50%, Triton X-100 1%, in PBS) for deep clearing. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
6.4 Replace with fresh BoneClear Solution B. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)

7 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
7.1 Incubation with RI matching solution (glycerol 80% in PBS, RI ~1.45–1.47) for refractive index homogenization. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
7.2 Replace with fresh RI matching solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

8 Final Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Mount sample in RI-matched imaging chamber using glycerol-based mounting medium.  
8.2 Store at 4 °C in the dark until imaging. (Time: up to 2 weeks)  
8.3 Image using light-sheet or confocal microscopy with appropriate filters: DiD (Ex/Em ~644/665 nm), DAPI (Ex/Em ~358/461 nm).

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1)+Alexa Fluor 488, MBP+Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for bone and mineralized tissues, enabling deep clearing of complex tissues like mouse vertebrae with surrounding muscle and nerves. It preserves fluorescence well and allows for simultaneous visualization of both mineralized and soft tissue components. The labeling strategy uses β-III Tubulin to label all nerve fibers and MBP to specifically label myelinated fibers, enabling distinction between general and heavily myelinated nerve populations. DAPI is used for nuclear counterstain to aid in anatomical orientation and segmentation. This combination is ideal for analyzing 3D nerve architecture across heterogeneous tissue boundaries.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preprocessing  
1.1 Wash sample in PBS for 1 hour at RT to remove residual fixatives. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubate in 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS for 2 hours to enhance permeabilization. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Block sample in blocking solution (5% normal donkey serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Incubate with primary antibodies: β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, 1:1000) and MBP (1:500) in blocking solution for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
2.3 Wash in 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS (5× 2 hours each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 hours total)  
2.4 Incubate with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit in blocking solution for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
2.5 Wash in 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS (5× 2 hours each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 hours total)  
2.6 Incubate with DAPI (1:1000 in PBS) for 12 hours for nuclear labeling. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
2.7 Final wash in PBS overnight. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  

3 BoneDecalcification and Clearing  
3.1 Incubate in BoneClear Solution A (0.5 M EDTA, pH 8.0 in PBS) for 48 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
3.2 Replace with fresh Solution A for another 48 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
3.3 Incubate in BoneClear Solution B (20% sucrose, 10% glycerol, 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.4 Incubate in BoneClear Solution C (50% glycerol, 2% DMSO, 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.5 Incubate in BoneClear Solution D (80% glycerol, 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 48 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  

4 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
4.1 Incubate in RI-matching solution (80% glycerol, 0.1% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Replace with fresh RI-matching solution and incubate for another 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Imaging Preparation and Storage  
5.1 Mount sample in custom chamber filled with RI-matching solution for light-sheet or confocal imaging.  
5.2 Store remaining sample in 80% glycerol solution at 4 °C if long-term preservation is needed.

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 647, DiD, DAPI]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for hard tissue-soft tissue composite samples like bone-muscle-nerve complexes. It enables efficient decalcification and lipid removal while preserving fine neural structures and fluorescent signals. Phalloidin targets F-actin to label muscle fibers with high resolution, DiD labels lipophilic membranes of nerve fibers, and DAPI labels nuclei for structural orientation and cellularity reference. These small molecule dyes do not require antibody penetration and are compatible with BoneClear’s processing conditions.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Wholemount Fluorescent Labeling  
1.1 Incubation with Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 647 (1:100 dilution in PBS with 0.3% Triton X-100) for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with DiD (1 μM in PBS with 0.3% Triton X-100) for retrograde labeling of nerve membranes for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 dilution in PBS) for nuclear counterstaining for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.4 Wash with PBS with 0.3% Triton X-100 (3 × 1 hour) to remove excess dye. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  

2 Decalcification  
2.1 Incubation with 10% (wt/vol) EDTA in PBS (pH 7.4) for decalcification. Change solution every 24 hours for 5 days. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 5 days total)  

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Delipidation  
4.1 Incubation with 1:1 (vol/vol) methanol:dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% DCM for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 100% DCM containing 5% (vol/vol) hydrogen peroxide for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
5.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) dibutyl phthalate (DBP) in DCM for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% DBP for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with RI-matching solution (e.g., 100% dibenzyl ether, DBE) for final clearing. Change solution twice. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per change)  

6 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Mount sample in a custom chamber with DBE to match refractive index for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.  
6.2 Store in sealed chamber with DBE at 4 °C if imaging is not immediate. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: up to 1 week)

1.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization solution: 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 5% (wt/vol) BSA, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)

1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488 anti-mouse (1:500), Alexa Fluor 647 anti-rabbit (1:500), and DAPI (1:1000). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.5 Wash with 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (6 × 1 hour). (Temperature: RT)

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
