**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [DAPI, Phalloidin, Ki67+Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is a fast, methanol-based optical clearing method that is highly suitable for small, fixed 3D tissues like brain organoids (1–3 mm). It preserves fluorescence well, especially for Alexa Fluor dyes, and enables deep imaging with light-sheet or confocal microscopy. The labeling strategy includes DAPI for nuclear density and overall structure, Phalloidin for F-actin to assess cell morphology and structural integrity, and Ki67 for cell proliferation. These markers together allow for comprehensive assessment of organoid size, cell density, proliferative zones, and structural damage, which are critical for high-throughput drug toxicity screening.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling Completion (if not already performed)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization solution (0.3% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 5% donkey serum in PBS) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-Ki67 (1:200 dilution) in labeling buffer (0.3% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 1% BSA in PBS) for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.3 Wash with wash buffer (0.3% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO in PBS) 3× 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3×1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) and Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488 (1:200) in labeling buffer for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.5 Wash with wash buffer 3× 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3×1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 in PBS) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.7 Wash with PBS 2× 30 minutes each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2×30 minutes)

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.6 Incubation with chilled 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 1 hour)

3 Bleaching (optional, for autofluorescence reduction)  
3.1 Incubation with 5% H₂O₂ in methanol (freshly prepared) at 4 °C for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Wash with 100% methanol 2× 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2×1 hour)

4 Delipidation/Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with 1:1 mixture of methanol/dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% DCM for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 100% DCM containing 0.001% methyl salicylate (optional, for fluorescence preservation) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
5.1 Incubation with dibenzyl ether (DBE) for RI matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
5.2 Transfer to fresh DBE for final clearing and imaging compatibility. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Mount organoids in DBE in a glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber.  
6.2 Image using light-sheet or confocal microscopy with appropriate filter sets for DAPI, Alexa Fluor 488, and Alexa Fluor 647.

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Ki67-Alexa Fluor 647, PCNA-Alexa Fluor 594, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for small, fixed 3D tissues like human brain organoids (1–3 mm), offering rapid and efficient clearing while preserving fluorescence from both endogenous and antibody-labeled fluorophores. It is compatible with multiplex immunolabeling and provides excellent tissue transparency for high-resolution 3D imaging using confocal or light-sheet microscopy. The labeling strategy uses Ki67 for cell cycle status and PCNA for DNA replication activity—two nuclear markers critical for validating drug effects on proliferation. DAPI is used as a nuclear counterstain to segment nuclei and normalize cell counts across organoid regions.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling (if not pre-labeled)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Ki67 (1:200) and anti-PCNA (1:300) in labeling buffer (1% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.05% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 in PBS (6 × 1 hour washes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse and Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-rabbit in labeling buffer for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.5 Wash with 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 in PBS (6 × 1 hour washes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 dilution in PBS) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
1.7 Wash with PBS (3 × 1 hour). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.6 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 1:1 DCM:MACS-RI matching solution (or BABB) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with fresh DCM for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
4.1 Incubation with 1:1 DCM:MACS-RI (or BABB) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% MACS-RI (or BABB) for RI matching (e.g., dibenzyl ether-based solution) for 12–24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12–24 hours)

5 Mounting and Imaging  
5.1 Mount organoids in custom chamber or glass capillary in fresh MACS-RI solution.  
5.2 Image using light-sheet or high-numerical aperture confocal microscope with multi-channel fluorescence detection.  
5.3 Acquire z-stacks with appropriate voxel resolution (e.g., 0.5 μm xy, 1 μm z-step) for 3D reconstruction and quantitative analysis of Ki67+, PCNA+, and DAPI+ cells.

6 Storage (if needed)  
6.1 Store cleared and labeled organoids in 100% MACS-RI at 4 °C in the dark. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: up to several weeks)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [DAPI, Phalloidin, Ki67]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is a fast, methanol-based clearing method that is highly suitable for small, fixed 3D tissues like human brain organoids (1–3 mm). It preserves fluorescence well, especially for dyes like DAPI, Phalloidin, and Alexa Fluor-conjugated antibodies, which are commonly used in this protocol. The method enables rapid optical clearing and is compatible with high-throughput imaging (e.g., light-sheet microscopy). DAPI provides nuclear staining for cell density quantification, Phalloidin labels F-actin to define organoid boundaries and cellular architecture, and Ki67 serves as a proliferation marker to assess drug-induced growth inhibition. These markers are compatible with iDISCO+ immunolabeling and clearing workflow.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preparation and Permeabilization  
1.1 Wash fixed organoids (4% PFA, overnight at 4 °C) in PBS (3 × 10 min, RT)  
1.2 Incubation with 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS for permeabilization (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.3 Wash in PBS (3 × 10 min, RT)  

2 Blocking and Immunolabeling  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% donkey serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-Ki67 (1:200 dilution in blocking solution) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
2.3 Wash in PBS with 0.3% Triton X-100 (5 × 30 min, RT)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse/rabbit IgG (1:500 dilution) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
2.5 Wash in PBS (5 × 30 min, RT)  

3 Nuclear and F-actin Staining  
3.1 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 dilution in PBS) for nuclear labeling (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.2 Wash in PBS (3 × 10 min, RT)  
3.3 Incubation with Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488 (1:200 dilution in PBS) for F-actin labeling (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.4 Wash in PBS (3 × 10 min, RT)  

4 Dehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS (v/v) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS (v/v) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS (v/v) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS (v/v) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (3 × 1 hour)  

5 Delipidation and Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 5% H2O2 in methanol (1:20 dilution of 30% H2O2 in methanol) to bleach autofluorescence (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
5.2 Wash with 100% methanol (3 × 1 hour, RT)  
5.3 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM) for delipidation (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.4 Incubation with 1:1 DCM:BABB (benzyl alcohol/benzyl benzoate, 1:1 vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.5 Incubation with 100% BABB for final clearing (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

6 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
6.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (BABB with 0.5% Tween 20) to optimize imaging (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

7 Storage and Imaging  
7.1 Store cleared organoids in BABB at 4 °C protected from light until imaging  
7.2 Image using light-sheet or confocal microscopy with appropriate filters for DAPI (Ex: 405 nm), Phalloidin-AF488 (Ex: 488 nm), and Ki67-AF647 (Ex: 647 nm)

1.5 Wash with PBST, 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)

**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5+Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for transparentizing fixed skin biopsies due to its excellent preservation of fluorescent signals, rapid clearing, and compatibility with immunolabeled samples. It uses a methanol-based delipidation approach that is effective for small, dense tissues like skin. PGP9.5 (Protein Gene Product 9.5) is a well-established pan-axonal marker for intraepidermal nerve fibers (IENF), and conjugation with Alexa Fluor 488 ensures strong, specific fluorescence for 3D visualization. DAPI is used as a nuclear counterstain to define tissue architecture and epidermal layers without interfering with the nerve fiber signal.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling (if not already performed)  
1.1 Incubate samples in blocking solution (10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubate with primary antibody: mouse anti-PGP9.5 (1:500 dilution) in labeling buffer (1% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash 3× with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBST), 2 hours each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
1.4 Incubate with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated goat anti-mouse IgG (1:1000 dilution) in labeling buffer for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.5 Wash 3× with PBST, 2 hours each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
1.6 Incubate with DAPI (1:10,000 dilution in PBS) for 2 hours to label nuclei. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.7 Wash 2× with PBS, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubate in 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubate in 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubate in 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubate in 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubate in 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.6 Incubate in fresh 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubate in freshly prepared dichloromethane (DCM)/methanol (2:1 vol/vol) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubate in fresh DCM/methanol (1:2 vol/vol) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubate in fresh 100% DCM for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Repeat step 3.3 with fresh DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubate in DCM/methanol (1:2 vol/vol) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubate in DCM/methanol (2:1 vol/vol) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubate in 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubate in 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubate in 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.6 Incubate in 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.7 Incubate in 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.8 Incubate in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
5.1 Incubate in iDISCO+ RI-matching solution (DBE/Toluene, 1:2 vol/vol) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubate in fresh iDISCO+ RI-matching solution (DBE/Toluene, 1:1 vol/vol) for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.3 Incubate in fresh iDISCO+ final clearing solution (DBE/Toluene, 2:1 vol/vol) for 3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
5.4 Incubate in 100% dibenzyl ether (DBE) for 6–12 hours or until fully cleared. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6–12 hours)

6 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Mount sample in a glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber using 100% DBE.  
6.2 Seal the chamber to prevent evaporation during imaging.  
6.3 Image using a confocal or light-sheet microscope optimized for cleared tissue (excitation/emission: Alexa Fluor 488 ~488/520 nm, DAPI ~358/461 nm).  

7 Optional Long-Term Storage  
7.1 Store cleared samples in 100% DBE at 4 °C in the dark. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: indefinite)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 (HuC/D) + Alexa Fluor 488, IB4 + Alexa Fluor 594, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for small clinical biopsies due to its rapid clearing, excellent preservation of fluorescent signals, and compatibility with immunolabeling. It is particularly suitable for 3D imaging of complex structures like nerve fibers and microvasculature. PGP9.5 (HuC/D) is a well-established marker for intraepidermal nerve fibers (IENF), and its labeling with Alexa Fluor 488 ensures high-resolution visualization. IB4, a lectin-based vascular marker, effectively labels endothelial cells in the dermal capillary network and is compatible with iDISCO+. DAPI is used for nuclear counterstaining to delineate tissue layers. This combination enables multiplexed 3D imaging of IENF architecture and vascular topology, supporting spatial correlation analysis.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: mouse anti-PGP9.5 (1:500) and IB4 (1:200) in labeling buffer (1% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBST), 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG and Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated streptavidin (for IB4) in labeling buffer for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBST, 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
1.6 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 in PBS) for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.7 Final wash with PBST, 3 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 5% (vol/vol) NaOH in methanol (1 volume of 30% NaOH in 5 volumes of methanol) at 4 °C for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with chilled methanol for 2 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 2 hours)  

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Tissue Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (200 mM dibasic sodium phosphate, 15% (wt/vol) N-butyldiethanolamine, 20% (vol/vol) dimethyl sulfoxide, 40% (vol/vol) methanol) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Replace with fresh iDISCO+ solution and incubate for another 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
6.1 Incubation with RI matching solution (benzyl alcohol:benzyl benzoate, 1:2 vol/vol) for 3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
6.2 Transfer to fresh RI matching solution and incubate until tissue becomes fully transparent (typically 6–12 hours). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6–12 hours)  

7 Mounting and Imaging  
7.1 Mount sample in RI-matched solution in a glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber.  
7.2 Image using a light-sheet or high-resolution confocal microscope with appropriate filter sets for Alexa Fluor 488, Alexa Fluor 594, and DAPI.

1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:1000), Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated streptavidin (1:1000) in labeling buffer for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBST, 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 5% (vol/vol) H2O2 in methanol (1:20 dilution of 30% H2O2 in methanol) at 4 °C for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Wash with 100% methanol, 3 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** ScaleS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5+Alexa Fluor 488, CD31+Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI, Melanin bleaching with 1% (w/v) Potassium Permanganate / 10% (v/v) Sulfuric Acid]  
**Justification:** ScaleS is a sorbitol-based aqueous clearing method that preserves fluorescence well, especially for Alexa Fluor dyes, and is particularly suitable for skin tissues with high melanin content. It allows for effective melanin bleaching without significant tissue deformation, which is critical for accurate 3D IENF tracing and quantification. The combination of PGP9.5 for nerve fibers and CD31 for vascular labeling provides dual-contrast for spatial alignment and reference. DAPI is used for nuclear counterstain to aid in segmentation and orientation. Melanin bleaching is integrated to reduce background absorption and autofluorescence from residual melanin in the basal epidermis.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling Completion and Washing  
1.1 Wash tissue in PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100 (PBST) for 3 × 1 hour at RT to remove residual fixative.  
(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  
1.2 Incubate with blocking solution (5% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 2 hours.  
(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.3 Incubate with primary antibodies: mouse anti-PGP9.5 (1:1000) and rat anti-CD31 (1:200) in blocking solution.  
(Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.4 Wash in PBST 5 × 1 hour at RT.  
(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 hours total)  
1.5 Incubate with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rat IgG (1:500 each) in blocking solution.  
(Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.6 Wash in PBST 5 × 1 hour at RT.  
(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 hours total)  
1.7 Incubate with DAPI (1:10,000 dilution in PBS) for 1 hour.  
(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.8 Wash in PBS 3 × 30 minutes.  
(Temperature: RT, Time: 1.5 hours total)

2 Melanin Bleaching  
2.1 Incubate tissue in freshly prepared bleaching solution: 1% (w/v) Potassium Permanganate / 10% (v/v) Sulfuric Acid for 2–3 hours or until tissue turns pale.  
(Temperature: RT, Time: 2–3 hours)  
2.2 Rinse in water for 10 minutes.  
(Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)  
2.3 Incubate in 5% (w/v) Sodium Metabisulfite in water for 10 minutes to stop bleaching reaction.  
(Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)  
2.4 Wash in PBS 3 × 10 minutes.  
(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes total)

3 ScaleS Clearing  
3.1 Incubate in ScaleS-1 solution (40% w/v urea, 10% w/v polyvinyl alcohol, 10% w/v glycerol in PBS) for 24 hours.  
(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Replace with fresh ScaleS-1 and incubate for another 24 hours.  
(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.3 Incubate in ScaleS-2 solution (40% w/v urea, 20% w/v glycerol, 2.5% w/v CHAPS in PBS) for 24 hours.  
(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.4 Replace with fresh ScaleS-2 and incubate for another 24 hours.  
(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

4 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
4.1 Incubate in ScaleS-3 solution (40% w/v urea, 30% w/v glycerol in PBS) for 12 hours.  
(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.2 Replace with fresh ScaleS-3 and incubate for another 12 hours.  
(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.3 Optional: Transfer to a final RI matching solution (e.g., 80% glycerol in PBS) for long-term storage and imaging.  
(Temperature: RT, Time: 12–24 hours)

5 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Mount tissue in a chamber filled with ScaleS-3 or 80% glycerol solution.  
(Temperature: RT)  
5.2 Image using a confocal or light-sheet microscope optimized for Alexa Fluor 488 (excitation: 488 nm, emission: 520 nm), Alexa Fluor 647 (excitation: 647 nm, emission: 665 nm), and DAPI (excitation: 405 nm, emission: 450 nm).

请根据该科学问题自行选择合适的荧光/标记策略，并基于所选标记样本选择匹配的组织透明方法。若已有 EGFP 和 mCherry/RFP 内源荧光报告信号可以直接完成神经元群体定位和结构追踪，则不应额外选择抗体靶点。请仅输出 protocol，第 1 行写明所选荧光/标记策略和组织透明方法，随后仅列出透明处理、RI 匹配和保存/成像前处理步骤的关键试剂、条件和时间。

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP, mCherry]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is a methanol-based clearing method that provides excellent tissue clearing and preservation of endogenous fluorescent proteins such as EGFP and mCherry. It is particularly suitable for small, fixed whole organisms like *C. elegans*, offering rapid processing and compatibility with light-sheet and confocal microscopy. Since the sample already expresses EGFP and mCherry in defined neuronal populations, no additional labeling is required, minimizing processing steps and preserving signal integrity.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Methanol Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS with 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS with 0.3% Triton X-100 for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS with 0.3% Triton X-100 for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS with 0.3% Triton X-100 for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Bleaching (Optional for Autofluorescence Reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) hydrogen peroxide in methanol. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Wash with 100% methanol three times, 30 minutes each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per wash)  

3 Delipidation and Clearing  
3.1 Incubation with freshly prepared dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with DCM containing 3% (vol/vol) hydrogen peroxide for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.3 Wash with 100% methanol twice, 30 minutes each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per wash)  

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS with 0.3% Triton X-100 for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.2 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS with 0.3% Triton X-100 for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.3 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS with 0.3% Triton X-100 for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS with 0.3% Triton X-100 for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.5 Incubation with PBS with 0.3% Triton X-100 for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
5.1 Incubation with BABB (1:2 solution of benzyl alcohol and benzyl benzoate) for RI matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
5.2 Transfer to fresh BABB and incubate until fully cleared (typically 12–24 hours). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12–24 hours)  

6 Mounting and Imaging  
6.1 Mount sample in BABB in a glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber.  
6.2 Image using confocal or light-sheet microscopy, ensuring appropriate filter sets for EGFP (Ex: ~488 nm, Em: ~509 nm) and mCherry (Ex: ~587 nm, Em: ~610 nm) are used.  

7 Storage (if not imaging immediately)  
7.1 Store sample in BABB at 4 °C for up to several weeks with minimal signal loss. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: up to 4 weeks)

**Chosen Method:** SeeDB2  
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP, mCherry]  
**Justification:** SeeDB2 is a fructose-based optical clearing method that provides excellent preservation of endogenous fluorescent proteins (including EGFP and mCherry), making it ideal for dual-color fluorescent imaging in *C. elegans*. It is fast, simple, and compatible with small, fixed whole organisms like *C. elegans* adults (~1 mm length). It avoids harsh chemical treatments that may quench fluorescence or damage fine neural structures. The method achieves high transparency and optimal refractive index (RI) matching for high-resolution imaging of the nervous system, including the nerve ring, head ganglia, and ventral nerve cord.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Washing  
1.1 Wash fixed *C. elegans* samples 3× in PBS for 10 minutes each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes total)  

2 Permeabilization  
2.1 Incubate in PBS + 0.5% Triton X-100 for 30 minutes to enhance penetration. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

3 Nuclear Counterstain (Optional)  
3.1 Incubate in DAPI (1:1000 dilution in PBS) for nuclear labeling. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Wash 3× in PBS for 10 minutes each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes total)  

4 SeeDB2 Clearing  
4.1 Incubate in SeeDB2 Solution 1 (25% D-sorbitol in PBS) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubate in SeeDB2 Solution 2 (25% D-sorbitol + 25% fructose in PBS) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubate in SeeDB2 Solution 3 (50% fructose in PBS) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubate in SeeDB2 Solution 4 (75% fructose in PBS) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubate in SeeDB2 Solution 5 (100% fructose) overnight or until fully cleared. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12–16 hours)  

5 Mounting and RI Matching  
5.1 Transfer worms to a glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber.  
5.2 Mount in fresh 100% fructose solution for imaging. (Temperature: RT)  

6 Imaging  
6.1 Perform 3D imaging using a confocal or light-sheet microscope equipped with appropriate filters for EGFP (excitation ~488 nm, emission ~509 nm) and mCherry/RFP (excitation ~587 nm, emission ~610 nm).  
6.2 Use a 20× or 40× water-immersion objective with correction collar adjusted for fructose RI (~1.47).  

7 Storage (if needed)  
7.1 Store samples in 100% fructose at 4 °C for up to 2 weeks without significant signal loss. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: up to 2 weeks)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP, mCherry/RFP]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is highly suitable for small, whole-organism samples like *C. elegans*, offering rapid and effective optical clearing while preserving endogenous fluorescent proteins such as EGFP and mCherry with high fidelity. It is a methanol-based protocol that efficiently removes lipids, enabling deep imaging penetration. The absence of embedding or sectioning preserves the 3D architecture, which is critical for mapping spatial relationships between the nerve ring, nerve cords, and neuronal somata. Since the sample already expresses dual-color fluorescent reporters, no additional labeling is required unless nuclear or structural counterstains are desired. However, in this case, the endogenous signals are sufficient for structural mapping.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preprocessing  
1.1 Wash fixed *C. elegans* adults 3× in PBS for 10 minutes each at RT to remove fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes total)  
1.2 Incubate in 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS for 1 hour to enhance permeabilization. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubate in 50% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubate in 70% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubate in 100% methanol twice, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubate in freshly prepared 5% H2O2 in methanol (1:5 dilution of 30% H2O2 in methanol) overnight at 4 °C. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Replace with fresh 5% H2O2 in methanol and incubate for another 6 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 6 hours)  

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubate in 70% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubate in 50% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubate in PBS with 0.3% Triton X-100 for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Optional Nuclear Staining (if needed for anatomical reference)  
5.1 Incubate in 1:10,000 dilution of DAPI in PBS with 0.3% Triton X-100 for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.2 Wash 3× in PBS with 0.3% Triton X-100, 30 minutes each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 90 minutes total)  

6 Clearing  
6.1 Incubate in 1:2 mixture of benzyl alcohol and benzyl benzoate (BABB) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Transfer to 100% BABB and incubate until fully transparent (typically 2–4 hours). (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  

7 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
7.1 Incubate in dibenzyl ether (DBE) for 1 hour to match RI for light-sheet or confocal imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

8 Imaging and Storage  
8.1 Mount worms in DBE on a glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber.  
8.2 Store in DBE at 4 °C in the dark if imaging is delayed. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: up to 2 weeks)

**Chosen Method:** SeeDB2  
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP, mCherry]  
**Justification:** SeeDB2 is a fructose-based optical clearing method that is highly suitable for small, whole-organism samples like *C. elegans*, offering rapid refractive index (RI) matching, minimal tissue deformation, and excellent preservation of endogenous fluorescent proteins such as EGFP and mCherry. It avoids harsh chemical treatments that may degrade fluorescence or alter morphology, making it ideal for 3D imaging of fine neural structures like the nerve ring and neuronal processes. The method is compatible with dual-color imaging and supports high-resolution light-sheet or confocal imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Pre-Wash  
1.1 Incubation with 1× PBS containing 0.1% Tween-20 (PBST) (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.2 Repeat step 1.1 (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 50% ethanol in PBST (vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
2.2 Incubation with 70% ethanol in PBST (vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
2.3 Incubation with 100% ethanol (freshly prepared, pre-chilled) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 30 minutes)  
2.4 Repeat step 2.3 (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 30 minutes)

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% methanol (prechilled) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 1:1 methanol:dichloromethane (vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 100% dichloromethane (freshly prepared) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Repeat step 3.3 (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 1:1 methanol:1× PBST (vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
4.2 Incubation with 50% methanol in PBST (vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
4.3 Incubation with 1× PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.4 Repeat step 4.3 (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

5 Mounting and RI Matching  
5.1 Incubation with SeeDB2 solution (50% fructose in 1× PBST, pH 8.0, RI ~1.47) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with SeeDB2G (50% fructose, 25% glycerol in 1× PBST, pH 8.0, RI ~1.49) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.3 Incubation with SeeDB2G+ (50% fructose, 50% glycerol in 1× PBST, pH 8.0, RI ~1.51) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12–24 hours)

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Mount sample in a glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber using SeeDB2G+ solution  
6.2 Seal chamber edges with vacuum grease to prevent evaporation during long-term imaging  
6.3 Perform 3D imaging using a confocal or light-sheet microscope optimized for EGFP (Ex/Em ~488/509 nm) and mCherry/RFP (Ex/Em ~587/610 nm) fluorescence detection

**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488/568/647, Myosin VIIa antibody (or GFP if available), DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for small whole organisms like 5 dpf zebrafish larvae due to its rapid clearing, excellent preservation of endogenous fluorescence (e.g., GFP, mCherry), and compatibility with immunolabeling. It is methanol-based and detergent-free, minimizing tissue damage and antigen loss. Phalloidin directly labels F-actin in stereocilia bundles, while Myosin VIIa confirms hair cell identity. DAPI labels nuclei for anatomical orientation. This combination enables high-resolution visualization of hair cell morphology, spatial organization, and stereocilia architecture in cleared whole larvae.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling (if using Myosin VIIa antibody)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)

1.3 Wash with PBST (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) 5 times, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour)

2.2 Wash with PBST 5 times, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour)

3.2 Wash with PBST 5 times, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour)

4.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

6.2 Incubation with 100% DCM for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

7.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.2 Incubation with 33% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.3 Incubation with PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

8.2 Replace with fresh iDISCO+ solution and incubate for another 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

9.2 Replace with fresh RI-matching solution and incubate for imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: up to 72 hours)

10.2 Image using confocal or light-sheet microscopy. Adjust z-stack and channel settings to capture Phalloidin (488/568/647), Myosin VIIa (Alexa Fluor 568/647), and DAPI signals.

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488/568/647, anti-Myosin VIIa (or anti-F-actin if Phalloidin is unavailable), DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole-mount small organisms like 5 dpf zebrafish larvae due to its rapid clearing, excellent preservation of fluorescent proteins and compatibility with small molecule dyes like Phalloidin. It is methanol-based, which enhances tissue penetration and lipid removal, and it is compatible with immunolabeling. Phalloidin directly labels F-actin-rich stereocilia with high specificity and signal-to-noise, avoiding the need for secondary antibodies. Myosin VIIa is a well-established hair cell marker in zebrafish. DAPI is used for nuclear counterstain to aid in anatomical orientation and cell identification.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling (if required)
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody (e.g., anti-Myosin VIIa, 1:500 dilution) in blocking solution for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS) 6 times over 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody (if applicable; not required if using directly conjugated Phalloidin) in blocking solution for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBST 6 times over 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours total)

2 Nuclear Counterstain
2.1 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 dilution in PBS) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Wash with PBS 3 times over 6 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 6 hours total)

3 Phalloidin Staining
3.1 Incubation with Phalloidin conjugated to Alexa Fluor (e.g., 488/568/647, 1:200 dilution in PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Wash with PBS 3 times over 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours total)

4 Dehydration
4.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.6 Incubation with 100% methanol for an additional 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

5 Delipidation (Clearing)
5.1 Incubation with freshly prepared dichloromethane (DCM)/methanol (2:1 vol/vol) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with fresh dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Repeat step 5.2 for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

6 Rehydration (Optional for imaging in PBS)
6.1 Incubation with DCM/methanol (1:2 vol/vol) for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with 100% methanol for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.3 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.4 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.5 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.6 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.7 Incubation with PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

7 Refractive Index (RI) Matching
7.1 Incubation with dibenzyl ether (DBE) for RI matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3–6 hours)  
7.2 Replace with fresh DBE and incubate until sample becomes fully transparent (typically 12–24 hours). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12–24 hours)

8.2 Store in DBE at 4 °C in the dark if not imaging immediately.

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488, tdTomato (for side line nerve fibers), DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole-mount small organisms like 5 dpf zebrafish larvae due to its excellent optical clearing, rapid processing time, and strong preservation of fluorescent signals such as tdTomato and Alexa Fluor dyes. It is compatible with direct labeling using Phalloidin for F-actin and allows deep imaging of 3D structures like hair cell bundles and innervating nerve fibers. The use of DAPI provides nuclear counterstaining for anatomical orientation and cell density mapping.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Whole-mount Immunolabeling and Staining  
1.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization solution (10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488 (1:200 dilution in blocking solution) for actin bundle labeling. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.3 Wash with 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (5× 1 hour each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 5× 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 dilution in PBS) for nuclear staining. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.5 Final wash with PBS (3× 30 minutes each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3× 30 minutes)

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.6 Replacement with fresh 100% methanol and incubation for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 5% (vol/vol) H2O2 in methanol (made from 30% H2O2 stock) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Wash with 100% methanol (3× 1 hour each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3× 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour to remove lipids. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with fresh dichloromethane for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 1:1 dichloromethane/methanol for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% methanol for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.3 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.4 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.5 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.6 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.7 Incubation with PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

5 Tissue Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (BABB: 1 part benzyl alcohol, 2 parts benzyl benzoate) for 1–3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1–3 hours)  
5.2 Replace with fresh BABB and incubate until full clearing is achieved (transparent body, visible internal structures). (Temperature: RT, Time: up to 6 hours)

6 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
6.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (100% BABB) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Transfer to imaging chamber with BABB for light-sheet or confocal imaging.

7 Storage and Imaging  
7.1 For long-term storage: Incubation with fresh BABB at 4 °C. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: indefinite)  
7.2 Prior to imaging: Ensure sample is fully submerged in BABB and free of bubbles. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate use or within 24 hours)

**Chosen Method:** ScaleS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin, mCherry, DAPI]  
**Justification:** ScaleS is a sorbitol-based, urea-containing clearing method that provides excellent fluorescence preservation, especially for fluorescent proteins like mCherry, and is well-suited for small whole organisms such as 5 dpf zebrafish. It avoids the abrupt osmotic shifts seen in ScaleS0→ScaleS4 transitions, thereby minimizing tissue swelling. Phalloidin is used for direct F-actin labeling of stereocilia bundles, and DAPI labels nuclei for anatomical orientation. The stepwise increase in sorbitol concentration ensures gradual RI matching and minimal morphological distortion.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preprocessing  
1.1 Incubation with PBS-T (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) for permeabilization. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with DAPI (1:1000 in PBS-T) for nuclear staining. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS-T (3 × 1 hour) to remove excess DAPI. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with Phalloidin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 or 568 (1:200 in PBS-T) for F-actin labeling. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBS-T (3 × 1 hour) to remove excess Phalloidin. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)

2 ScaleS Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with ScaleS0 (urea 4 M, sorbitol 30%, glycerol 10%, in PBS, pH 7.5) for equilibration. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with ScaleS1 (urea 4 M, sorbitol 40%, glycerol 20%, in PBS, pH 7.5). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with ScaleS2 (urea 4 M, sorbitol 50%, glycerol 30%, in PBS, pH 7.5). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with ScaleS3 (urea 4 M, sorbitol 60%, glycerol 40%, in PBS, pH 7.5). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)

3 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
3.1 Incubation with ScaleS4 (urea 4 M, sorbitol 70%, glycerol 50%, in PBS, pH 7.5) for final RI matching. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)

4 Mounting and Imaging  
4.1 Transfer cleared sample to a glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber.  
4.2 Add a small volume of ScaleS4 solution to maintain RI matching during imaging.  
4.3 Perform 3D imaging using a confocal or light-sheet microscope optimized for cleared samples (e.g., with water or silicone immersion objectives and adjusted zoom settings for refractive index).  

5 Optional Long-Term Storage  
5.1 Store samples in ScaleS4 at 4 °C in the dark for up to several weeks with minimal fluorescence loss.

**Chosen Method:** ClearSee  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP, YFP, SCRI Renaissance 2200]  
**Justification:** ClearSee is a plant-specific optical clearing method that effectively reduces tissue autofluorescence and chlorophyll content while preserving endogenous fluorescent proteins such as GFP and YFP. It is ideal for whole-mount plant samples like *Arabidopsis* seedlings, especially when combined with SCRI Renaissance 2200 for cell wall labeling. This method balances clearing speed, fluorescence preservation, and refractive index matching, making it suitable for 3D imaging of root and shoot architecture with subcellular resolution.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Decolorization and Delipidation  
1.1 Incubation with freshly prepared chloral hydrate solution (8 g chloral hydrate, 1 mL glycerol, 2 mL ddH₂O) for chlorophyll removal. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Replace solution with fresh chloral hydrate solution and continue incubation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Cell Wall Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with 0.1% (w/v) SCRI Renaissance 2200 in PBS for cell wall staining. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Wash with PBS (3×, 1 hour each at RT) to remove excess dye.  

3 Tissue Clearing  
3.1 Incubation with ClearSee solution I (25% w/v urea, 10% w/v glycerol, 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) to initiate clearing. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with ClearSee solution II (50% w/v urea, 20% w/v glycerol, 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with ClearSee solution III (75% w/v urea, 25% w/v glycerol, 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) until tissue becomes macroscopically transparent. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24–48 hours)  

4 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
4.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (80% glycerol in PBS) to equilibrate tissue for imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.2 Replace with fresh 80% glycerol solution and continue incubation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

5 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Transfer cleared and stained sample into a glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber.  
5.2 Add 80% glycerol solution to maintain RI matching and prevent drying during imaging.  
5.3 Proceed with light-sheet or high-resolution confocal microscopy for 3D visualization of GFP/YFP expression and SCRI Renaissance 2200-labeled cell walls.

**Chosen Method:** ClearSee  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP, YFP, Calcofluor White]  
**Justification:** ClearSee is a plant-specific optical clearing method that effectively renders plant tissues transparent while preserving fluorescent protein signals such as GFP and YFP. It is especially suitable for whole-mount plant samples like *Arabidopsis* seedlings and is compatible with fluorescent dyes. Calcofluor White is a well-established fluorescent cell wall stain that labels cellulose and is fully compatible with GFP/YFP signals. This combination allows for simultaneous visualization of gene expression patterns and cell morphology, including root apical organization, vascular boundaries, and lateral root initiation sites, without the need for antibody labeling.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Optical Clearing  
1.1 Incubation with freshly prepared Clearing Solution I (8 N Urea, 1% (v/v) Triton X-100, 150 mM NaCl, 50 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with Clearing Solution II (8 N Urea, 1% (v/v) Triton X-100, 25% (v/v) Glycerol, 150 mM NaCl, 50 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with Clearing Solution III (8 N Urea, 1% (v/v) Triton X-100, 50% (v/v) Glycerol, 150 mM NaCl, 50 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with Clearing Solution IV (8 N Urea, 1% (v/v) Triton X-100, 75% (v/v) Glycerol, 150 mM NaCl, 50 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Cell Wall Staining  
2.1 Incubation with 0.1% (w/v) Calcofluor White in PBS (pH 7.4) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Wash with PBS (3 × 30 min) to remove excess dye (Temperature: RT)  

3 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
3.1 Incubation with RI Matching Solution I (8 N Urea, 1% (v/v) Triton X-100, 90% (v/v) Glycerol, 150 mM NaCl, 50 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with RI Matching Solution II (8 N Urea, 1% (v/v) Triton X-100, 99% (v/v) Glycerol, 150 mM NaCl, 50 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

4 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
4.1 Transfer samples into a glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber.  
4.2 Mount in RI Matching Solution II or 80% Glycerol in PBS for confocal or light-sheet imaging.  
4.3 Store samples at 4 °C in the dark if imaging is not immediate (samples can be stored for up to 2 weeks without significant signal loss).  

**Imaging Notes:**  
- Use appropriate filter sets for GFP (excitation ~488 nm, emission ~510 nm), YFP (~514 nm excitation, ~527 nm emission), and Calcofluor White (~405 nm excitation, ~450 nm emission).  
- For deep imaging, light-sheet microscopy is recommended; confocal microscopy is suitable for high-resolution subcellular imaging.

**Chosen Method:** ClearSee  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP, YFP, SCRI Renaissance 2200]  
**Justification:** ClearSee is a plant-specific optical clearing method that effectively renders plant tissues transparent while preserving endogenous fluorescent proteins such as GFP and YFP. It is especially suitable for whole seedlings like *Arabidopsis*, which have complex cellular structures and lignified cell walls. SCRI Renaissance 2200 is a plant cell wall-specific fluorescent dye that labels lignin and cellulose without requiring immunostaining, making it ideal for visualizing cell wall architecture in 3D. This combination allows for simultaneous visualization of cell wall boundaries and transgene expression patterns across root developmental zones, including the root apical meristem, elongation zone, and differentiation zone.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Pretreatment  
1.1 Incubation with 100 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0, 10 mM EDTA for 1 hour to enhance permeability. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in Tris-EDTA buffer for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

2 Chlorophyll Removal  
2.1 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) ethanol in water for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Sequential incubation with 80% ethanol for 1 hour, then 100% ethanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each step)  
2.3 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) ethanol:chloral hydrate solution for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Clearing with ClearSee  
3.1 Incubation with ClearSee solution (25% w/v urea, 10% w/v NaOH, 15% w/v glycerol) at 37 °C. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 24–48 hours or until fully transparent)

4.2 Wash with ClearSee solution 3 times for 1 hour each to remove excess dye. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
5.1 Incubation with RI matching solution (80% glycerol, 20% ClearSee) for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
5.2 Transfer to 100% glycerol for final RI matching and long-term storage. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

6.1 Mount sample in 100% glycerol in a glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber.  
6.2 Image using a confocal or light-sheet microscope with:  
  - **GFP/YFP channel**: Excitation 488 nm, Emission 500–550 nm  
  - **Cell wall (SCRI Renaissance 2200)**: Excitation 561 nm, Emission 580–620 nm  
6.3 Adjust z-stack settings to capture full 3D root architecture, including root tip, elongation, and differentiation zones.

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP, YFP, SCRI Renaissance 2200]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is highly suitable for small whole-plant tissues like *Arabidopsis* seedlings due to its effective delipidation and refractive index (RI) matching while preserving endogenous fluorescent proteins (GFP/YFP). It is methanol-based and provides superior chlorophyll removal compared to ClearSee, especially when combined with H2O2 bleaching. SCRI Renaissance 2200 specifically labels cell walls and is compatible with iDISCO+ clearing, enabling clear visualization of tissue architecture and precise localization of fluorescent reporter signals. This method supports deep imaging of root systems and 3D cellular mapping.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Bleaching and Chlorophyll Removal  
1.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H2O2 in methanol (1 volume of 30% H2O2 in 5 volumes of methanol) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
1.2 Wash with 100% methanol (3×, 30 min each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min × 3)  

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with freshly prepared iDISCO+ delipidation solution (60% (vol/vol) methanol, 30% DMSO, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24–48 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Replace solution with fresh delipidation solution and incubate for another 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Wash  
3.1 Wash with 100% methanol (3×, 30 min each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min × 3)  
3.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% Tween-20 (PBSTw) (3×, 30 min each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min × 3)  

4 Cell Wall Staining  
4.1 Incubation with SCRI Renaissance 2200 (1:100 dilution in PBSTw) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Wash with PBSTw (3×, 1 hour each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 3)  

5 Tissue Optical Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (60% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM), 30% methanol, 10% DMSO) for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.2 Replace with fresh iDISCO+ clearing solution and incubate for another 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
6.1 Incubation with dibenzyl ether (DBE) for RI matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
6.2 Replace with fresh DBE and incubate for an additional 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

7 Mounting and Imaging  
7.1 Mount sample in DBE in a glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber.  
7.2 Perform deep imaging using confocal or light-sheet microscopy to visualize GFP/YFP reporter signals and SCRI Renaissance 2200-labeled cell walls.  

**Notes:**  
- Ensure all incubations are performed on a gentle orbital shaker.  
- For long-term storage post-clearing, samples can be kept in DBE at 4 °C in the dark.  
- Avoid exposure to light during and after staining and clearing to preserve fluorescence.

**Chosen Labeling:** [α-bungarotoxin-Alexa Fluor 647, β-III Tubulin-Alexa Fluor 488]

Both Alexa Fluor dyes are highly photostable and compatible with BoneClear’s clearing chemistry.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Whole Mount Immunolabeling (if not already performed)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-β-III Tubulin (1:1000) in labeling buffer (1% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% Tween-20 (PBST), 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:1000) and α-bungarotoxin-Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in labeling buffer for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBST, 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol, 2 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 1:2 methanol/dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% DCM for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 1:1 DCM:ethyl cinnamate (EC) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 100% EC for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Tissue Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with BoneClear solution (EC:benzyl benzoate 1:1, RI ≈ 1.54) for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [α-Bungarotoxin-Alexa Fluor 647, β-III Tubulin (TUJ1)-Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole-organ skeletal muscle clearing due to its excellent preservation of fluorescent proteins and compatibility with immunolabeling. It provides rapid and effective delipidation and refractive index homogenization, which is critical for high-resolution 3D imaging of NMJs. α-Bungarotoxin specifically labels AChR clusters (post-synaptic), while β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) labels neuronal processes (pre-synaptic), enabling precise co-visualization of NMJ components. This combination allows for accurate assessment of synaptic alignment, fragmentation, and spatial distribution across muscle regions.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling  
1.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization solution (0.3% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 5% donkey serum in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: α-Bungarotoxin-Alexa Fluor 647 (1:200) and β-III Tubulin (TUJ1)-Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) in labeling buffer (0.3% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO in PBS) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100 (5 × 1 hour at RT)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (3 × 1 hour at RT)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 5% H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes methanol) at 4 °C (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 1:2 DCM:BABB (benzyl alcohol/benzyl benzoate) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 100% BABB for 2 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

4 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
4.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with 100% glycerol (RI = 1.47) for final clearing (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  

5 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Mount sample in 100% glycerol in a custom imaging chamber with spacers to prevent compression  
5.2 Seal chamber with coverslip using silicone grease  
5.3 Image using light-sheet or confocal microscopy optimized for Alexa Fluor 488 and Alexa Fluor 647 channels  

6 Optional Long-Term Storage  
6.1 Store cleared sample in 100% glycerol at 4 °C in the dark (up to several months without significant signal loss)

请根据该科学问题自行选择合适的荧光/标记策略，并匹配适合完整骨骼肌三维成像的组织透明方法。若限制范围内的 alpha-bungarotoxin 可直接标记突触后膜，应作为主标记；若 Phalloidin 可提供肌纤维 F-actin 结构参考，可作为辅助探针，但不能替代 NMJ 或神经末梢标记。请仅输出 protocol，第 1 行写明所选荧光/标记策略和组织透明方法，随后仅列出透明处理、RI 匹配和保存/成像前处理步骤的关键试剂、条件和时间。

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [α-bungarotoxin-Alexa Fluor 594, Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488, β-III Tubulin (TUJ1)-Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for small, fixed tissues like skeletal muscle due to its rapid clearing, excellent preservation of fluorescent proteins and dye signals, and compatibility with whole-mount immunolabeling. It allows deep 3D imaging with light-sheet or confocal microscopy. α-bungarotoxin directly labels NMJ AChR clusters, Phalloidin highlights F-actin for myofiber orientation, and β-III Tubulin labels motor axons, enabling precise mapping of NMJ spatial relationships.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling and Dye Staining  
1.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization solution (20% DMSO, 5% donkey serum, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with α-bungarotoxin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 594 (1:200 dilution), Phalloidin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:100 dilution), and β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) primary antibody (1:500 dilution) in labeling buffer (1% DMSO, 3% donkey serum, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS (6 × 1 hour). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500 dilution) in labeling buffer for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.5 Wash with 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS (6 × 1 hour). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 1 hour)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour (2 changes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with freshly prepared dichloromethane (DCM)/methanol (2:1 vol/vol) for 3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour (2 changes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

4 Tissue Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with 100% dibenzyl ether (DBE) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with fresh 100% DBE for 3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Optional: Incubation with DBE containing 0.1% Sudan Black B for 1–3 hours to reduce autofluorescence. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1–3 hours)  
5.2 Final incubation with fresh 100% DBE for refractive index matching and imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: overnight or until imaging)  

6 Imaging  
6.1 Mount sample in DBE in a custom chamber with anti-fade support (e.g., coverslip sealed with silicone grease).  
6.2 Image using light-sheet or high-penetration confocal microscopy with appropriate filter sets for Alexa Fluor 488, 594, and 647.

**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5+Alexa Fluor 647, HuC/D+Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole-organ optical clearing due to its excellent lipid removal efficiency, compatibility with immunolabeling, and preservation of fluorescent protein signals and antibody labeling. It is particularly suitable for thick, multilayered tissues like the mouse stomach, enabling deep imaging of fine neural structures. PGP9.5 and HuC/D are pan-neuronal markers that label all nerve fibers, including vagal terminals, while DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for anatomical orientation. This labeling strategy ensures comprehensive visualization of the entire intramural neural network across all gastric regions.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling (if not already performed)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization solution (0.3% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 5% donkey serum in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-PGP9.5 (1:500) and anti-HuC/D (1:200) in labeling solution (0.3% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 3% donkey serum in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100 (6× 1 hour each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit and Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse (1:1000 each) in labeling solution for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100 (6× 1 hour each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
1.6 Optional nuclear counterstain: incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 in PBS) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour (×2 changes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 5% H₂O₂ in methanol (v/v) at 4 °C for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour (×2 changes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)  

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with PBS for 1 hour (×2 changes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)  

5 Tissue Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (20% DMSO, 30% ethyl cinnamate in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with fresh iDISCO+ solution for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.3 Repeat step 5.2 until full transparency is achieved (typically 2–3 cycles).  

6 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
6.1 Incubation with RI matching solution (100% ethyl cinnamate) for 3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
6.2 Transfer to fresh RI matching solution and store at RT until imaging.  

7 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Mount the cleared stomach in a custom imaging chamber filled with ethyl cinnamate.  
7.2 Image using light-sheet fluorescence microscopy or high-penetration confocal microscopy.

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5+Alexa Fluor 647, β-III Tubulin+Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI, Phalloidin-TRITC]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole-organ clearing such as the mouse stomach due to its excellent tissue penetration, rapid delipidation, and strong preservation of fluorescent signals, which is critical for detecting both endogenous and antibody-labeled signals. It is compatible with multiple fluorophores and allows high-resolution 3D imaging via light-sheet or confocal microscopy. The labeling strategy includes PGP9.5 (a pan-neuronal marker) and β-III Tubulin (neuronal cytoskeleton) to comprehensively label the intramural nerve network. DAPI is used for nuclear counterstain, and Phalloidin-TRITC labels smooth muscle layers to provide structural context for nerve localization across different gastric wall layers.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling Completion (if not already performed)  
1.1 Wash tissue 3× 1 hour with PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100 (PBSTx) at RT to remove fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  
1.2 Incubate with blocking solution (5% donkey serum, 0.3% PBSTx in PBS) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
1.3 Incubate with primary antibodies: anti-PGP9.5 (1:500) and anti-β-III Tubulin (1:1000) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.4 Wash 5× 2 hours with 0.3% PBSTx at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 hours total)  
1.5 Incubate with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit and Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.6 Wash 5× 2 hours with 0.3% PBSTx at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 hours total)  
1.7 Incubate with DAPI (1:10,000) and Phalloidin-TRITC (1:200) in PBS for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
1.8 Wash 5× 2 hours with PBS at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 hours total)

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubate in 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubate in 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubate in 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubate in 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubate in 100% methanol for 1 hour (×2 changes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubate in freshly prepared 5% H₂O₂ in methanol (v/v) at 4 °C for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Incubate in 100% methanol for 1 hour (×2 changes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubate in 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubate in 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubate in 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubate in 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubate in PBS for 1 hour (×2 changes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)

5 Tissue Clearing  
5.1 Incubate in iDISCO+ clearing solution (Dibenzyl Ether, DBE) at RT without shaking until tissue becomes transparent (typically 24–48 hours). (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)

6 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
6.1 Incubate in RI-matching solution (100% DBE) for 3 hours to equilibrate. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
6.2 Replace with fresh RI-matching solution and incubate overnight. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

7 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Mount sample in a glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber using 100% DBE.  
7.2 Store in the dark at RT if imaging is not immediate. (Temperature: RT, Time: up to 2 weeks)  
7.3 Image using light-sheet or high-magnification confocal microscopy with multi-channel detection for Alexa Fluor 488 (β-III Tubulin), Alexa Fluor 647 (PGP9.5), TRITC (Phalloidin), and DAPI (nuclei).

2.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

请根据该科学问题自行选择合适的荧光/标记策略，并基于所选标记样本选择匹配的组织透明方法。若已有 EGFP 与 tdTomato 内源荧光报告信号可以直接完成投射神经元和轴突示踪，应优先保留该信号，不应额外选择抗体替代同一主示踪目标。请仅输出 protocol，第 1 行写明所选荧光/标记策略和组织透明方法，随后仅列出透明处理、RI 匹配和保存/成像前处理步骤的关键试剂、条件和时间。

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP, tdTomato]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is highly suitable for whole mouse brain clearing, offering excellent preservation of endogenous fluorescent proteins (e.g., EGFP and tdTomato), fast processing, and compatibility with light-sheet microscopy. It uses a methanol-based dehydration and delipidation strategy that effectively clears lipids while maintaining fluorescent signal integrity. This method is ideal for mapping long-range projections in the whole brain, especially in emotion-related circuits such as amygdala–prefrontal cortex–thalamus–nucleus accumbens pathways.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preprocessing  
1.1 Wash brain in PBS for 1 hour at RT to remove residual fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubate brain in 0.3% glycine in PBS for 1 hour to quench residual aldehydes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Perform three 1-hour PBS washes at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubate brain in 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Transfer to 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Continue dehydration in 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Proceed to 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubate in 100% methanol for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubate brain in freshly prepared dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Replace with fresh DCM and incubate for 2–4 hours until brain becomes visibly transparent. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2–4 hours)  
3.3 Repeat DCM incubation if full transparency is not achieved. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2–4 hours)

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Transfer brain to 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubate in 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Continue in 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubate in 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Final wash in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
5.1 Incubate brain in iDISCO+ RI-matching solution (DBE/Toluene, 1:1 vol/vol) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Transfer to 100% dibenzyl ether (DBE) and incubate for 12–24 hours until full RI matching is achieved. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12–24 hours)

6 Imaging and Storage  
6.1 Mount brain in a light-sheet imaging chamber using 1% agarose in PBS.  
6.2 Image using light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) with appropriate filter sets for EGFP (excitation ~488 nm, emission ~509 nm) and tdTomato (excitation ~554 nm, emission ~581 nm).  
6.3 Store cleared brain in DBE at 4 °C in the dark for long-term preservation. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: up to several months)

**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP, tdTomato, Phalloidin]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is highly suitable for whole mouse brain clearing, offering excellent preservation of endogenous fluorescent proteins (e.g., EGFP and tdTomato), fast processing, and compatibility with immunolabeling. It is particularly effective for 3D imaging of long-range projections and fine neuronal structures such as dendrites. Phalloidin staining labels F-actin in dendritic spines and enhances visualization of the local neuronal architecture. This method avoids harsh denaturation steps, preserving both fluorescent proteins and antigenicity, and achieves high refractive index (RI) homogenization for deep imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preprocessing  
1.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 20% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) DMSO and 5 mg/mL glycine in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS for 3 × 30 min. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1.5 hours total)

2 Permeabilization  
2.1 Incubation with 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Wash with PBS for 3 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)

3 Blocking  
3.1 Incubation with blocking solution (0.3% Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum in PBS) for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)

4 Immunolabeling  
4.1 Incubation with Phalloidin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 at 1:200 dilution in blocking solution for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
4.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100 for 5 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 hours total)

5 Dehydration  
5.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.3 Incubation with 100% methanol for 2 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)

6 Delipidation  
6.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1:20 dilution of 30% H₂O₂ in methanol) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with 100% methanol for 2 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)

7 Clearing  
7.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) in methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.2 Incubation with 100% DBE for 2 × 3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
7.3 Incubation with fresh 100% DBE for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

8 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
8.1 Incubation with RI matching solution (100% DBE) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

9 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
9.1 Store sample in 100% DBE at RT until imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)  
9.2 Prior to imaging, mount brain in a chamber filled with DBE and image using light-sheet or confocal microscopy optimized for EGFP, tdTomato, and Alexa Fluor 647 channels.

2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% H2O2 in methanol for 12–24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12–24 hours)
