3.1 Incubation with methanol series (80%, 60%, 40%, 20%) in PBS-T (0.2% Triton X-100), each step for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours total)  
3.2 Incubation with PBS-T (0.2% Triton X-100) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% DMSO, 5% donkey serum in PBS-T) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 1 day)

4.5 Incubation with PBS-T (0.2% Triton X-100) for 1 hour (×3 washes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)

5.1 Incubation with methanol series (20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100%) in PBS-T, each step for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 hours total)

8.2 Image using light-sheet or high-penetration confocal microscopy (e.g., 20× dipping objective, NA ≥ 1.0).

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP, tdTomato, F-Actin (Phalloidin)]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole mouse brain clearing, especially when preserving endogenous fluorescent proteins like EGFP and tdTomato. It provides excellent lipid removal, deep penetration, and strong fluorescence retention. The methanol-based delipidation is highly effective and compatible with 3D imaging of long-range projections. Phalloidin labeling of F-actin allows for high-resolution visualization of dendritic spines and cytoskeletal structures, which is critical for analyzing local neuronal architecture. This method also supports high-quality antibody labeling and avoids the issues of incomplete clearing and weak far-red signal often seen in SWITCH protocols.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preprocessing  
1.1 Incubation with methanol:H2O (1:1) solution. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with methanol:H2O (3:1) solution. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with 100% methanol. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Bleaching (if endogenous autofluorescence is a concern)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% H2O2 in methanol. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12–24 hours, optional)  
2.2 Wash with 100% methanol until tissue regains original color. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  

3 Immunolabeling  
3.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization solution (0.2% gelatin, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-F-Actin (Phalloidin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 or similar far-red fluorophore, 1:200 dilution) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 5–7 days)  
3.3 Wash with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) to remove unbound antibody. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 5 × 24 hours)  
3.4 Optional: Counterstain with DAPI (1:10,000 in PBST) for nuclei. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
3.5 Wash with PBST. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 3 × 24 hours)  

4 Delipidation  
4.1 Incubation with freshly prepared dichloromethane:methanol (2:1) solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with fresh dichloromethane:methanol (2:1) solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.3 Wash with methanol to remove residual lipids. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
5.1 Incubation with dibenzyl ether (DBE) for RI matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with fresh DBE. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Imaging and Storage  
6.1 Mount brain in a glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber using DBE.  
6.2 Store in dark at RT in sealed container with parafilm to prevent evaporation.  
6.3 Perform light-sheet or confocal imaging using appropriate filters for EGFP, tdTomato, Alexa Fluor 647, and DAPI.

**Protocol Steps:**

1.5 Wash with PBST for 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [c-Fos-Alexa Fluor 647, Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole-brain and extended peripheral tissue clearing, offering excellent preservation of fluorescent proteins and immunolabeling (e.g., c-Fos), which is critical for mapping neuronal activation. It is compatible with lipophilic dyes and immunostaining, and its methanol-based delipidation is fast and scalable for both brain and tongue tissues. Phalloidin provides structural reference of tongue musculature, while DAPI offers nuclear counterstain for anatomical alignment. Alexa Fluor 647 and 488 ensure high signal-to-noise and compatibility with standard light-sheet imaging systems.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling and Staining  
1.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization solution (0.3% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 5% donkey serum in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: c-Fos (rabbit monoclonal, 1:1000 dilution) in blocking solution for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100 (6 × 1 hour each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500 dilution) and Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488 (1:200 dilution) in blocking solution for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100 (6 × 1 hour each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
1.6 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 dilution in PBS) for 12 hours for nuclear staining. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
1.7 Final wash with PBS (3 × 1 hour). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% MeOH in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% MeOH in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% MeOH in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% MeOH in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% MeOH (2 changes) for 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H2O2 in methanol (1 volume 30% H2O2 to 19 volumes MeOH) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 1:1 DCM:MACS-R0 (or BABB) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Tissue Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% dibenzyl ether, 15% sorbitol in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% dibenzyl ether, 30% sorbitol in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% dibenzyl ether, 50% sorbitol in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
5.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (100% dibenzyl ether, RI ~1.56) for 6 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  

6 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Mount sample in refractive index-matched chamber using dibenzyl ether.  
6.2 Store at 4 °C in dark if not imaging immediately. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: up to 2 weeks)  
6.3 Prior to imaging, equilibrate sample in fresh dibenzyl ether for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [DiI, DiD]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is highly suitable for whole-tissue optical clearing of large CNS samples such as spinal cord, thalamus, and cortex due to its excellent lipid removal efficiency, preservation of fluorescent signals, and compatibility with lipophilic tracers like DiI and DiD. These dyes are ideal for long-range axonal tracing without requiring immunostaining, aligning perfectly with the goal of mapping sensory projections in 3D. iDISCO+ uses methanol-based dehydration and BABB (dibenzyl ether) for refractive index (RI) matching, which preserves DiI/DiD fluorescence and enables deep imaging with light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Washing and Permeabilization  
1.1 Wash fixed samples in PBS (pH 7.4) for 1 hour at RT to remove residual fixatives. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubate samples in PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 for 12–24 hours at 4 °C to enhance permeability. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12–24 hours)  

2 Lipophilic Dye Labeling  
2.1 Apply DiI and DiD crystals or solutions to targeted peripheral regions (e.g., dorsal root ganglia) for anterograde labeling. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 2–4 weeks)  
2.2 After labeling, wash samples in PBS for 3 × 30 minutes at RT to remove excess dye. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1.5 hours total)  

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubate samples in 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Transfer to 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Move to 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubate in 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Transfer to 100% methanol for 2 × 1 hour at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)  

4 Delipidation and Clearing  
4.1 Incubate samples in freshly prepared 66% dichloromethane (DCM) and 33% methanol for 1 hour at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Repeat step 4.1 with fresh solution for another 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Transfer samples to 100% DCM for 1 hour to complete delipidation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
5.1 Incubate samples in 1:1 mixture of BABB (dibenzyl ether/benzyl alcohol, 1:2 vol/vol) and DCM for 1 hour at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Transfer to 100% BABB solution and incubate until fully transparent (typically 12–24 hours for spinal cord and cortical/thalamic samples). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12–24 hours)  

6 Mounting and Imaging  
6.1 Mount samples in custom chambers or glass-bottom dishes using BABB as the mounting medium. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate use or long-term storage)  
6.2 Image using light-sheet fluorescence microscopy or high-magnification confocal microscopy with appropriate filter sets for DiI (excitation ~549 nm, emission ~565 nm) and DiD (excitation ~644 nm, emission ~665 nm).  

7 Storage  
7.1 Store samples in sealed containers with BABB at RT in the dark for long-term preservation. (Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [DiI, DiD]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is highly suitable for large, fixed nervous tissue samples like the spinal cord, thalamus, and cortex due to its excellent lipid removal efficiency, good preservation of fluorescent signals (including lipophilic dyes), and compatibility with whole-tissue imaging. It is fast compared to aqueous-based methods and supports high-resolution 3D imaging with light-sheet or confocal microscopy. DiI and DiD are lipophilic tracers with distinct emission spectra, ideal for dual-channel tracing of separate sensory pathways without requiring antibody labeling. Their stability and compatibility with organic clearing methods like iDISCO+ make them optimal for this application. Nuclear counterstaining with DAPI is included for anatomical reference and registration.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Washing and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100 (PBSTx) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Repeat step 1.1 with fresh PBSTx solution for another 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Lipophilic Dye Labeling  
2.1 Apply DiI and DiD crystals or solutions to targeted peripheral entry points or injection sites to label two distinct sensory pathways. Incubate in a humidified chamber at 37 °C for 2–4 weeks to allow dye diffusion along axons. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 21–30 days)  
2.2 Wash tissue thoroughly with PBSTx (5–6 times over 3 days) to remove excess dye. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 days)  

3 Bleaching (Optional for Autofluorescence Reduction)  
3.1 Incubation with chilled 5% H₂O₂ in methanol (1:5 vol/vol) for 12–24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Wash with methanol (MeOH) until tissue regains original color. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

4 Dehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 20% MeOH in PBSTx for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% MeOH in PBSTx for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% MeOH in PBSTx for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 80% MeOH in PBSTx for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with 100% MeOH for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.6 Repeat step 4.5 with fresh 100% MeOH for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Delipidation  
5.1 Incubation with freshly prepared dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Replace with fresh DCM and incubate for 1–2 days depending on tissue size and lipid content. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
5.3 Repeat with fresh DCM until tissue becomes translucent. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24–48 hours)  

6 Rehydration  
6.1 Incubation with 80% MeOH in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Incubation with 60% MeOH in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.3 Incubation with 40% MeOH in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.4 Incubation with 20% MeOH in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.5 Incubation with PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

7 Nuclear Counterstaining (Optional)  
7.1 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 dilution in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
7.2 Wash with PBSTx (5 times over 2 days). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 days)  

8 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
8.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ RI-matching solution (DBE/Toluene, 1:1 vol/vol) for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
8.2 Replace with fresh RI-matching solution and incubate until tissue becomes fully transparent (typically 24–48 hours). (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  

9 Imaging and Storage  
9.1 Mount tissue in RI-matching solution in an imaging chamber suitable for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.  
9.2 Store remaining tissue in RI-matching solution at 4 °C in the dark for long-term preservation.

**Protocol Steps:**

2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole-tissue optical clearing of large, fixed tissues like the spinal cord and brain regions, offering excellent preservation of lipophilic dyes such as DiI and DiD. It uses a methanol-based dehydration and delipidation process that effectively clears dense, lipid-rich tissues while maintaining fluorescent signal integrity. The protocol can be scaled for long spinal cords and discrete brain regions, and it supports uniform refractive index (RI) matching with dibenzyl ether (DBE), enabling high-resolution 3D imaging via light-sheet or confocal microscopy. This method avoids harsh deterginate like SDS that can strip lipophilic tracers and cause uneven clearing.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (MeOH/PBS) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) MeOH/PBS (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) MeOH/PBS (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) MeOH/PBS (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (pre-chilled) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol (DCM/MeOH) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with fresh 66% DCM/MeOH (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Repeat steps 2.1–2.2 until tissue becomes visibly translucent (typically 4–6 cycles)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) MeOH/PBS (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) MeOH/PBS (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) MeOH/PBS (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) MeOH/PBS (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  

4 Whole-mount Fluorescent Labeling (if needed for anatomical landmarks)  
4.1 Optional incubation with nuclear counterstain: 1:10,000 DAPI in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 24–48 hours)  
4.2 Wash with PBS (3 × 24 hours at RT)  

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
5.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 48–72 hours)  
5.2 Replace with fresh DBE and incubate until tissue is fully cleared and optically transparent (Temperature: RT, Time: 24–48 hours)  

6 Imaging and Storage  
6.1 Mount tissue in DBE-filled imaging chamber suitable for light-sheet or high-magnification confocal imaging  
6.2 Store cleared tissue in 100% DBE at RT in the dark for long-term preservation and repeated imaging sessions

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [tdTomato, IB4 (凝集素), DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is highly suitable for lipid-rich tissues like scWAT due to its efficient delipidation and excellent preservation of fluorescent proteins such as tdTomato. It allows deep imaging in large tissue volumes and is compatible with multiple labeling strategies. tdTomato is used to specifically label the sensory nerve fibers (e.g., via genetically labeled TrkA+ or Nav1.8+ neurons), IB4 labels the pan-nerve network (especially non-peptidergic C-fibers), and DAPI is used for nuclear counterstaining to provide anatomical context. This combination enables precise 3D mapping of sensory nerve distribution and its proportion within the total innervation network.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Washing  
1.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Repeat step 1.2 for a total of 3 washes.  

2 Whole-mount Immunolabeling (if applicable)  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution (PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 10% DMSO + 5% donkey serum) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody (e.g., anti-TrkA or anti-Nav1.8) diluted in blocking solution for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Repeat step 2.3 for a total of 3 washes.  
2.5 Incubation with secondary antibody (e.g., Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated) and IB4-Alexa Fluor 647 in blocking solution for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
2.6 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.7 Repeat step 2.6 for a total of 3 washes.  
2.8 Incubation with DAPI (1:1000 in PBS) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
2.9 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.10 Repeat step 2.9 for a total of 3 washes.  

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.6 Repeat step 3.5 for a total of 2 times.  

4 Delipidation  
4.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 100% dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Repeat step 4.1 for a total of 3 cycles.  
4.3 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Rehydration  
5.1 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.4 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.5 Incubation with PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.6 Repeat step 5.5 for a total of 2 washes.  

6 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
6.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ RI matching solution (DBE:BB:EA = 8:1:1) for 3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with fresh iDISCO+ RI matching solution for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
6.3 Incubation with fresh iDISCO+ RI matching solution for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Mount tissue in a glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber using iDISCO+ RI matching solution.  
7.2 Image using light-sheet or high-penetration confocal microscopy.  

8 Storage (if needed)  
8.1 Store tissue in iDISCO+ RI matching solution at 4 °C in the dark. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: up to 6 months)

1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit and Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse in labeling buffer for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBST, 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with IB4 conjugated to Alexa Fluor 555 (1:200 dilution in PBST) for 24 hours to label vascular lumens. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.7 Wash with PBST, 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CGRP-Alexa Fluor 488, β-III Tubulin-Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is highly effective for lipid-rich tissues like scWAT, offering strong delipidation, excellent preservation of fluorescent signals, and compatibility with whole-mount immunolabeling. It supports deep imaging and progressive RI matching. The dual labeling with CGRP (specific sensory marker) and β-III Tubulin (pan-neuronal marker) ensures clear distinction between sensory and general innervation. Alexa Fluor dyes are bright, photostable, and compatible with iDISCO+ clearing.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling (if not already performed)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 5% (wt/vol) BSA, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: CGRP (1:500), β-III Tubulin (1:1000) in labeling buffer (1% DMSO, 3% BSA, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 (6 × 1 hour at RT)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488 anti-rabbit (CGRP), Alexa Fluor 647 anti-mouse (β-III Tubulin), both at 1:1000 in labeling buffer (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 (6 × 1 hour at RT)

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (2 changes) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (made from 30% H₂O₂ stock) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 1:1 DCM:MACS-R0 (v/v) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20% vol/vol methyl salicylate, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

4 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
4.1 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40% vol/vol MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40% vol/vol MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.3 Optional: Incubation with DBE (Dibenzyl Ether) for final RI matching (Temperature: RT, Time: 6–12 hours) if deeper imaging is required

5 Mounting and Imaging  
5.1 Mount sample in DBE or MACS-R2 in an imaging chamber with low-fluorescence glass  
5.2 Image using light-sheet or high-penetration confocal microscopy (e.g., 20× or 25× dipping objective)  
5.3 For long-term storage: Keep in MACS-R2 at 4 °C (stable for up to several months)

6 Optional: Post-imaging tissue preservation  
6.1 Incubation with 1:1 MACS-R2:PBS (v/v) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
6.3 Store in PBS with 0.05% NaN₃ at 4 °C for future re-labeling or re-clearing

**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1), GFAP, DiI, DAPI]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for dense, calcified tissues like bone, enabling efficient decalcification, delipidation, and deep clearing while preserving endogenous fluorescence and antigenicity. It allows for high-resolution 3D imaging of complex bone structures, including neural elements within the bone marrow cavity, cranial sutures, and foramina. The labeling strategy combines β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) for pan-axonal labeling, GFAP for glial ensheathment, DiI for lipophilic tracing of neural pathways, and DAPI for nuclear counterstain. This combination ensures comprehensive visualization of neural architecture within the bone microenvironment.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preparation and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 10 mM EDTA in PBS (pH 7.4) for decalcification. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours, with gentle shaking)  
1.2 Wash with PBS for 3 × 1 hour to remove EDTA. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  
1.3 Incubation with 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS for permeabilization. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Blocking with 10% normal goat serum (NGS) in PBST (0.3% Triton X-100) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies:  
  - β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) (1:500 dilution)  
  - GFAP (1:1000 dilution)  
(Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours, with gentle shaking)  
2.3 Wash with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100) for 5 × 6 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 hours total)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies:  
  - Alexa Fluor 488 anti-mouse (1:1000)  
  - Alexa Fluor 647 anti-rabbit (1:1000)  
(Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
2.5 Wash with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100) for 5 × 6 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 hours total)  

3 Lipophilic Dye Labeling (DiI)  
3.1 Incubation with 1% DiI in dimethylformamide (DMF) for neural tract tracing. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
3.2 Wash with PBS for 3 × 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  

4 Nuclear Staining  
4.1 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 in PBS) for nuclear labeling. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.2 Wash with PBS for 3 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

5 Dehydration  
5.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

6 Delipidation and Clearing  
6.1 Incubation with 1:1 methanol/dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Incubation with 100% DCM for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.3 Incubation with 1:1 DCM/BABB (benzyl alcohol:benzyl benzoate, 1:1 vol/vol) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.4 Incubation with 100% BABB for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

7 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
7.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (BABB with 0.5% N-phenyl-1-naphthylamine) for final clearing. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

8 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Mount samples in RI-matched chamber with BABB-based mounting medium.  
8.2 Store at 4 °C in the dark until imaging. (Time: up to 2 weeks)  
8.3 Image using light-sheet or confocal microscopy with appropriate filter sets for DAPI, Alexa Fluor 488, Alexa Fluor 647, and DiI.

1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit, Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse, Alexa Fluor 555-conjugated anti-rat (all 1:1000) in 3% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.5 Wash with 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS (5 × 24 hours). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 5 days total)  
1.6 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000) in PBS for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)

2.1 Incubation with 10% EDTA in PBS (pH 7.4) for 7 days with daily solution changes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 7 days total)

3.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

4.1 Incubation with 1:2 benzyl alcohol:benzyl benzoate (BABB) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CGRP-Alexa Fluor 647, IB4-Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for dense calcified tissues like bone, enabling effective optical clearing while preserving fluorescence and tissue architecture. It includes a mild decalcification step compatible with immunolabeling and vascular markers. CGRP labels sensory nerve fibers, IB4 (isolectin B4) directly labels endothelial surfaces of blood vessels, and DAPI stains nuclei for structural reference. This combination allows precise mapping of neurovascular and bone marrow spatial relationships in complex bone-tissue samples.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Antigen Retrieval and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS for permeabilization. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Optional antigen retrieval: Incubation with 10 mM sodium citrate buffer (pH 6.0) at 70°C for 30 minutes, then cool to RT for 30 minutes. (Temperature: 70°C → RT, Time: 1 hour total)

2 Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) to reduce nonspecific binding. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

3 Immunolabeling  
3.1 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-CGRP (1:500 dilution) in labeling buffer (1% normal goat serum, 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 4°C, Time: 48 hours)  
3.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100 (3 × 1 hour) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  
3.3 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:1000 dilution) and IB4-Alexa Fluor 488 conjugate (1:200 dilution) in labeling buffer (Temperature: 4°C, Time: 48 hours)  
3.4 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100 (3 × 1 hour) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)

4 Nuclear Staining  
4.1 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 dilution in PBS) for nuclear labeling. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.2 Wash with PBS (3 × 30 minutes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1.5 hours total)

5 Decalcification  
5.1 Incubation with 0.5 M EDTA (pH 8.0) for mild decalcification. Change solution every 24 hours. (Temperature: 4°C, Time: 72 hours total)  
5.2 Confirm decalcification with a needle test or Alizarin Red S staining of a small tissue piece.

6 Post-fixation  
6.1 Incubation with 4% PFA in PBS for 2 hours to stabilize labeling. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

7 Dehydration  
7.1 Incubation with ascending methanol series: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% (each step for 1 hour). (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 hours total)

8 BoneClear Clearing  
8.1 Incubation with BoneClear solution I (50% glycerol, 50% methanol) for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
8.2 Incubation with BoneClear solution II (80% glycerol, 20% methanol) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
8.3 Incubation with BoneClear solution III (100% glycerol) for 48 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)

9 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
9.1 Incubation with RI matching solution (87% glycerol, 13% PBS, RI ~1.47) for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

10 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
10.1 Store sample in RI matching solution at 4°C until imaging. (Temperature: 4°C, Time: up to 2 weeks)  
10.2 Mount sample in RI-matched chamber with coverslip or custom holder for light-sheet or confocal imaging.

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH (Tyrosine Hydroxylase)+Alexa Fluor 488, NPY+Alexa Fluor 594, DAPI]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for dense calcified tissues like mouse bones, enabling deep optical clearing while preserving fluorescence and antigenicity. It effectively decalcifies and clears bone without compromising structural integrity or fluorescent signals. The labeling strategy targets TH for noradrenergic sympathetic nerve fibers and NPY for peptidergic sympathetic fibers, with DAPI for nuclear counterstain to define bone marrow architecture. This combination allows for high-resolution 3D imaging of sympathetic innervation patterns in relation to bone marrow microdomains.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Decalcification  
1.1 Incubation with 10% (wt/vol) EDTA in PBS (pH 7.4) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.2 Replace with fresh 10% EDTA solution and continue incubation. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)

2 Permeabilization  
2.1 Incubation with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
2.2 Wash with PBS (3×, 1 hour each at RT)

3 Immunolabeling  
3.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-TH (1:500) and anti-NPY (1:200) in blocking buffer (0.3% Triton X-100, 5% normal goat serum in PBS). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
3.2 Wash with PBS (3×, 1 hour each at RT)  
3.3 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit and Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-mouse. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
3.4 Wash with PBS (3×, 1 hour each at RT)  
3.5 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 dilution in PBS) for nuclear staining. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.6 Wash with PBS (3×, 30 minutes each at RT)

4 Dehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

5 Delipidation  
5.1 Incubation with 1:1 methanol/dichloromethane (DCM) solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.3 Incubation with 100% DCM until tissue becomes translucent (up to 6 hours). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)

6 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
6.1 Incubation with 1:1 DCM/BoneClear RI solution (RI = 1.52). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with fresh BoneClear RI solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
6.3 Replace with fresh BoneClear RI solution and continue incubation until full transparency is achieved. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

7 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Transfer samples into a glass-bottom imaging dish.  
7.2 Add BoneClear RI solution to fully submerge the samples.  
7.3 Seal the dish with silicone grease to prevent evaporation during imaging.  
7.4 Store at 4 °C in the dark until imaging. (Time: up to 1 week)  
7.5 For imaging, use light-sheet or confocal microscopy with appropriate filter sets for Alexa Fluor 488, Alexa Fluor 594, and DAPI.

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH (酪氨酸羟化酶), NPY, CD31-Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for bone tissue optical clearing, effectively decalcifying and rendering dense mineralized bone transparent while preserving fluorescence and antigenicity. It allows deep penetration for immunolabeling and is compatible with multiple fluorophores. The labeling strategy targets TH (catecholaminergic marker), NPY (peptidergic marker), CD31 for vasculature, and DAPI for nuclear counterstain, enabling multiplexed imaging of sympathetic nerve distribution, vascular architecture, and cellular organization. This combination supports the quantitative analysis of fiber density, branching, and spatial relationships within the marrow microenvironment.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Decalcification and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 10% (wt/vol) EDTA in PBS (pH 7.4) for decalcification. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 5 days, gentle shaking)  
1.2 Wash with PBS for 1 hour to remove EDTA. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 min washes)  
1.3 Incubation with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS for permeabilization. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-TH (1:500), anti-NPY (1:200) in labeling buffer (1% serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 5 days)  
2.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour washes)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488- and Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-rabbit/mouse IgG (1:1000 each) and CD31-Alexa Fluor 647 (1:200). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 5 days)  
2.5 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour washes)  
2.6 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 dilution in PBS) for nuclear staining. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.7 Final wash with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 min washes)

3 Tissue Dehydration  
3.1 Incubation with ascending methanol series: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% (vol/vol) in PBS, each for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)  
3.2 Incubation with chilled 100% methanol. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 2 hours)

4 Delipidation and Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) benzyl alcohol:benzyl benzoate (BABB) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% BABB. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with fresh 100% BABB. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
5.1 Incubation with RI matching solution (RI = 1.52–1.56, e.g., dibenzyl ether or Visikol HISTO-2). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
5.2 Replace with fresh RI matching solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

6 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Transfer sample to a glass-bottom imaging dish or chamber with RI matching solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: equilibrate for 2 hours before imaging)  
6.2 Store in RI matching solution at 4 °C if imaging is delayed. (Time: up to 2 weeks)

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH-Alexa Fluor 488, NPY-Alexa Fluor 594, IB4-Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for mineralized bone tissues, enabling deep optical clearing while preserving the integrity of both calcified and soft bone marrow structures. It allows for high-resolution 3D imaging of complex bone-bone marrow interfaces. The selected labeling strategy enables multiplexed visualization: TH and NPY label sympathetic and peptidergic nerve fibers respectively, IB4 labels vascular endothelium as a vascular reference, and DAPI labels nuclei for spatial orientation and cell density mapping. This combination supports the scientific goal of analyzing spatial relationships between sympathetic innervation, vasculature, and hematopoietic regions across different bone types.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling Completion  
1.1 Incubate samples with secondary antibodies: Goat anti-Rabbit IgG Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500), Goat anti-Mouse IgG Alexa Fluor 594 (1:500), and IB4-Alexa Fluor 647 (1:200) in PBST-DS (0.3% Triton X-100, 5% DMSO in PBS) at 4 °C for 48 hours.  
1.2 Wash samples in PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 6 × 1 hour at RT.  
1.3 Incubate with DAPI (1:10,000 in PBS) for 1 hour at RT to label nuclei.  
1.4 Wash samples in PBS for 3 × 30 minutes at RT.

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubate samples in 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour at RT.  
2.2 Incubate in 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour at RT.  
2.3 Incubate in 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour at RT.  
2.4 Incubate in 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour at RT.  
2.5 Incubate in 100% methanol for 1 hour at RT (repeat once).  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubate samples in 100% dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour at RT.  
3.2 Incubate in 1:1 DCM:MeOH for 1 hour at RT.  
3.3 Incubate in 100% methanol for 1 hour at RT (repeat twice).  

4 Clearing  
4.1 Incubate samples in BoneClear Solution I (50% glycerol, 50% ethylene glycol in PBS, pH 7.4) for 24 hours at 37 °C.  
4.2 Incubate in BoneClear Solution II (70% glycerol, 30% ethylene glycol in PBS, pH 7.4) for 48 hours at 37 °C.  
4.3 Incubate in BoneClear Solution III (85% glycerol, 15% ethylene glycol in PBS, pH 7.4) for 72 hours at 37 °C.  

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
5.1 Incubate samples in RI-matching solution (90% glycerol, 10% ethylene glycol in PBS, pH 7.4) for 24 hours at 37 °C.  
5.2 Transfer samples into final RI-matching immersion solution (95% glycerol, 5% ethylene glycol in PBS, pH 7.4) and equilibrate for 24–48 hours at 37 °C.  

6 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Mount samples in custom chambers or glass-bottom dishes using 1% agarose in PBS to prevent movement during imaging.  
6.2 Seal samples with silicone grease or imaging chamber covers to prevent evaporation during long-term imaging.  
6.3 Store samples at 4 °C in the dark when not imaging; imaging should be performed at RT using light-sheet or high-penetration confocal microscopy.

**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for mineralized bone tissues, enabling efficient decalcification while preserving fine tissue architecture and antigenicity. It allows deep antibody penetration and is compatible with tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) and neuropeptide Y (NPY) immunostaining. This method balances decalcification, structural preservation, and optical clearing, making it ideal for 3D imaging of bone marrow microarchitecture and sympathetic nerve distribution. TH and NPY labeling are essential for identifying catecholaminergic and peptidergic sympathetic nerve fibers, respectively, which aligns directly with the scientific goal.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunostaining (Post-Fixation)
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-TH (1:500) and anti-NPY (1:1000) in antibody dilution buffer (1% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (5×, 1 hour each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-rabbit and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-goat (1:1000 each) in antibody dilution buffer for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.5 Wash with 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (5×, 1 hour each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 hours total)  

2 Decalcification and Tissue Softening  
2.1 Incubation with 10% (wt/vol) EDTA in PBS (pH 7.4) for 7 days with daily solution changes. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 7 days total)  
2.2 Wash with PBS (3×, 1 hour each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

3 BoneClear Optical Clearing  
3.1 Incubation with BoneClear Solution A (urea 8 M, glycerol 20%, Triton X-100 1%, in PBS) for 48 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with BoneClear Solution B (urea 8 M, glycerol 40%, Triton X-100 1%, in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 72 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with BoneClear Solution C (urea 8 M, glycerol 60%, Triton X-100 1%, in PBS) for 96 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 96 hours)  

4 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
4.1 Incubation with RI matching solution (80% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS, pH 7.4) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with final RI matching solution (100% (vol/vol) glycerol) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Mount sample in 100% glycerol in a glass-bottom imaging dish.  
5.2 Seal sample with silicone grease to prevent evaporation during imaging.  
5.3 Store at 4 °C in the dark until imaging. (Time: up to 2 weeks)  

6 Imaging  
6.1 Acquire 3D images using a light-sheet or high-penetration confocal microscope optimized for glycerol-immersion objectives.  
6.2 Use 594 nm and 647 nm laser lines for TH and NPY signal detection, respectively.  
6.3 Collect z-stacks with 5–10 μm step size for full 3D reconstruction of bone marrow innervation patterns.

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1)+Alexa Fluor 647, NeuroTrace Green, Pan-Cytokeratin+Alexa Fluor 555, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole-organ clearing such as mouse pancreas due to its rapid delipidation, excellent preservation of fluorescent proteins and immunolabeling, and compatibility with light-sheet microscopy. It allows deep imaging of complex tissues while maintaining structural integrity. The labeling strategy includes β-III Tubulin for axonal structures, NeuroTrace Green for neuronal cell bodies, Pan-Cytokeratin for tumor epithelial boundaries, and DAPI for nuclear counterstain, enabling comprehensive visualization of tumor-neuron interactions and PNI architecture.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-β-III Tubulin (1:1000), anti-Pan-Cytokeratin (1:500), and NeuroTrace Green (1:500) in labeling buffer (1% DMSO, 3% donkey serum, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (6 × 1 hour). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse IgG and Alexa Fluor 555-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (both at 1:1000) in labeling buffer for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (6 × 1 hour). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
1.6 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 in PBS) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour (repeat twice). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% DCM for 1 hour (repeat twice). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)  
3.3 Incubation with 100% DCM containing 5% (vol/vol) hydrogen peroxide for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with PBS for 1 hour (repeat twice). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)  

5 Tissue Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (20% (wt/vol) DMSO, 30% (vol/vol) benzyl alcohol, 50% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Replace with fresh iDISCO+ solution and incubate for another 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
6.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (100% dibenzyl ether) for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
6.2 Replace with fresh dibenzyl ether and incubate for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

7 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Transfer the cleared tissue into a light-sheet imaging chamber.  
7.2 Fill the chamber with dibenzyl ether to maintain RI matching during imaging.  
7.3 Store at 4 °C in the dark until imaging. (Time: up to 2 weeks)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1), TH (酪氨酸羟化酶), Pan-Cytokeratin, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole-organ clearing, especially for tissues like pancreas with high lipid content. It enables deep antibody penetration, preserves fluorescence well, and supports multiple rounds of immunolabeling. Compared to PEGASOS, iDISCO+ provides more efficient delipidation and includes a decolorization step to reduce background autofluorescence, which should enhance weak neural signals. The use of β-III Tubulin labels all nerve fibers, while TH labels sympathetic nerves specifically. Pan-Cytokeratin provides a clear tumor boundary reference, and DAPI labels nuclei for structural context and alignment.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Decolorization and Delipidation  
1.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 5% H₂O₂ in methanol (1:20 dilution of 30% H₂O₂ in methanol) to decolorize tissue. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with methanol (100%) to dehydrate tissue. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM) to remove lipids. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with fresh DCM until tissue becomes translucent. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6–12 hours)  

2 Rehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 66% methanol in PBS-Triton X-100 (0.2%) to begin rehydration. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 33% methanol in PBS-Triton X-100 (0.2%). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with PBS-Triton X-100 (0.2%) to fully rehydrate tissue. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Blocking and Antibody Labeling  
3.1 Incubation with blocking solution (6% donkey serum, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: β-III Tubulin (1:1000), TH (1:500), Pan-Cytokeratin (1:500), and DAPI (1:10000) in antibody labeling solution (1% donkey serum, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with PBS-Triton X-100 (0.2%) to wash out unbound primary antibodies. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, repeat 3 times)  
3.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies (if required; e.g., Alexa Fluor 488 and 594 conjugated) in antibody labeling solution. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS-Triton X-100 (0.2%) to wash out unbound secondary antibodies. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, repeat 3 times)  

4 Final Delipidation and Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with 66% DCM in methanol to remove residual lipids. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% DCM until tissue becomes fully transparent. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6–12 hours)  

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
5.1 Incubation with dibenzyl ether (DBE) for RI matching and final clearing. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Incubation with fresh DBE before imaging to maintain clarity. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1–2 hours)  
6.2 Mount tissue in DBE-filled imaging chamber and seal for light-sheet or confocal imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**

1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBST), 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 555-conjugated anti-rat, Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit, and Lectin-Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in PBST for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBST, 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
1.6 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 in PBST) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)

2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1:5 dilution of 30% H₂O₂ in methanol) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 1:1 DCM:MeOH for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin-Alexa Fluor 647, IB4-Alexa Fluor 594, CD31 (PECAM1)]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole-tissue clearing of fixed, perfused mouse brain samples, offering excellent preservation of fluorescent signals, rapid clearing, and compatibility with immunolabeling. It is particularly suitable for vascular imaging due to its ability to clear lipids effectively while maintaining 3D architecture. Lectin and IB4 are widely used to label functional, perfused vessels, and CD31 labels all endothelial-lined vessels, enabling a comprehensive comparison of vascular structure and function across tumor core, invasive margin, and adjacent brain tissue. This combination allows for high-resolution 3D imaging of vascular networks using light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: rat anti-CD31 (1:200 dilution) in labeling buffer (1% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBT), 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rat IgG (1:500 dilution) in labeling buffer for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBT, 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  

2 Whole-mount labeling with functional vascular markers  
2.1 Incubation with 10 μg/mL Lectin-Alexa Fluor 647 and 10 μg/mL IB4-Alexa Fluor 594 in PBS for 24 hours to label perfused vessels. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Wash with PBT, 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Delipidation  
4.1 Incubation with freshly prepared dichloromethane (DCM)/methanol (2:1 vol/vol) for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.2 Replace with fresh DCM/methanol (2:1) and incubate for another 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

5 Rehydration  
5.1 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.4 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.5 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.6 Incubation with PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

6 Tissue Clearing  
6.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (200 mM dibasic sodium phosphate, 15% (w/v) N-butyldiethanolamine, 40% (vol/vol) sorbitol, pH 8.5) for 24–48 hours until fully transparent. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 24–48 hours)  

7 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
7.1 Incubation with RI matching solution (benzyl alcohol:benzyl benzoate, 1:2 vol/vol) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

8 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Transfer sample into a glass-bottom imaging dish or custom chamber.  
8.2 Add fresh RI matching solution to fully submerge the sample.  
8.3 Seal the chamber to prevent evaporation during long-term imaging.  

9 Optional Long-Term Storage  
9.1 Store in RI matching solution at 4 °C in the dark for up to several months without significant signal loss.

**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole-organ clearing of fixed mouse brains due to its excellent preservation of endogenous fluorescent proteins (like tdTomato/RFP), compatibility with immunolabeling, and rapid clearing speed. It is particularly suitable for 3D imaging of metastatic lesions using light-sheet or confocal microscopy. The use of E-cadherin as an epithelial tumor marker ensures specific identification of breast cancer cells, distinguishing them from background fluorescence. Alexa Fluor 647 is a bright, photostable fluorophore compatible with iDISCO+ clearing and RI matching.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 5% (wt/vol) BSA, 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: Rabbit anti-E-cadherin (1:500 dilution in labeling buffer: 1% DMSO, 3% BSA, 0.2% Tween-20 in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBST), 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:1000 in labeling buffer) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBST, 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1:20 dilution of 30% H₂O₂ in methanol) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 1:1 DCM:DBE for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) for 3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  

4 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) DBE in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE for final RI matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

5 Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Mount the cleared brain in a custom imaging chamber or glass cuvette filled with DBE.  
5.2 Image using light-sheet fluorescence microscopy or high-penetration confocal microscopy.  
5.3 Acquire z-stacks and tile scans to cover the entire brain volume.  
5.4 Use 3D reconstruction software (e.g., Imaris, Fiji) to visualize and quantify metastatic lesions (tdTomato/RFP+ and E-cadherin+), including their 3D location, volume, boundary morphology, and invasion patterns.  

6 Storage (Optional)  
6.1 Store cleared and RI-matched samples in 100% DBE at RT in the dark for up to several months without significant signal loss.

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [tdTomato/RFP, E-cadherin+Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole-organ clearing of fixed tissues, especially for preserving endogenous fluorescent proteins like tdTomato/RFP with high fidelity. It is fast, scalable, and compatible with immunolabeling. The methanol/BABB-based delipidation is effective for mouse brain tissue and allows for deep penetration of antibodies. E-cadherin is a specific epithelial marker for tumor cells and can be used to confirm tumor identity in combination with the tdTomato signal. Alexa Fluor 647 is a far-red fluorophore that is compatible with iDISCO+ clearing and multiplexed imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Rehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.5 Incubation with PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Whole-mount Immunolabeling  
2.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization solution (0.3% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 5% donkey serum in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody: E-cadherin (1:200 dilution) in labeling buffer (0.3% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 1% donkey serum in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
2.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% Tween-20 (PBST), 6 times for 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500 dilution) in labeling buffer for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
2.5 Wash with PBST, 6 times for 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Delipidation  
4.1 Incubation with freshly prepared dichloromethane (DCM)/methanol (2:1 vol/vol) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Replace with fresh DCM/methanol (2:1) and incubate overnight. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with 100% dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Replace with fresh DCM and incubate for 1–2 hours until tissue becomes visibly transparent. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
5.1 Incubation with dibenzyl ether (DBE) for RI matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
5.2 Replace with fresh DBE and incubate until full optical clarity is achieved. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

6 Imaging and Storage  
6.1 Mount the cleared brain in a custom chamber filled with DBE.  
6.2 Image using light-sheet or confocal microscopy with appropriate filters for tdTomato (Ex: 554 nm, Em: 581 nm) and Alexa Fluor 647 (Ex: 644 nm, Em: 669 nm).  
6.3 Store sample in DBE at RT in the dark if long-term preservation is needed.

2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-E-cadherin (1:500), anti-CD31 (1:200) in blocking solution for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)

1.6 Incubation with 66% DCM (Dichloromethane) + 33% MeOH for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CGRP-Alexa Fluor 488, TH-Alexa Fluor 594, DAPI, CD31-Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for mineralized tissues like bone, effectively combining decalcification, delipidation, and refractive index (RI) matching in a single workflow. It enables deep penetration and 3D visualization of complex bone structures while preserving fluorescence from immunolabeled markers such as CGRP and TH. The selected labeling strategy allows for multiplexed visualization of sensory (CGRP+), sympathetic (TH+), vascular (CD31+), and nuclear (DAPI) structures with minimal spectral overlap, fulfilling the goal of comparing their 3D spatial organization in bone microenvironments.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling Completion and Washing  
1.1 Wash sample in PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100 (PBST) for 1 hour at RT to remove residual fixatives. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Continue washing with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100) with 3–5 changes over 12–24 hours at 4 °C. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12–24 hours)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubate sample in 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Increase methanol concentration stepwise: 40%, 60%, 80%, and 100%, each for 1 hour at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubate sample in 100% methanol for 2–4 hours at RT to complete dehydration. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
3.2 Transfer sample to freshly prepared delipidation solution (methanol:benzyl ether = 1:2, v/v) and incubate at 37 °C for 24–48 hours. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 48 hours)  

4 Decalcification (Integrated with Delipidation)  
4.1 Include 5% EDTA in methanol-based delipidation solution to promote gradual decalcification without compromising tissue integrity. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 48 hours)  

5 Rehydration  
5.1 Rehydrate sample in reverse methanol gradient: 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% methanol in PBS, each for 1 hour at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)  
5.2 Final rinse in PBS for 1 hour at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

6 Tissue Clearing  
6.1 Incubate sample in BoneClear solution (80% glycerol, 20% PBS, 5% urea, 0.1% Tween-20, RI ~1.47) at 37 °C for 24–48 hours. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 48 hours)  

7 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
7.1 Transfer sample to RI matching solution (90% glycerol in PBS, RI ~1.47) and incubate at RT for 12–24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
7.2 Optional: Use 100% glycerol for long-term storage and optimal clearing (RI ~1.47). (Temperature: RT, Time: >24 hours)  

8 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Mount sample in a glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber using 1% low-melting agarose in PBS to prevent movement during imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour to solidify)  
8.2 Seal chamber edges with vacuum grease to prevent evaporation during long-term imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)  

9 Imaging  
9.1 Acquire 3D images using light-sheet microscopy or high-penetration confocal microscopy.  
9.2 Use 488 nm (CGRP), 594 nm (TH), 647 nm (CD31), and 405 nm (DAPI) excitation lasers for multichannel imaging.

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CGRP-Alexa Fluor 488, β-III Tubulin-Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI, CD31-Alexa Fluor 594]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for dense, calcified tissues like bone, enabling deep optical clearing while preserving fluorescence of both endogenous and antibody-labeled fluorophores. It effectively decalcifies and clears bone without destroying fine neural structures. The labeling strategy uses CGRP for specific labeling of sensory fibers, β-III Tubulin for pan-neuronal labeling, DAPI for nuclear counterstain, and CD31 for vascular reference. These markers allow for 3D mapping of CGRP+ fibers within the overall neural network and their spatial relationship to vasculature and bone subcompartments.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling (if not already labeled)
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-CGRP (1:500), anti-β-III Tubulin (1:1000), anti-CD31 (1:200) in labeling buffer (1% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% Tween-20 (PBST) for 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit, Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse, Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-rat in labeling buffer for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBST for 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
1.6 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 in PBS) for 12 hours for nuclear labeling. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  

2 Decalcification  
2.1 Incubation with 10% EDTA in PBS (pH 7.4) for 5 days with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 days)  
2.2 Replace solution daily. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 h per day)  

3 Delipidation and Clearing  
3.1 Incubation with BoneClear Solution A (urea, glycerol, Triton X-100-based decolorizing solution) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with BoneClear Solution B (urea, glycerol, Triton X-100, and clearing enhancer) for 48 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  

4 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
4.1 Incubation with BoneClear Solution C (final RI matching solution, RI ~1.46) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Transfer sample to a glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber.  
5.2 Add fresh BoneClear Solution C to submerge the sample.  
5.3 Seal the chamber to prevent evaporation during imaging.  

6 Imaging  
6.1 Acquire images using a light-sheet fluorescence microscope or high-penetration confocal microscope.  
6.2 Use 488 nm laser for CGRP-Alexa Fluor 488, 594 nm for CD31-Alexa Fluor 594, 647 nm for β-III Tubulin-Alexa Fluor 647, and 405 nm for DAPI.

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CGRP-Alexa Fluor 488, TH-Alexa Fluor 594, IB4-Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for hard tissues like long bones, enabling deep optical clearing while preserving fluorescence and antigenicity. It balances lipid removal and refractive index (RI) matching for high-resolution 3D imaging of complex structures such as mineralized bone, marrow, and embedded neural and vascular networks. The selected labeling strategy allows for simultaneous visualization of CGRP+ sensory fibers (Alexa Fluor 488), TH+ sympathetic fibers (Alexa Fluor 594), IB4-labeled vasculature (Alexa Fluor 647), and nuclear counterstain (DAPI), fulfilling the goal of mapping 3D spatial relationships between nerves, vasculature, and tumor regions in the bone.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling Completion  
1.1 Incubate sample in blocking solution (10% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubate with primary antibodies: anti-CGRP (1:500) and anti-TH (1:1000) in labeling buffer (1% NGS, 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash 3× with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  
1.4 Incubate with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit and Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-mouse at 1:1000 dilution, along with IB4-Alexa Fluor 647 (1:200) and DAPI (1:10,000) in labeling buffer for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.5 Wash 3× with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubate in 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubate in 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubate in 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubate in 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubate in 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubate in 1:2 mixture of methanol:dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubate in 100% DCM for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubate in 1:1 mixture of DCM:BoneClear Solution A for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Tissue Clearing  
4.1 Incubate in BoneClear Solution A (80% glycerol, 5% urea, 15% deionized water, RI ~1.45) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubate in BoneClear Solution B (85% glycerol, 5% urea, 10% deionized water, RI ~1.47) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.3 Incubate in BoneClear Solution C (90% glycerol, 5% urea, 5% deionized water, RI ~1.49) for 48 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
5.1 Incubate in BoneClear Solution D (95% glycerol, 5% deionized water, RI ~1.51) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubate in BoneClear Solution E (98% glycerol, 2% deionized water, RI ~1.52) for 24–48 hours until fully transparent. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24–48 hours)  

6 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Transfer sample into a glass-bottom imaging dish or custom chamber filled with BoneClear Solution E.  
6.2 Seal the chamber to prevent evaporation and maintain RI stability during imaging.  
6.3 Proceed with light-sheet or high-magnification confocal imaging for 3D reconstruction and spatial analysis.

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CGRP+Alexa Fluor 488, TH+Alexa Fluor 594, DAPI]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically designed for mineralized tissues like long bones, and includes a controlled EDTA-based decalcification step that preserves antigenicity and enables deep antibody penetration. This is critical for imaging CGRP+ sensory and TH+ sympathetic nerve fibers within the marrow cavity and cortical bone. The method is compatible with immunofluorescence labeling and maintains structural integrity of the bone marrow and neural architecture. Alexa Fluor 488 and 594 are bright, photostable fluorophores suitable for 3D imaging, and DAPI labels nuclei for anatomical orientation and cellularity assessment.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) ethanol in PBS (pH 7.4) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) ethanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) ethanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethanol for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Decalcification  
3.1 Incubation with 0.5 M EDTA (pH 8.0) in PBS for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours, gentle shaking)  
3.2 Replace EDTA solution and incubate for an additional 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  

4 Immunolabeling  
4.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 10% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-CGRP (1:500) and anti-TH (1:1000) in labeling buffer (1% serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
4.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100 (3 × 2 hours). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
4.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit and Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-mouse (1:1000) + DAPI (1:10,000) in labeling buffer for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
4.5 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100 (5 × 2 hours). (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 hours total)  

5 Tissue Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with BoneClear Solution I (20% (wt/vol) urea, 25% (vol/vol) glycerol, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with BoneClear Solution II (40% (wt/vol) urea, 50% (vol/vol) glycerol, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) for 48 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
5.3 Incubation with BoneClear Solution III (60% (wt/vol) urea, 80% (vol/vol) glycerol, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 72 hours)  

6 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
6.1 Incubation with RI matching solution (80% (vol/vol) glycerol, 20% (vol/vol) PBS, pH 7.4) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Transfer to 100% (vol/vol) glycerol and incubate for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Mounting and Imaging  
7.1 Mount sample in 100% glycerol in a custom imaging chamber with spacers to avoid compression.  
7.2 Image using light-sheet or confocal microscopy with appropriate filter sets for Alexa Fluor 488, Alexa Fluor 594, and DAPI.  
7.3 Store samples in 100% glycerol at 4 °C in the dark if long-term preservation is required.

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [tdTomato, Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-Sox10]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for small whole embryos or dissected embryonic organs like the E9.5–E10.5 mouse trunk due to its rapid clearing, excellent preservation of fluorescent proteins (including tdTomato), and compatibility with immunolabeling. It is particularly suitable for 3D imaging of migrating neural crest cells and their spatial relationships. The use of tdTomato allows direct visualization of neural crest-derived cells, while anti-Sox10 labels glial and neural crest lineage cells, enabling differentiation of migration paths and early differentiation states. The methanol-based protocol is compatible with endogenous fluorescence and antibody penetration in small tissues.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Pretreatment  
1.1 Incubation with methanol series (20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100%) for dehydration. Each step: 1 hour at RT.  
1.2 Incubation with chilled 5% H₂O₂ in methanol for endogenous peroxidase inactivation. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
1.3 Rehydration with methanol series (80%, 60%, 40%, 20%) for 1 hour each at RT.  

2 Whole-mount Immunolabeling  
2.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization solution (0.2% gelatin, 0.5% Triton X-100, 15% DMSO in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody: rabbit anti-Sox10 (1:500 dilution) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
2.3 Wash with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) ×5, 1 hour each at RT.  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:1000 dilution) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
2.5 Wash with PBST ×5, 1 hour each at RT.  

3 Tissue Optical Clearing  
3.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ R0 solution (20% DMSO, 20% N,N-dimethylacetamide in PBS) for 6 hours. (Temperature: RT)  
3.2 Incubation with iDISCO+ R1 solution (50% DMSO, 50% N,N-dimethylacetamide in PBS) for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT)  
3.3 Incubation with iDISCO+ R2 solution (80% DMSO, 20% N,N-dimethylacetamide in PBS) for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT)  
3.4 Incubation with iDISCO+ R3 solution (100% DMSO) for 6 hours. (Temperature: RT)  

4 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
4.1 Incubation with dibenzyl ether (DBE) for RI matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
4.2 Replace with fresh DBE and incubate until tissue becomes fully transparent. (Time: 3–6 hours)  

5 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Mount sample in DBE in a custom chamber or imaging cuvette suitable for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.  
5.2 Store in DBE at 4 °C in the dark if imaging is not immediate.  
5.3 Prior to imaging, ensure sample is fully submerged and free of bubbles.

**Protocol Steps:**
