1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated donkey anti-rabbit IgG (1:1000) in blocking solution for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)

2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% DCM for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) DCM in methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.4 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.5 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

7.1 Mount sample in a glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber using 100% BABB.  
7.2 Image using light-sheet or confocal microscopy with appropriate filters:

 - Alexa Fluor 647: excitation 650 nm, emission 668 nm

8.1 Store cleared sample in 100% BABB at 4 °C in the dark. (Time: up to several months)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [tdTomato, Sox10+Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for small embryonic tissues like mouse E9.5–E10.5 trunk samples due to its rapid clearing, excellent preservation of fluorescent proteins (e.g., tdTomato), and compatibility with immunolabeling. It allows high-resolution 3D imaging via light-sheet microscopy. tdTomato provides robust lineage tracing of neural crest cells, while Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated Sox10 antibody labels migrating and differentiating neural crest-derived cells. DAPI serves as a nuclear counterstain for tissue registration and cell density mapping without interfering with the fluorescent reporter or immunolabeling.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling (if not already performed)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: rabbit anti-Sox10 (1:500 dilution in blocking solution) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBST), 6× 2 hours each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated donkey anti-rabbit IgG (1:500 dilution in PBST) for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBST, 6× 2 hours each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours total)

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.6 Incubation with chilled 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 1 hour)

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (freshly prepared) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with fresh methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Repeat step 3.2 once. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

5 Nuclear Counterstaining  
5.1 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 dilution in PBS) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
5.2 Wash with PBS, 3× 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)

6 Tissue Clearing  
6.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Incubation with 100% DCM for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.3 Incubation with 100% dibenzyl ether (DBE) for refractive index (RI) matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)

7 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Transfer sample into a glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber.  
7.2 Fill chamber with fresh DBE to submerge the sample.  
7.3 Seal chamber to prevent evaporation and proceed to light-sheet or confocal imaging.  

8 Optional Long-Term Storage  
8.1 Store sample in DBE at 4 °C in the dark. (Time: up to several months)

Sox10 labeling with Alexa Fluor 647 is compatible with iDISCO+ and provides high signal-to-noise for identifying neural crest/glial lineage cells. This method supports 3D imaging of migration paths with minimal tissue deformation and low background.

**Protocol Steps:**

1.5 Wash with PBST (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 6 × 2 hours)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS (vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS (vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS (vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS (vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [IB4-Alexa Fluor 647, Collagen IV-Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole-organ clearing, especially for tissues like placenta that are moderately thick (3–4 mm) and rich in lipids and blood. It provides excellent lipid removal, good refractive index (RI) homogenization, and strong preservation of fluorescent signals. IB4 is a well-established marker for vascular endothelium and directly labels functional vascular lumens, making it ideal for visualizing the 3D vascular tree. Collagen IV labels basement membranes to define vessel boundaries and tissue architecture. DAPI is used for nuclear counterstaining to identify cellular layers at the maternal-fetal interface. This combination enables high-resolution 3D mapping of vascular architecture, including branching, connectivity, and perfusion patterns.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Permeabilization and Blocking  
1.1 Incubation with freshly prepared iDISCO+ permeabilization solution (0.2% Triton X-100, 0.3 M glycine, 1% BSA, 0.06% Tween-20 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Wash with iDISCO+ washing solution (1% BSA, 0.06% Tween-20 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 2 hours)

2.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: Collagen IV (1:200 dilution) and IB4-Alexa Fluor 647 (1:100 dilution) in iDISCO+ antibody solution (1% BSA, 0.06% Tween-20, 0.01% sodium azide in PBS) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
2.2 Wash with iDISCO+ washing solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 2 hours)  

3 Nuclear Staining  
3.1 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 dilution in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Wash with iDISCO+ washing solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 2 hours)  

4 Dehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

5 Delipidation  
5.1 Incubation with freshly prepared dichloromethane (DCM) and methanol (2:1 vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with fresh DCM:methanol (2:1) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with 100% DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

6 Rehydration  
6.1 Incubation with DCM:methanol (1:2 vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.4 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.5 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.6 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

7 Tissue Clearing  
7.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (benzyl alcohol:benzyl benzoate, 1:2 vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24–48 hours or until fully transparent)  

8 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
8.1 Incubation with RI matching solution (benzyl alcohol:benzyl benzoate, 1:1 vol/vol, RI ~1.56) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

9 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
9.1 Mount sample in custom chamber with RI matching solution to avoid mechanical compression  
9.2 Seal chamber with coverslip using silicone grease  
9.3 Store at 4 °C in dark until imaging  

10 Imaging  
10.1 Acquire 3D images using light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) or high-penetration confocal microscopy  
10.2 Use 405 nm (DAPI), 488 nm (Collagen IV), and 647 nm (IB4) excitation lasers for multichannel imaging  
10.3 Perform z-stack acquisition with 2–5 μm step size depending on resolution needs

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [IB4-Alexa Fluor 647, CD31 (PECAM1) antibody + Alexa Fluor 555, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole-organ clearing such as mouse placenta due to its rapid delipidation, excellent preservation of endogenous and immunofluorescence signals, and compatibility with multiple labeling strategies. IB4-Alexa Fluor 647 is a perfusion-compatible lectin that labels functional vascular lumens, while CD31 labels endothelial structure. DAPI is used for nuclear counterstain. This combination enables precise distinction between structural (CD31+) and functional (IB4+) vasculature across the placental labyrinth, maternal-fetal interface, and edge regions.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling (if not pre-labeled)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization solution (0.3% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 5% donkey serum in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: rat anti-CD31 (PECAM1), 1:200 dilution in labeling buffer (0.3% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO in PBS) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100 (6 × 2 hours) (Temperature: RT)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 555-conjugated anti-rat IgG, 1:500 dilution in labeling buffer (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100 (6 × 2 hours) (Temperature: RT)  

2 Perfusion Labeling (for functional vasculature)  
2.1 Retrograde perfusion via uterine artery with IB4-Alexa Fluor 647 (1:100 dilution in PBS) under low pressure (10–20 mmHg) to label luminal surface of functional vessels (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
2.2 Post-fixation with 4% PFA in PBS for 2 hours to preserve IB4 labeling (Temperature: RT)  
2.3 Wash with PBS (3 × 1 hour) (Temperature: RT)  

3 Nuclear Counterstaining  
3.1 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 dilution in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.2 Wash with PBS (3 × 1 hour) (Temperature: RT)  

4 Dehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS (vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS (vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS (vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS (vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (3 × 1 hour) (Temperature: RT)  

5 Delipidation  
5.1 Incubation with freshly prepared methanol/chloroform (2:1 vol/vol) solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% chloroform (3 × 1 hour) (Temperature: RT)  

6 Rehydration  
6.1 Incubation with methanol/chloroform (1:1 vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Incubation with methanol (3 × 1 hour) (Temperature: RT)  
6.3 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS (vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.4 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS (vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.5 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS (vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.6 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS (vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.7 Incubation with PBS (3 × 1 hour) (Temperature: RT)  

7 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
7.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (DBE/Toluene, 1:2 vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
7.2 Incubation with 100% DBE (Dibenzyl Ether) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

8 Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Mount sample in 100% DBE in an imaging chamber suitable for light-sheet or high-magnification confocal imaging  
8.2 Store in dark at RT if imaging is not immediate (up to 2 weeks without significant signal loss)

1 Immunolabeling  
1.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization solution (10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)

1.3 Wash with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (6 × 1 hour). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rat IgG at 1:500 dilution (if CD31 is rat-derived) in labeling solution for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.5 Wash with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (6 × 1 hour). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 dilution in PBS) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)

2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

6.3 For long-term storage, keep sample in 100% DBE at RT in the dark.

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (MAP2), 4G8-Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for 1–2 mm thick fixed tissue blocks due to its rapid clearing speed, excellent preservation of fluorescent proteins (e.g., GFP), and compatibility with immunolabeling. It allows high-resolution 3D imaging with light-sheet or confocal microscopy. The labeling strategy uses MAP2-GFP to label dendritic morphology, 4G8 (anti-PSD95) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 for excitatory postsynaptic scaffolds, and DAPI for nuclear counterstain, enabling layer-specific analysis in CA1. This combination ensures structural preservation of spines and puncta while providing molecular identity to synapses.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Permeabilization and Blocking  
1.1 Incubation with freshly prepared permeabilization solution (0.3% Triton X-100, 15% DMSO in PBS) at 37 °C for 24 hours. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) 3× 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with blocking solution (6% donkey serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Primary Antibody Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with primary antibody solution: 4G8 (anti-PSD95, 1:500) + anti-GFP (1:1000) in blocking solution for 72 hours. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
2.2 Wash with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) 5× 2 hours each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 2 hours)  

3 Secondary Antibody Labeling  
3.1 Incubation with secondary antibody solution: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:1000) + Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:1000) + DAPI (1:10,000) in blocking solution for 72 hours. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
3.2 Wash with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) 5× 2 hours each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 2 hours)  

4 Dehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour (×2 changes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

5 Delipidation  
5.1 Incubation with freshly prepared dichloromethane (DCM)/methanol (2:1 vol/vol) for 3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% DCM for 1 hour (×2 changes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

6 Tissue Clearing  
6.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (benzyl alcohol:benzyl benzoate, 1:2 vol/vol) for 3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with fresh iDISCO+ solution for 12–24 hours until fully transparent. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12–24 hours)  

7 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
7.1 Incubation with RI matching solution (iDISCO+ with 0.5% N-phenylglycine) for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

8 Mounting and Imaging  
8.1 Mount sample in a custom chamber filled with iDISCO+ clearing solution.  
8.2 Image using light-sheet or high-penetration confocal microscopy (e.g., 25× water-dipping objective, 1.0 NA).  
8.3 Acquire z-stacks with appropriate excitation/emission filters: 488 nm (GFP), 647 nm (PSD95), and 405 nm (DAPI).

**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP, mCherry, DAPI, MAP2]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for small to medium-sized fixed tissue blocks (1–2 mm), offers excellent fluorescence preservation, and achieves high transparency with relatively fast processing times. It is compatible with a wide range of fluorophores including GFP and mCherry, which are suitable for labeling two different synaptic scaffold proteins. MAP2 is used to label dendritic structures for spatial orientation, and DAPI serves as a nuclear counterstain for anatomical reference. This combination enables high-resolution 3D imaging of synaptic puncta across CA1 sublayers with clear dendritic morphology.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preprocessing  
1.1 Wash fixed mouse hippocampal tissue blocks (1–2 mm thickness) in PBS (pH 7.4) for 1 hour at RT to remove residual fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubate tissue in methanol (MeOH) at RT for 1 hour, gradually increasing MeOH concentration to 60% over 3 days at 4 °C. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 3 days)

2 Whole-mount Immunolabeling  
2.1 Incubate tissue in blocking/permeabilization solution (0.2% gelatin, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours at 4 °C. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubate with primary antibodies: anti-Homer1 (raised in mouse, 1:500) and anti-PSD95 (raised in rabbit, 1:1000) in blocking solution for 5 days at 4 °C. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 5 days)  
2.3 Wash tissue in PBS with 0.1% Tween-20 (PBST) 5 times over 24 hours at 4 °C. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
2.4 Incubate with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse and Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-rabbit (1:1000 each) along with DAPI (1:10,000) and MAP2 antibody (1:1000, raised in chicken) for 5 days at 4 °C. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 5 days)  
2.5 Wash tissue in PBST 5 times over 24 hours at 4 °C. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubate tissue in 20% MeOH in PBS for 1 hour at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubate in 40% MeOH in PBS for 1 hour at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubate in 60% MeOH in PBS for 1 hour at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubate in 80% MeOH in PBS for 1 hour at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubate in 100% MeOH twice for 1 hour each at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)

4 Delipidation  
4.1 Incubate tissue in freshly prepared iDISCO+ clearing solution (200 mM dibasic sodium phosphate, 30% w/v sucrose, 60% vol/vol DMSO, 30% vol/vol MeOH) at 37 °C for 3–5 days depending on tissue transparency. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 3–5 days)

5 Rehydration  
5.1 Incubate in 80% MeOH in PBS for 1 hour at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubate in 60% MeOH in PBS for 1 hour at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubate in 40% MeOH in PBS for 1 hour at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.4 Incubate in 20% MeOH in PBS for 1 hour at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.5 Incubate in PBS for 1 hour at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

6 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
6.1 Incubate tissue in iDISCO mounting solution (benzyl alcohol:benzyl benzoate, 1:2 vol/vol) for 1–2 days at RT in the dark. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1–2 days)

7 Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Mount tissue in a chamber filled with RI-matching solution and secure with low-melting agarose to prevent movement.  
7.2 Store samples in the dark at RT until imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: up to 2 weeks)  
7.3 Image using light-sheet or confocal microscopy with appropriate filter sets for Alexa Fluor 488, Alexa Fluor 594, DAPI, and MAP2.

Triple labeling with Alexa Fluor dyes ensures clear distinction between PSD95, Homer1, and MAP2, enabling precise spatial mapping of excitatory synapses along dendrites while preserving neuronal morphology for accurate spine and puncta detection.

**Protocol Steps:**

1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 (5 × 1 hour) (Temperature: RT)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse, Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-rabbit, Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-chicken (1:500 each) in labeling buffer (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 (5 × 1 hour) (Temperature: RT)

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS (v/v) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS (v/v) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS (v/v) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS (v/v) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (3 × 1 hour) (Temperature: RT)

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 66% dichloromethane (DCM), 33% methanol (v/v) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Replace with fresh DCM/methanol solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with 100% DCM (2 × 1 hour) (Temperature: RT)

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 66% methanol in PBS (v/v) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS (v/v) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS (v/v) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with PBS (3 × 1 hour) (Temperature: RT)

6.1 Mount tissue in 100% glycerol in a glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber

**Chosen Method:** SeeDB2  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP, tdTomato, Synapsin, MAP2, DAPI]  
**Justification:** SeeDB2 is an aqueous-based optical clearing method that preserves fluorescence (including GFP and tdTomato), minimizes tissue deformation, and achieves excellent refractive index (RI) homogenization, making it ideal for high-resolution 3D imaging of 1–2 mm thick brain tissues. It is particularly suitable for preserving synaptic puncta, dendritic morphology, and layered tissue architecture. The labeling strategy uses GFP and tdTomato for genetically labeled neurons, Synapsin to label presynaptic terminals, MAP2 for dendrites, and DAPI for nuclear counterstain, all of which are compatible with SeeDB2.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling Completion and Washing  
1.1 Wash tissue blocks 3× in PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  
1.2 Incubate with secondary antibodies (e.g., Alexa Fluor 488 anti-rabbit, Alexa Fluor 594 anti-mouse) diluted 1:500 in PBST with 5% normal goat serum for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.3 Wash tissue blocks 5× in PBST (0.3% Triton X-100) for 2 hours each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 hours total)  

2 Dehydration in Ethanol Series  
2.1 Incubate in 50% ethanol (in PBS) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubate in 70% ethanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubate in 90% ethanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubate in 100% ethanol for 1 hour (×2 changes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)  

3 Clearing with Fructose-Based Solution  
3.1 Incubate in 20% fructose in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.2 Incubate in 40% fructose in PBS for 6 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
3.3 Incubate in 60% fructose in PBS overnight (~12 hours). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  

4 Final Clearing and RI Matching  
4.1 Incubate in SeeDB2 solution (58.8% w/w sucrose, 27.8% w/w D-sorbitol, 13.4% w/w glycerol in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Replace with fresh SeeDB2 solution and incubate for another 24–48 hours until full optical transparency is achieved. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  

5 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Mount tissue in a chambered coverslip or imaging chamber using SeeDB2 as the mounting medium.  
5.2 Seal the chamber with vacuum grease or nail polish and store at 4 °C until imaging. (Time: Immediate imaging recommended within 7 days)  
5.3 Perform high-resolution 3D imaging using a cleared-tissue-optimized confocal or light-sheet microscope with RI-matched objectives (e.g., water or glycerol immersion).

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Cx40, Hcn4, Phalloidin, CD31, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole-organ clearing such as the intact mouse heart due to its excellent preservation of fluorescent proteins and antigenicity, rapid clearing speed, and compatibility with multiple antibody labeling. It is particularly suitable for dense, vascularized tissues like the heart. The methanol-based delipidation effectively clears lipids while maintaining structural integrity and molecular signals. The selected labeling strategy targets key components of the cardiac conduction system: Cx40 and Hcn4 for identification of conduction system cells (e.g., SA node, AV node, Purkinje fibers), CD31 for vascular architecture, Phalloidin for F-actin to preserve and visualize myofiber orientation, and DAPI for nuclear counterstain. This combination enables 3D mapping of the conduction system in the context of myocardial architecture.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling (if not already performed)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 5% (wt/vol) BSA, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Cx40 (1:500), anti-Hcn4 (1:300), anti-CD31 (1:200) in labeling buffer (1% BSA, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBST), 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488 anti-rabbit, Alexa Fluor 647 anti-goat, Alexa Fluor 555 anti-rat (all 1:500) in labeling buffer for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBST, 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
1.6 Incubation with Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 633 (1:200) and DAPI (1:1000) in PBST for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.7 Wash with PBST, 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.6 Incubation with chilled 100% methanol for 2 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Bleaching  
3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H2O2 in methanol (1 volume 30% H2O2 to 5 volumes MeOH). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Wash with 100% methanol, 3 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

4 Delipidation  
4.1 Incubation with freshly prepared dichloromethane (DCM) for 4 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with DCM containing 0.3% (vol/vol) TWEEN 20 for 4 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
4.3 Repeat step 4.1 and 4.2 for 2–3 cycles until tissue becomes translucent. (Temperature: RT, Time: 8–12 hours total)  

5 Rehydration  
5.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) DCM in methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.4 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.5 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.6 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.7 Incubation with PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

6 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
6.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ RI matching solution (BABB: benzyl alcohol/benzyl benzoate = 1:2 vol/vol) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Replace with fresh BABB and incubate for another 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Store sample in BABB at 4 °C in the dark until imaging. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: up to several weeks)  
7.2 Prior to imaging, mount sample in a custom chamber filled with BABB to match RI and minimize spherical aberration. (Temperature: RT)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Cx40, Hcn4, α-Actinin, Phalloidin, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole-organ clearing such as the mouse heart due to its rapid delipidation, excellent preservation of fluorescent proteins and antigenicity, and compatibility with multiple immunolabeling rounds. It allows deep penetration and high-resolution 3D imaging of large structures like the cardiac conduction system. The labeling strategy targets Cx40 and Hcn4 for specific identification of pacemaking and conduction system cells (including SA and AV nodes), α-Actinin and Phalloidin for cardiomyocyte structure and fiber orientation, and DAPI for nuclear counterstaining. This combination enables precise spatial mapping of conduction system architecture and its relationship with myocardial fiber alignment.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Permeabilization and Delipidation  
1.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 20% (vol/vol) DMSO in methanol at 4 °C for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS-T (0.2% Tween-20) at 4 °C for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with 100% methanol at 4 °C for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with chilled methanol:hydrogen peroxide solution (5:1 ratio) at 4 °C for 6 hours to block autofluorescence. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 6 hours)  

2 Whole-mount Immunolabeling  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% DMSO, 5% donkey serum, 0.2% Tween-20 in PBS) at 4 °C for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Cx40 (1:500), anti-Hcn4 (1:200), anti-α-Actinin (1:1000) in labeling buffer (3% DMSO, 0.2% Tween-20 in PBS) at 4 °C for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
2.3 Wash with PBS-T (0.2% Tween-20) 6 times over 24 hours at 4 °C. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488 anti-rabbit (anti-Cx40), Alexa Fluor 555 anti-mouse (anti-Hcn4), Alexa Fluor 647 anti-mouse (anti-α-Actinin) at 1:1000 dilution in labeling buffer at 4 °C for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
2.5 Wash with PBS-T (0.2% Tween-20) 6 times over 24 hours at 4 °C. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  

3 F-actin Staining and Nuclear Counterstaining  
3.1 Incubation with Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 405 (1:200) and DAPI (1:1000) in PBS-T for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Wash with PBS-T (0.2% Tween-20) 6 times over 24 hours at 4 °C. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  

4 Delipidation and Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with freshly prepared dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour to remove lipids. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with DCM containing 0.001% (vol/vol) BHT to prevent fluorophore bleaching for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with 1:1 DCM:BABB (benzyl alcohol:benzyl benzoate, 1:1 vol/vol) for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.4 Incubation with 100% BABB for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching and Mounting  
5.1 Incubation with dibutyl phthalate (DBP, RI ~1.52) for final RI matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Mount sample in DBP-filled imaging chamber with gentle agitation to avoid air bubbles.  

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Image using light-sheet fluorescence microscopy or high-magnification confocal microscopy with multi-channel detection.  
6.2 Use 10× or 20× immersion objective with DBP-compatible clearing chamber for 3D reconstruction of conduction system architecture and fiber orientation.

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [HCN4, Cntn2, Cx40, Phalloidin, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole-organ clearing such as the mouse heart due to its excellent preservation of fluorescent proteins and compatibility with immunolabeling. It enables deep penetration and high-resolution imaging of large tissues using light-sheet or confocal microscopy. The methanol-based delipidation is fast and effective, and the RI matching with DBE allows for high-resolution 3D imaging. The labeling strategy targets key components of the cardiac conduction system (HCN4 for pacemaker cells, Cntn2 for Purkinje fibers, Cx40 for gap junctions in the conduction system), while Phalloidin labels F-actin to reveal myocardial fiber orientation, and DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for anatomical orientation.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling  
1.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization solution (0.3% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 5% donkey serum in PBS) at 4 °C for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-HCN4 (1:500), anti-Cntn2 (1:1000), anti-Cx40 (1:200) in labeling buffer (0.3% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 1% donkey serum in PBS) at 4 °C for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100 (PBT), 6 × 1 hour at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488 anti-rabbit (for HCN4), Alexa Fluor 594 anti-mouse (for Cx40), Alexa Fluor 647 anti-chicken (for Cntn2), all at 1:1000 in labeling buffer at 4 °C for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBT, 6 × 1 hour at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488 (1:200) and DAPI (1:1000) in PBT for 24 hours at 4 °C. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.7 Final wash with PBT, 6 × 1 hour at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 1 hour)

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol, 2 × 1 hour at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 5% H₂O₂ in methanol (1:20 dilution of 30% H₂O₂ in methanol) at 4 °C for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% dichloromethane (DCM) for 2 hours at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with 1:1 DCM:DBE for 2 hours at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.4 Incubation with 100% dibenzyl ether (DBE) for 3 hours at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)

4 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
4.1 Incubation with fresh 100% DBE for RI matching and clearing at RT for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Replace with fresh DBE and incubate for an additional 24 hours if needed for full transparency. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

5 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Transfer the cleared heart into a glass-bottom imaging dish using forceps or a spatula.  
5.2 Submerge the sample in 100% DBE to maintain RI matching during imaging.  
5.3 Seal the dish with vacuum grease or imaging-compatible adhesive film to prevent evaporation.  
5.4 Store at 4 °C in the dark until imaging. For long-term storage, replace DBE with 100% glycerol and store at 4 °C.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling  
1.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization solution (10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 5% (wt/vol) BSA, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)

1.3 Wash with 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 in PBS (PBST) for 6 × 2 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse (1:1000) in labeling buffer for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBST for 6 × 2 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours total)  
1.6 Incubation with Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 555 (1:200) and DAPI (1:1000) in labeling buffer for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.7 Wash with PBST for 6 × 2 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours total)

2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 2 × 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours total)

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with freshly prepared dichloromethane (DCM) for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with DCM for an additional 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [HuC/D, β-III Tubulin, Phalloidin, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole-organ optical clearing of large, fixed tissues like the mouse colon. It provides excellent tissue transparency, good preservation of fluorescent signals, and compatibility with multiple immunolabeling steps. The methanol-based delipidation is fast and effective for lipid-rich tissues while maintaining structural integrity. HuC/D is a pan-neuronal marker that labels ENS neuronal cell bodies, β-III Tubulin labels all neuronal processes, Phalloidin highlights muscle layers (for structural orientation), and DAPI stains nuclei to aid in identifying ganglia and layer boundaries. This combination enables clear distinction between myenteric and submucosal plexuses, and supports quantitative analysis of ganglion size, density, and network connectivity.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling  
1.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization solution (10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-HuC/D (1:500) and anti-β-III Tubulin (1:1000) in labeling buffer (1% DMSO, 3% donkey serum, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBT), 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488 anti-mouse and Alexa Fluor 647 anti-rabbit (1:1000 each) + Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 594 (1:200) in labeling buffer for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBT, 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
1.6 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000) in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol, 2 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 5% (vol/vol) H2O2 in methanol (1:20 dilution of 30% H2O2 in methanol) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Wash with 100% methanol, 3 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

4 Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with 1:1 (vol/vol) methanol:dibenzyl ether (DBE) for 3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% DBE, 2 × 3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
4.3 Incubation with fresh 100% DBE for at least 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
5.1 Optional RI matching in DBE with refractive index ~1.56 for light-sheet or confocal imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: up to 24 hours)  

6 Storage/Imaging  
6.1 Store in 100% DBE at RT in the dark until imaging.  
6.2 Mount sample in DBE-filled chamber with gentle support to avoid mechanical distortion.  
6.3 Image using light-sheet fluorescence microscopy or high-penetration confocal microscopy.

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [HuC/D+Alexa Fluor 488, β-III Tubulin+Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI, Phalloidin 633]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole-organ clearing such as the mouse colon due to its excellent preservation of fluorescent proteins and compatibility with multiple antibody labeling. It is fast compared to aqueous-based methods and suitable for large tissues (up to ~10 cm), maintaining structural integrity including layered wall organization. The selected labeling strategy targets ENS neuronal cell bodies (HuC/D), pan-neuronal fibers (β-III Tubulin), nuclear counterstain (DAPI), and smooth muscle layers (Phalloidin), enabling precise mapping of ganglia, fiber tracts, and layer-specific distribution.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preparation  
1.1 Wash fixed mouse colon in PBS for 1 hour at RT to remove fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Perform permeabilization with methanol gradient: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% methanol in PBS (each step 1 hour at RT). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)  
1.3 Incubate tissue in chilled 5% H2O2 in methanol overnight at 4 °C to enhance antibody penetration. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Block tissue in iDISCO blocking solution (10% DMSO, 5% donkey serum, 0.2% Tween-20 in PBS) for 24 hours at 37 °C. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubate with primary antibodies: anti-HuC/D (1:500) and anti-β-III Tubulin (1:1000) in blocking solution for 5 days at 37 °C. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 5 days)  
2.3 Wash tissue in PBS with 0.2% Tween-20 (PTw) for 6 × 2 hours at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 6)  
2.4 Incubate with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit in blocking solution for 5 days at 37 °C. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 5 days)  
2.5 Wash tissue in PTw for 6 × 2 hours at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 6)  
2.6 Stain nuclei with DAPI (1:10,000 in PTw) for 2 hours at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.7 Wash tissue in PTw for 3 × 1 hour at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 3)  
2.8 Stain F-actin in muscle layers with Phalloidin 633 (1:200 in PTw) for 2 hours at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.9 Wash tissue in PTw for 3 × 1 hour at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 3)

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubate in methanol series: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% methanol in PTw (each step 1 hour at RT). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)

4 Delipidation  
4.1 Incubate in dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Replace with fresh DCM and incubate overnight at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.3 Repeat DCM incubation until tissue becomes translucent (typically 2–3 cycles). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours per cycle)

5 Rehydration  
5.1 Incubate in methanol series: 100%, 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% methanol in PTw (each step 1 hour at RT). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)

6 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
6.1 Incubate in iDISCO clearing solution (DBE with 1% Tween-20) for 3 hours at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
6.2 Replace with fresh DBE and incubate overnight at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
6.3 Replace with fresh DBE and incubate until fully cleared (typically 24–48 hours). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24–48 hours)

7 Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Mount tissue in custom chamber with DBE to maintain RI matching during imaging.  
7.2 Store cleared tissue in DBE at 4 °C in the dark if not imaging immediately. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: up to several weeks)

This combination enables precise mapping of ENS networks relative to intestinal wall layers.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling  
1.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization solution (0.3% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 5% donkey serum in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-HuC/D (1:500 dilution) in labeling solution (0.3% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100 (3 × 24 hours). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 3 × 24 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:1000) and Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 594 (1:200) in labeling solution for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100 (3 × 24 hours). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 3 × 24 hours)  
1.6 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)

2.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour (×2 changes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Nephrin (NPHS1)+Alexa Fluor 647, Podocin (NPHS2)+Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole-organ clearing, especially for immunolabeled samples, due to its excellent preservation of fluorescence and compatibility with multiple antibody labeling. It provides rapid delipidation and refractive index (RI) homogenization, which is critical for achieving uniform transparency across the heterogeneous kidney tissue (cortex, medulla, pelvis). The methanol-based protocol minimizes tissue swelling and maintains fine ultrastructural details such as foot process morphology and slit diaphragm integrity. The selected labeling strategy targets key slit diaphragm proteins (Nephrin and Podocin) for high-resolution visualization of the glomerular filtration barrier, while DAPI labels nuclei to aid in identifying glomerular boundaries and cellularity.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling (if not already performed)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization solution (0.3% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 5% donkey serum in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Nephrin (Alexa Fluor 647 conjugated) at 1:200 and anti-Podocin (Alexa Fluor 488 conjugated) at 1:200 in labeling buffer (0.3% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100 (6 × 12 hours). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 6 × 12 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 dilution in PBS) for 12 hours to label nuclei. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100 (3 × 12 hours). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 3 × 12 hours)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 2 hours (×2 changes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 2)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 66% dichloromethane (DCM), 33% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% DCM for 1 hour (×2 changes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 2)  

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 15 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
4.2 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 15 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
4.3 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 15 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 15 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
4.5 Incubation with PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100 for 30 minutes (×2 changes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes × 2)  

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
5.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ RI matching solution (DBE:Toluene = 1:1, v/v) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% dibenzyl ether (DBE) for 1 hour (×2 changes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 2)  

6 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Transfer the cleared kidney into a glass-bottom imaging dish.  
6.2 Cover the sample with 100% DBE to maintain RI matching and prevent drying during imaging.  
6.3 Proceed to light-sheet or high-magnification confocal imaging for 3D reconstruction of glomerular distribution and slit diaphragm integrity assessment.  

7 Storage (if needed)  
7.1 Store the sample in 100% DBE at 4 °C in the dark. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: up to several months)

2.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour (2×). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2× 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Nephrin (NPHS1)+Alexa Fluor 488, Podocin (NPHS2)+Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole-organ clearing such as kidneys due to its excellent lipid removal, preservation of endogenous and immunofluorescence signals, and compatibility with deep imaging. It allows for efficient antibody penetration even in large tissues like kidneys, which is critical for dual labeling of glomerular slit diaphragm proteins (Nephrin and Podocin). The methanol-based dehydration and BABB RI matching provide uniform transparency across cortex and medulla, reducing background and enhancing signal-to-noise ratio.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling (if not already performed)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization solution: 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: Nephrin (NPHS1) at 1:200 and Podocin (NPHS2) at 1:200 in labeling buffer (1% DMSO, 1% donkey serum, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 (3 × 24 hours at 4 °C)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse at 1:500 dilution in labeling buffer. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 (5 × 24 hours at 4 °C)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.6 Incubation with chilled 100% methanol. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 5% (vol/vol) H2O2 in methanol (1:20 dilution of 30% H2O2 in methanol). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% dichloromethane (DCM). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 1:1 dichloromethane:BABB (benzyl alcohol:benzyl benzoate, 1:1 vol/vol). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 100% BABB. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

4 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
4.1 Incubation with 100% BABB (RI ≈ 1.56). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24–48 hours until fully transparent)  

5 Imaging and Storage  
5.1 Mount kidney in custom chamber with BABB to maintain RI matching and prevent drying.  
5.2 Image using light-sheet or high-penetration confocal microscopy (e.g., 25× water-dipping objective).  
5.3 Store sample in 100% BABB at RT in the dark for long-term preservation.

The method enables high-resolution 3D imaging of the entire visual pathway, including retinal layers, LGN, and V1, while maintaining structural integrity.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Optical Clearing  
1.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (MeOH/PBS) for dehydration. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

2 Lipophilic Dye Labeling (if not previously performed)  
2.1 Apply DiI and DiD crystals to specific retinal regions to label distinct projection branches. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2–4 weeks, depending on diffusion distance)  
2.2 Rinse samples in 100% methanol to remove excess dye. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 15 minutes)

3.1 Incubation with freshly prepared iDISCO+ delipidation solution (200 mM CHAPS, 200 mM NaOH, 10% MeOH in PBS) under nitrogen gas to prevent oxidation. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48–72 hours, depending on tissue size)

4.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.6 Incubation with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)

5.2 Replace DBE once after 12 hours to ensure full clearing and optical homogeneity.

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [DiI, DiD]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole-tissue clearing of fixed neural tissues, offering excellent preservation of fluorescent signals (including lipophilic dyes like DiI and DiD), rapid delipidation, and compatibility with downstream light-sheet microscopy. The methanol-based protocol is particularly suitable for small to medium-sized brain regions like LGN and V1, and it allows for effective refractive index (RI) matching. Since the scientific goal is to distinguish two different visual pathway projections using retrograde or anterograde labeling, DiI and DiD are optimal choices due to their bright, spectrally distinct fluorescence and long-term stability in fixed tissue. These dyes do not require antibody amplification and are retained well through iDISCO+ clearing steps.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 **Labeling with Lipophilic Dyes (DiI and DiD)**  
1.1 Inject DiI (1,1'-dioctadecyl-3,3,3',3'-tetramethylindocarbocyanine perchlorate) into one eye to label one visual pathway branch (e.g., ipsilateral or contralateral retinal projections). (Temperature: RT, Time: Allow 7–10 days for dye transport at 4 °C post-injection)  
1.2 Inject DiD (1,1'-dioctadecyl-3,3,3',3'-tetramethylindodicarbocyanine, 4-chlorobenzenesulfonate salt) into the other eye to label the second visual pathway branch. (Temperature: RT, Time: Allow 7–10 days for dye transport at 4 °C post-injection)  
1.3 After transport, perfuse-fix the animal with 4% PFA in PBS. Post-fix the whole brain and eyes in 4% PFA for 24 hours at 4 °C.  

2 **Dehydration**  
2.1 Wash the tissue (retina, LGN, V1) in PBS for 1 hour at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubate in 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubate in 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubate in 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubate in 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.6 Incubate in 100% methanol for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 **Delipidation and Clearing**  
3.1 Incubate the tissue in freshly prepared 5% H₂O₂ in methanol (1:5 dilution of 30% H₂O₂ in methanol) at 4 °C for 12–16 hours to bleach autofluorescence. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12–16 hours)  
3.2 Wash in 100% methanol for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.3 Begin delipidation by incubating in 66% dichloromethane (DCM)/33% methanol solution for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Replace with fresh 66% DCM/33% methanol and incubate for another 1–2 hours until tissue becomes visibly transparent. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1–2 hours)  
3.5 Wash in 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 **Rehydration and Immunolabeling (Optional Structural Markers Only)**  
4.1 If needed, rehydrate the tissue through a methanol series: 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% methanol in PBS, each for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 0.5 hour per step)  
4.2 Incubate with nuclear stain (e.g., DAPI, 1:10,000 in PBS) for 12–24 hours at 4 °C for anatomical reference. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12–24 hours)  
4.3 Wash in PBS for 3 hours with several changes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

5 **Refractive Index (RI) Matching**  
5.1 Incubate the tissue in iDISCO+ RI matching solution (DBE/Toluene, 1:1 vol/vol) for 3 hours at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
5.2 Transfer to 100% dibenzyl ether (DBE) for final clearing and RI matching. Incubate without shaking for 6–12 hours or until fully cleared. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6–12 hours)  

6 **Imaging and Storage**  
6.1 Mount the tissue in DBE in a custom chamber suitable for light-sheet or high-magnification confocal imaging.  
6.2 Store samples in DBE at 4 °C in the dark for long-term preservation. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: indefinite)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [DiI, DiD, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole-mount immunolabeling and optical clearing of small to medium-sized tissues such as the retina, LGN, and V1. It provides excellent preservation of fluorescent signals (including lipophilic dyes like DiI/DiD), rapid clearing, and compatibility with 3D imaging using light-sheet or confocal microscopy. DAPI is used as a nuclear counterstain to aid in anatomical registration without interfering with the lipophilic tracers. The methanol-based dehydration and BABB-based refractive index (RI) matching ensure high tissue transparency and long-term sample stability.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Washing and Permeabilization  
1.1 Wash tissue in PBS containing 0.1% Tween-20 (PBST) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubate in PBST with 0.3% Triton X-100 for 2 hours to enhance permeabilization. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.3 Rinse 3 times in PBST for 30 minutes each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)

2 Lipophilic Dye Labeling (if not already performed)  
2.1 Apply DiI and DiD crystals or microinjections to designated regions for retrograde/antegrade labeling. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 7–14 days)  
2.2 Post-labeling, fix tissue in 4% PFA in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.3 Wash 3 times in PBS for 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)

3 Nuclear Staining  
3.1 Incubate tissue in 1 μg/mL DAPI in PBS for nuclear labeling. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Wash 3 times in PBS for 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)

4 Dehydration  
4.1 Incubate in 50% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Transfer to 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Replace with 100% methanol for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.4 Replace with fresh 100% methanol and incubate overnight. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

5 Delipidation and Clearing  
5.1 Incubate in a freshly prepared solution of 1 volume 30% H2O2 : 2 volumes methanol for 12 hours to enhance clearing. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
5.2 Wash in 100% methanol 3 times for 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  
5.3 Transfer tissue into dichloromethane (DCM) for 1–2 hours until visibly cleared. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1–2 hours)  
5.4 Rinse in 100% methanol for 1 hour to remove residual DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

6 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
6.1 Incubate in a 1:2 mixture of benzyl alcohol and benzyl benzoate (BABB) for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
6.2 Transfer to 100% BABB and incubate until fully transparent (typically 12–24 hours). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12–24 hours)

7 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Mount tissue in a custom chamber using 100% BABB to maintain RI matching.  
7.2 Seal chamber with coverslip using silicone grease or nail polish.  
7.3 Image using light-sheet or high-magnification confocal microscopy with appropriate filters for DiI (Ex: 549 nm, Em: 565 nm), DiD (Ex: 644 nm, Em: 665 nm), and DAPI (Ex: 358 nm, Em: 461 nm).

8 Storage (if needed)  
8.1 Store cleared tissue in 100% BABB at 4 °C in the dark. (Time: up to several months)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [DiI, DiD]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is a methanol-based clearing method that provides excellent preservation of lipophilic dye signals (e.g., DiI/DiD), minimal tissue deformation, and high transparency for deep 3D imaging. It is particularly suitable for small tissue blocks like retinal explants, LGN, and V1, where maintaining fine structural integrity and fluorescent signal is critical. The method avoids harsh detergents or high temperatures that can damage retinal lamination or quench lipophilic dyes. DiI and DiD are ideal for dual-color tracing of distinct visual pathways due to their stable fluorescence and compatibility with organic clearing solvents.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Washing and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100 (PBSTx) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Repeat incubation with fresh PBSTx (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Lipophilic Dye Labeling (if not already performed)  
2.1 Apply DiI and DiD crystals to designated retinal regions or axonal targets (e.g., V1 or LGN) using a fine tungsten needle (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 7 days)  
2.2 Incubate in PBSTx at 37 °C to allow dye diffusion along axons (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 14–21 days)  

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 50% methanol in PBS (vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS (vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

4 Delipidation and Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 66% dichloromethane (DCM) and 33% methanol (vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Replace with fresh DCM/methanol solution and incubate (Temperature: RT, Time: 1–2 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with 100% DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Replace with fresh 100% DCM and incubate until fully transparent (Temperature: RT, Time: 1–3 hours depending on tissue size)  

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
5.1 Incubation with 1:1 mixture of dibenzyl ether (DBE) and DCM (vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.3 Replace with fresh 100% DBE and incubate until tissue settles at the bottom of the vial (Temperature: RT, Time: 4–6 hours)  

6 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Transfer tissue into a glass-bottom imaging dish or custom chamber  
6.2 Fill chamber with 100% DBE to maintain RI matching during imaging  
6.3 Seal chamber with silicone grease or imaging-compatible adhesive to prevent evaporation  

7 Optional Long-Term Storage  
7.1 Store cleared tissue in 100% DBE at 4 °C in the dark (Time: up to several months without significant signal loss)  

**Imaging Recommendation:** Use light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) or two-photon confocal microscopy with appropriate excitation/emission filters for DiI (Ex ~549 nm, Em ~565 nm) and DiD (Ex ~644 nm, Em ~665 nm) to visualize 3D projections from retina to LGN to V1 while preserving retinal lamination.

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488, Myosin VIIa (primary antibody), DAPI]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically designed for optical clearing of calcified or mineralized tissues such as bone and is ideal for preserving fine structures within hard tissues like the mouse cochlea. It effectively decalcifies and clears the bony cochlear capsule without disrupting the spiral architecture or cellular structures. Phalloidin directly labels F-actin in stereocilia, providing high-resolution visualization of hair cell bundles. Myosin VIIa is a well-established marker for both inner and outer hair cells, ensuring accurate identification of all hair cell types. DAPI is used for nuclear counterstaining to assess cellular integrity and spatial organization. This combination ensures high-resolution 3D imaging of hair cell morphology and spatial distribution across cochlear turns.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling (if not already performed)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: Rabbit anti-Myosin VIIa (1:500 dilution in blocking solution) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS (5 × 1 hour). (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Goat anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 594 (1:1000 in blocking solution) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.5 Wash with 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS (5 × 1 hour). (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488 (1:100 in PBS) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
1.7 Wash with PBS (3 × 1 hour). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  
1.8 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 in PBS) for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.9 Wash with PBS (3 × 1 hour). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)

2 Decalcification  
2.1 Incubation with 10% EDTA in PBS (pH 7.4) for 48–72 hours (change solution every 24 hours). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48–72 hours)

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 2 hours (×2 changes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours ×2)

4 Delipidation  
4.1 Incubation with 100% dichloromethane (DCM) for 2 hours (×2 changes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours ×2)

5 Rehydration  
5.1 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.4 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.5 Incubation with PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

6 Tissue Clearing  
6.1 Incubation with BoneClear solution (8 M urea, 0.25% Iodixanol, 20% DMSO in PBS) for 24–48 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24–48 hours)

7 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
7.1 Incubation with RI matching solution (8 M urea, 50% glycerol in PBS) for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
7.2 Incubation with final RI matching solution (8 M urea, 80% glycerol in PBS) for 24–48 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24–48 hours)

8 Mounting and Imaging  
8.1 Mount sample in 80% glycerol in PBS with anti-fade reagent (e.g., N-Propyl Gallate, 1 mg/mL).  
8.2 Image using light-sheet or high-resolution confocal microscopy. (Temperature: RT, Time: as needed)

9 Storage (if not imaging immediately)  
9.1 Store in 80% glycerol in PBS at 4 °C. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: up to several weeks)

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488, Myosin VIIa (primary antibody) + Alexa Fluor 594 secondary, DAPI]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically designed for bone-containing tissues like the cochlea, enabling efficient decalcification and lipid removal while preserving fluorescence and tissue architecture. It allows deep imaging in intact cochlea by removing bone without damaging soft tissue structures. Phalloidin directly labels F-actin in stereocilia bundles, Myosin VIIa is a specific marker for hair cells, and DAPI labels nuclei for anatomical orientation. This combination enables precise identification of hair cells, their stereociliary bundles, and spatial relationships within the intact cochlea.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Decalcification  
1.1 Incubation with 10% EDTA in PBS (pH 7.4) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS for 3 × 1 hour to remove EDTA. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)

2 Permeabilization  
2.1 Incubation with 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS for 12 hours to enhance antibody penetration. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Blocking  
3.1 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)

4 Primary Antibody Labeling  
4.1 Incubation with anti-Myosin VIIa primary antibody diluted in blocking solution (1:200 dilution). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
4.2 Wash with PBS + 0.1% Tween-20 (PBST) for 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)

5 Secondary Antibody Labeling  
5.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated secondary antibody (goat anti-rabbit) diluted 1:500 in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
5.2 Wash with PBST for 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)

6 F-actin Staining  
6.1 Incubation with Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488 (1:200 dilution in PBS) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
6.2 Wash with PBS for 3 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)

7 Nuclear Staining  
7.1 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 dilution in PBS) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
7.2 Wash with PBS for 3 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)

8 Tissue Clearing  
8.1 Incubation with BoneClear Solution A (urea, glycerol, Triton X-100) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Incubation with BoneClear Solution B (sodium hydroxide, glycerol) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
8.3 Incubation with BoneClear Solution C (final RI matching solution, 80% glycerol in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

9 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
9.1 Incubation with 80% glycerol in PBS for imaging (RI ~1.45–1.47). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

10 Mounting and Imaging  
10.1 Mount sample in 80% glycerol in PBS with anti-fade reagent (e.g., N-propyl gallate, 1 mg/mL).  
10.2 Image using light-sheet or confocal microscopy with appropriate filter sets for Alexa Fluor 488, Alexa Fluor 594, and DAPI.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Decalcification  
1.1 Incubation with 10% (wt/vol) EDTA in PBS (pH 7.4) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.2 Replace with fresh 10% EDTA solution and continue incubation. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: Rabbit anti-Myosin VIIa (1:500), Mouse anti-Neurofilament-H (1:200) in labeling buffer (3% NGS, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
2.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100 (PBST), 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG, Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:1000 each) in labeling buffer. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
2.5 Wash with PBST, 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT)  
2.6 Incubation with Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 568 (1:200) in PBS for F-actin labeling. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.7 Wash with PBS, 3 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT)  

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS, 1 hour. (Temperature: RT)  
3.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS, 1 hour. (Temperature: RT)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS, 1 hour. (Temperature: RT)  
3.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS, 1 hour. (Temperature: RT)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% methanol, 2 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT)  

4 Delipidation  
4.1 Incubation with 1:1 (vol/vol) methanol/dichloromethane (DCM), 1 hour. (Temperature: RT)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% DCM, 1 hour. (Temperature: RT)  
4.3 Incubation with fresh 100% DCM, 1 hour. (Temperature: RT)  

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
5.1 Incubation with 1:1 (vol/vol) DCM/BABB (benzyl alcohol:benzyl benzoate = 1:2), 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% BABB, until tissue becomes fully transparent (typically 1–2 hours). (Temperature: RT)  

6 Mounting and Imaging  
6.1 Mount sample in a glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber using BABB as mounting medium.  
6.2 Seal the chamber with vacuum grease to prevent evaporation.  
6.3 Image using light-sheet or high-resolution confocal microscopy (objective: 20× or 40× water/glycerol immersion, NA ≥ 1.0).  

7 Storage (if not imaging immediately)  
7.1 Store sample in BABB at 4 °C in the dark. (Duration: up to several weeks with minimal signal loss)

1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% Tween-20 (PBST), 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)

1.5 Wash with PBST, 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
1.6 Incubation with Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 568 (1:100 dilution) in labeling buffer for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.7 Wash with PBST, 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFAP-Alexa Fluor 488, β-III Tubulin-Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole-organ clearing of fixed tissues, especially for large-scale 3D imaging of immunolabeled structures. It provides excellent tissue transparency and preservation of fluorescent signals, including Alexa Fluor dyes. The method is fast, scalable, and compatible with spinal cord dimensions. GFAP labels reactive astrocytes defining the glial scar; β-III Tubulin labels axons to assess regeneration across the scar; DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for tissue architecture and cell density analysis.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling (if not already performed)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 5% (wt/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: GFAP (1:500), β-III Tubulin (1:1000) in labeling buffer (1% DMSO, 3% serum, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 (6 × 1 hour). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit (GFAP), Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse (β-III Tubulin) at 1:1000 dilution in labeling buffer for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 (6 × 1 hour). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000) in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.7 Final wash with PBS (3 × 30 minutes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.6 Incubation with chilled 100% methanol for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1:20 dilution of 30% H₂O₂ in methanol) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 1:1 DCM:DBE for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

4 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
4.1 Incubation with 100% DBE for RI matching and long-term storage. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours for imaging readiness)

5 Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Mount sample in DBE in a custom chamber with spacers to avoid compression.  
5.2 Image using light-sheet or high-penetration confocal microscopy with appropriate filter sets for Alexa Fluor 488, Alexa Fluor 647, and DAPI.  
5.3 Perform 3D reconstruction and quantitative analysis of astrocyte density, morphology, scar thickness, and axon penetration across scar zones.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Fixation and Washing  
1.1 Incubation with 4% PFA in PBS for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)
