2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization solution (10% DMSO, 5% donkey serum, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-GFAP (1:500) and anti-Cx43 (1:300) in labeling buffer (1% DMSO, 3% donkey serum, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
2.3 Wash with PBS (0.2% Triton X-100) (5× 2 hours each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 hours total)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit (GFAP), Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-mouse (Cx43) in labeling buffer for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
2.5 Wash with PBS (0.2% Triton X-100) (5× 2 hours each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 hours total)  
2.6 Incubation with NeuroTrace (Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated) at 1:200 dilution in PBS for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
2.7 Wash with PBS (0.2% Triton X-100) (3× 2 hours each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour (2×). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)  

4 Delipidation  
4.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 5% H2O2 in methanol (1:5 dilution of 30% H2O2 in methanol) at 4 °C for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour (2×). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)  

5 Rehydration  
5.1 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.2 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.3 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.4 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.5 Incubation with PBS for 30 minutes (2×). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour total)  

6 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
6.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ RI matching solution (DBE/Toluene, 1:2 vol/vol) for 3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with 100% DBE for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

7.1 Mount the cleared spinal cord in a chamber filled with DBE.  
7.2 Image using light-sheet or high-penetration confocal microscopy (excitation wavelengths: 488 nm for GFAP, 594 nm for Cx43, 647 nm for NeuroTrace).  

8 Storage (Optional)  
8.1 Store in 100% DBE at RT for up to several weeks without significant signal loss.

**Chosen Labeling:** [GFAP+Alexa Fluor 488, β-III Tubulin+Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for large, fixed tissues like whole spinal cords due to its excellent optical clearing, compatibility with immunolabeling, and rapid processing time. It preserves fluorescence well and is compatible with multiple fluorophores, enabling multiplexed labeling of both GFAP (for astrocytic scar) and β-III Tubulin (for axons), along with nuclear counterstaining with DAPI. This combination allows precise 3D mapping of axon-scar spatial relationships.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling Preparation  
1.1 Incubation with 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS for permeabilization. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with blocking solution (10% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: GFAP (1:500), β-III Tubulin (1:1000) in labeling buffer (3% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
2.2 Wash with 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS (5× 2 hours each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 hours total)  
2.3 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit (GFAP), Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse (β-III Tubulin) in labeling buffer for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
2.4 Wash with 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS (5× 2 hours each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 hours total)  
2.5 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 in PBS) for nuclear staining. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour (2 changes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)  

4 Delipidation  
4.1 Incubation with freshly prepared dichloromethane (DCM)/methanol (2:1 vol/vol) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Replace with fresh DCM/methanol (2:1) and incubate for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Repeat step 4.1–4.2 until tissue becomes visibly transparent (typically 2–3 cycles).  

5 Rehydration  
5.1 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 15 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
5.2 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 15 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
5.3 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 15 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
5.4 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 15 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
5.5 Incubation with PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

6 Tissue Clearing  
6.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (20% DMSO, 20% NMP in methanol) for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
6.2 Replace with fresh iDISCO+ solution and incubate until full transparency is achieved (typically 2–3 days). (Temperature: RT, Time: 72 hours total)

7.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (DBE/methanol 1:1 vol/vol) for 6 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
7.2 Incubation with 100% dibenzyl ether (DBE) for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
7.3 Replace with fresh DBE and incubate for an additional 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

8 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Mount the cleared spinal cord in a custom imaging chamber filled with DBE.  
8.2 Store in sealed chamber at RT in the dark until imaging.  
8.3 Perform light-sheet or high-resolution confocal imaging to capture 3D architecture.  

**Note:** All incubations are performed with gentle shaking unless otherwise specified. Tissue should be fully submerged and protected from light during fluorescent labeling and clearing steps.

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFAP, S100β, β-III Tubulin]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for large, fixed nervous tissue like spinal cords due to its excellent preservation of fluorescent signals, minimal tissue shrinkage, and compatibility with multiple immunolabeling targets. It avoids harsh organic solvents that can degrade antigenicity and fluorescence. The selected markers—GFAP and S100β—label reactive astrocytes and glial scar, while β-III Tubulin marks axons, enabling assessment of axon regeneration across the scar. This combination meets the scientific goal without introducing new fluorophores or antigens.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling (if not already performed)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-GFAP (1:500), anti-S100β (1:200), and anti-β-III Tubulin (1:1000) in labeling buffer (1% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.01% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (6 × 1 hour). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488 anti-rabbit (GFAP), Alexa Fluor 555 anti-mouse (S100β), and Alexa Fluor 647 anti-chicken (β-III Tubulin) at 1:500 dilution in labeling buffer for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBS containing 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (6 × 1 hour). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 1 hour)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Bleaching (optional, for autofluorescence reduction)  
3.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H2O2 in methanol at 4 °C for 12–16 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12–16 hours)  
3.2 Wash with 100% methanol (2 × 1 hour). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.5 Incubation with PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

5 Delipidation & Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (20% (wt/vol) NaOH, 20% (vol/vol) DMSO in methanol) for 24–48 hours depending on tissue size. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 24–48 hours)  
5.2 Replace with fresh iDISCO+ solution and continue clearing until tissue becomes translucent (monitor visually). (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: up to 72 hours total)  

6 RI Matching  
6.1 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) DCM in methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.3 Incubation with 100% DCM for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.4 Incubation with DBE (Dibenzyl Ether) for RI matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24–48 hours)  

7 Mounting and Imaging  
7.1 Transfer spinal cord into a glass-bottom imaging dish or custom chamber filled with DBE.  
7.2 Image using light-sheet or confocal microscopy with appropriate filter sets for Alexa Fluor 488, 555, and 647.  
7.3 Store samples in DBE at 4 °C in the dark if long-term preservation is needed.

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [ChAT (to label cholinergic ICN ganglia), TH (to label noradrenergic sympathetic fibers), Phalloidin (to label F-actin in cardiomyocytes), DAPI (for nuclear counterstain)]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole-organ clearing such as mouse hearts due to its excellent optical clearing, good preservation of fluorescence from immunolabeling, and compatibility with large tissue volumes. It is a fast, organic solvent-based method that enables deep 3D imaging with light-sheet or confocal microscopy. The labeling strategy targets ChAT+ neurons (ICN ganglia), TH+ sympathetic fibers, F-actin orientation via Phalloidin, and nuclear architecture via DAPI, enabling precise 3D spatial mapping of neural and myocardial structures.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling and Staining  
1.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization solution (10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-ChAT (1:500), anti-TH (1:1000) in labeling buffer (1% DMSO, 3% donkey serum, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBST) for 6 × 2 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-goat (ChAT) and Alexa Fluor 555-conjugated anti-rabbit (TH), both at 1:500 dilution, in labeling buffer for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBST for 6 × 2 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours total)  
1.6 Incubation with Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488 (1:200) and DAPI (1:1000) in PBST for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 5% (vol/vol) H2O2 in methanol (1 volume of 30% H2O2 in 19 volumes of methanol) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 1:2 DCM:BABB (benzyl alcohol:benzyl benzoate, 1:2 vol/vol) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% BABB for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
4.1 Incubation with 1:1 BABB:DBE (dibenzyl ether) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% DBE for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with fresh 100% DBE for final RI matching (optional: up to 3 hours for full equilibration). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  

5 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Mount the cleared heart in a custom imaging chamber or glass-bottom dish using DBE as the immersion medium.  
5.2 Store in 100% DBE at 4 °C in the dark if not imaging immediately. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: up to several weeks)  
5.3 Prior to imaging, ensure sample is fully submerged in DBE and equilibrated at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1–2 hours equilibration)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [ChAT+Alexa Fluor 488, TH+Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI, IB4+Alexa Fluor 555]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole-organ clearing of small tissues like the mouse heart due to its rapid delipidation, excellent preservation of fluorescent signals (including antibody labeling), and compatibility with multiple fluorophores. It effectively removes heme pigments and lipids, which is critical for reducing red background and improving signal-to-noise. The method supports deep penetration of antibodies and dyes, making it suitable for dual labeling of ChAT (parasympathetic) and TH (sympathetic) neurons, as well as nuclear staining (DAPI) and endothelial/vasculature labeling (IB4). The refractive index (RI) matching is compatible with light-sheet or confocal imaging of intact hearts.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling and Blocking  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-ChAT (1:500) and anti-TH (1:1000) in blocking solution for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Washing with 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (6 × 2 hours). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-goat and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit in blocking solution for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.5 Washing with 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (6 × 2 hours). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours total)  
1.6 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000) and IB4-Alexa Fluor 555 (1:200) in PBS for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Bleaching  
3.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol for 12 hours to reduce heme pigmentation. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Washing with 100% methanol (3 × 1 hour). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

4 Delipidation  
4.1 Incubation with freshly prepared iDISCO+ clearing solution (200 mM dibasic sodium phosphate, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 60% (vol/vol) DMSO, 30% (vol/vol) methanol) for 48 hours. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
4.2 Replace with fresh iDISCO+ solution and incubate for another 24 hours. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 24 hours)

5.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ RI matching solution (15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 60% (vol/vol) DMSO, 25% (vol/vol) benzyl alcohol, 10% (vol/vol) benzyl benzoate) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Replace with fresh RI matching solution and incubate for another 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

6.1 Mount the cleared heart in a chamber filled with RI matching solution.  
6.2 Perform 3D imaging using light-sheet or high-penetration confocal microscopy.  

7 Storage (Optional)  
7.1 Store in fresh RI matching solution at 4 °C for up to 2 weeks without significant signal loss.

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD31+Alexa Fluor 488, LYVE-1+Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is a fast, methanol-based optical clearing method that is highly suitable for thin (1 mm) fixed tissues like mouse liver. It preserves fluorescence well, especially from Alexa Fluor dyes, and can complete clearing and refractive index (RI) matching within 24 hours. The labeling strategy uses CD31 to label all endothelial cells (including portal and larger vessels), LYVE-1 to specifically label liver sinusoidal endothelial cells, and DAPI for nuclear counterstain, enabling clear spatial orientation and segmentation of liver lobules and vascular structures.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling (if not pre-labeled)  
1.1 Incubate tissue in blocking/permeabilization solution: 0.3% Triton X-100, 10% normal goat serum in PBS (pH 7.4) for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubate with primary antibodies: rat anti-CD31 (1:200), goat anti-LYVE-1 (1:100) in 0.3% Triton X-100, 3% normal goat serum in PBS for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
1.3 Wash 3× with PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100, 10 min each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min total)  
1.4 Incubate with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rat IgG and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-goat IgG (both at 1:500) + DAPI (1:10,000) in PBS with 0.3% Triton X-100 for 6 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
1.5 Wash 3× with PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100, 10 min each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min total)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubate in 50% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubate in 70% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubate in 100% methanol twice, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)  

3 Bleaching (optional for autofluorescence reduction)  
3.1 Incubate in chilled 5% H₂O₂ in methanol for 4–6 hours or overnight. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 6 hours)  
3.2 Wash in 100% methanol twice, 30 min each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour total)  

4 Delipidation and Clearing  
4.1 Incubate in freshly prepared iDISCO+ clearing solution (60% DMSO, 30% methanol, 10% H2O in PBS) for 12–24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
5.1 Incubate in 100% dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour to remove residual methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubate in dibenzyl ether (DBE) for RI matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  

6 Mounting and Imaging  
6.1 Mount sample in DBE-filled imaging chamber.  
6.2 Image using confocal microscopy with appropriate filter sets for Alexa Fluor 488, Alexa Fluor 647, and DAPI.

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD3-Alexa Fluor 488, CD8-Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is a methanol-based clearing method that provides rapid and effective optical clearing while preserving fluorescent signals, making it ideal for 3D immunofluorescence imaging of thick paraffin sections. It is particularly suitable for distinguishing subpopulations like CD3+ pan-T cells and CD8+ cytotoxic T cells using compatible Alexa Fluor dyes. The method is compatible with common immunolabeling techniques and maintains tissue architecture well. Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 are bright, photostable, and spectrally distinct, enabling clear separation of pan-T and cytotoxic T cell populations in 3D imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling  
1.1 Incubate deparaffinized and rehydrated 500 μm human tumor section with blocking solution (10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubate with primary antibodies: anti-CD3 (1:200) and anti-CD8 (1:200) in antibody diluent (2% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.3 Wash 3× 1 hour with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  
1.4 Incubate with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500 each) in antibody diluent for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.5 Wash 3× 1 hour with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubate in 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubate in 70% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubate in 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubate in freshly prepared 5% (vol/vol) H2O2 in methanol (1:5 dilution of 30% H2O2 in methanol) at 4 °C for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubate in 70% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubate in 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubate in PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
5.1 Incubate in iDISCO+ RI-matching solution (DBE:Toluene = 1:1 vol/vol) for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.2 Incubate in 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) for clearing and final RI matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  

6 Imaging and Storage  
6.1 Mount the cleared tissue in a glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber using DBE as the immersion medium.  
6.2 Store in 100% DBE at 4 °C in the dark if imaging is not immediate. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: up to 1 week)  
6.3 Perform 3D imaging using a light-sheet or high-resolution confocal microscope optimized for DBE (RI ~1.56).

**Chosen Labeling:** [Nephrin (NPHS1)+Alexa Fluor 647, Podocin (NPHS2)+Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for thick tissue sections like 500 μm mouse kidney cortex due to its excellent optical clearing, rapid processing time, and strong preservation of fluorescent signals. It is particularly suitable for immunolabeled tissues and compatible with commonly used Alexa Fluor dyes. The selected labeling strategy targets two key components of the glomerular filtration barrier: Nephrin (a core component of the slit diaphragm) and Podocin (a key podocyte foot process protein), enabling high-resolution visualization of the glomerular architecture with high signal-to-noise ratio.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling (if not pre-labeled)
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Nephrin (NPHS1) and anti-Podocin (NPHS2) diluted in blocking solution for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with 0.1% Tween-20 in PBS (PBST), 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit and Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG diluted 1:500 in PBST for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBST, 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 1 hour)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 66% dichloromethane (DCM), 33% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Repeat step 3.1 once. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 100% DCM for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 66% methanol, 33% DCM for 15 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% methanol for 15 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
4.3 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 15 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
4.4 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 15 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
4.5 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 15 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
4.6 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 15 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
4.7 Incubation with PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

5 Tissue Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (200 mM dibasic sodium phosphate, 30% w/v sucrose, 60% v/v DMSO) for 24–48 hours. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 24–48 hours)  

6 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
6.1 Incubation with RI matching solution (80% glycerol, 20% PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Optional: Incubation with 100% glycerol for 24 hours for deeper RI matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Mount tissue in a chambered coverslip or imaging chamber using glycerol-based mounting medium.  
7.2 Seal the chamber with vacuum grease or nail polish to prevent drying.  
7.3 Store at 4 °C in the dark until imaging. (Time: up to 1 week)  
7.4 Image using a confocal or light-sheet microscope optimized for Alexa Fluor 488 and Alexa Fluor 647 fluorescence.

1 Immunolabeling  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)

1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse and Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-rabbit (1:1000 each) in labeling buffer for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)

**Chosen Labeling:** [α-SMA+Alexa Fluor 488, F-Actin+Phalloidin-iFluor 594, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for small tissue blocks like mouse heart apex due to its rapid clearing, excellent preservation of fluorescent proteins and immunolabels, and compatibility with lipophilic dyes. It allows deep penetration of antibodies and dyes, making it suitable for 3D visualization of complex structures such as coronary vasculature (via α-SMA labeling) and fibrotic regions (via F-Actin+Phalloidin for myofibroblasts). DAPI is used for nuclear counterstain to aid in segmentation and orientation.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling (if not already performed)
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: α-SMA (1:500) and F-Actin (1:200) in 3% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% Tween-20 (PBST) 5 times, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG and iFluor 594-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:1000) and DAPI (1:10,000) in PBST for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBST 5 times, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 hours total)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 5% H2O2 in methanol at 4 °C for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Wash with 100% methanol twice, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)  

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Tissue Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (20% DMSO, 20% NMP in 1×PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Replace with fresh iDISCO+ solution and incubate for another 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
6.1 Incubation with DBE (Dibenzyl Ether) for RI matching for 3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
6.2 Replace with fresh DBE and incubate for an additional 3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  

7 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Mount the cleared tissue in a glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber using DBE.  
7.2 Store in the dark at RT until imaging.  
7.3 Image using light-sheet or confocal microscopy with appropriate filter sets for Alexa Fluor 488, iFluor 594, and DAPI.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Washing and Permeabilization  
1.1 Wash fixed mouse lung tissue (PFA-fixed) in PBS (1X, pH 7.4) for 1 hour at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubate tissue in methanol series: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% methanol in PBS (each step 1 hour at RT). (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 hours total)  
1.3 Incubate in chilled 100% methanol for 2 hours at 4 °C. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 2 hours)  
1.4 Incubate in freshly prepared 5% H2O2 in methanol at 4 °C for 12 hours to enhance antibody penetration. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Incubate tissue in blocking solution: 0.2% gelatin, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS (PBGT) for 2 hours at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubate with primary antibodies: rat anti-CD31 (1:200 dilution) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated IB4 (1:500 dilution) in PBGT for 5 days at 37 °C. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 5 days)  
2.3 Wash tissue in PBGT (5× 1 hour each at RT). (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 hours total)  
2.4 Incubate with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rat IgG (1:500 dilution) in PBGT for 3 days at 37 °C. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 3 days)  
2.5 Wash tissue in PBGT (5× 1 hour each at RT). (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 hours total)

3 Nuclear Staining  
3.1 Incubate tissue with DAPI (1:10,000 dilution in PBGT) for 12 hours at 37 °C. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Wash tissue in PBGT (5× 1 hour each at RT). (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 hours total)

4 Dehydration and Clearing  
4.1 Incubate in methanol series: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% methanol in PBS (each step 1 hour at RT). (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 hours total)  
4.2 Incubate in 1:1 mixture of methanol and dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubate in 100% DCM for 2 hours at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.4 Incubate in 1:1 mixture of DCM and dibenzyl ether (DBE) for 1 hour at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubate in 100% DBE for 3 hours at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)

5.1 Transfer tissue into a glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber filled with fresh DBE. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [tdTomato, Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole mouse brain clearing with excellent preservation of fluorescent proteins like tdTomato. It is fast compared to aqueous-based methods and compatible with small fluorescent dyes such as Alexa Fluor. Phalloidin labels F-actin, a key component of the axonal cytoskeleton, and can be directly conjugated (e.g., Alexa Fluor 488) to avoid antibody penetration issues in large, intact tissues. This combination allows for rapid, high-resolution imaging of long-range projections (tdTomato) and axonal structure (F-actin), while accepting moderate tissue shrinkage.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Pre-Treatment  
1.1 Incubation with methanol (MeOH) at gradually increasing concentrations: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% (each step 2 hours at RT).  
(Temperature: RT, Time: 10 hours total)  
1.2 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H₂O₂ in methanol (1:5 dilution of 30% H₂O₂ in MeOH).  
(Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  

2 Whole-mount Staining  
2.1 Incubation with Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488 (1:200 dilution in 100% MeOH) to label F-actin in axonal skeletons.  
(Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Wash with 100% MeOH (3×, 1 hour each).  
(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

3 Delipidation and Clearing  
3.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM) for 2 hours to initiate delipidation.  
(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with DCM for 12 hours to complete delipidation.  
(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with DCM for 24 hours (final clearing step).  
(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

4 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
4.1 Incubation with dibenzyl ether (DBE) for RI matching.  
(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with fresh DBE for 24 hours (final RI equilibration).  
(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Imaging and Storage  
5.1 Mount brain in DBE-filled imaging chamber and seal with silicone grease.  
5.2 Image using light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) with appropriate filters:  
- tdTomato: Ex ~554 nm / Em ~581 nm  
- Alexa Fluor 488: Ex ~495 nm / Em ~519 nm  
5.3 Store cleared brain in DBE at 4 °C if further imaging is planned.  
(Temperature: 4 °C, Time: up to several weeks)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD31 (PECAM1), Stabilin-2] + [Alexa Fluor 488, Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole-organ clearing such as adult mouse liver due to its excellent preservation of fluorescent protein signals (e.g., Alexa Fluor dyes), compatibility with immunolabeling, and efficient delipidation without significant tissue swelling or deformation. It is particularly suitable for 3D vascular mapping with high-resolution light-sheet microscopy. The dual labeling with CD31 (a pan-endothelial marker) and Stabilin-2 (a liver sinusoidal endothelial cell-specific marker) ensures comprehensive visualization of both general vasculature and specialized liver sinusoids, avoiding underrepresentation when using only generic endothelial markers.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Fixation and Washing  
1.1 Post-fixation in 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Wash in PBS for 1 hour, repeat 3 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Incubate in blocking/permeabilization solution: 0.3% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 5% donkey serum in PBS for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubate with primary antibodies: rat anti-CD31 (1:200) and rabbit anti-Stabilin-2 (1:100) in labeling buffer (0.3% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO in PBS) for 5 days. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 5 days)

1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit, Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-mouse, Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rat (all at 1:500 dilution) in labeling buffer for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBS containing 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 6 times over 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours total)  
1.6 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 dilution in PBS) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)

2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

5.1 Incubation with 100% DBE for RI matching and long-term storage. (Temperature: RT, Time: >6 hours as needed)

6.1 Mount sample in a chamber filled with DBE.  
6.2 Image using light-sheet or high-penetration confocal microscopy with appropriate filter sets for Alexa Fluor 488, Alexa Fluor 594, Alexa Fluor 647, and DAPI.

DAPI provides nuclear contrast for anatomical registration across the embryo. NeuroTrace 500 enhances contrast for live neurons and complements the TUJ1 signal.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preparation and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with freshly prepared 4% PFA in PBS for 2 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS (3 × 1 hour) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100 for 12 hours (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Blocking: Incubation with blocking solution (10% DMSO, 5% donkey serum in PBS with 0.3% Triton X-100) for 24 hours (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody: β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) at 1:1000 dilution in blocking solution for 72 hours (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
2.3 Wash with PBS + 0.3% Triton X-100 (5 × 6 hours) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 5 × 6 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG at 1:500 dilution in blocking solution for 48 hours (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
2.5 Wash with PBS + 0.3% Triton X-100 (5 × 6 hours) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 5 × 6 hours)  

3 Whole-Embryo Nuclear Staining  
3.1 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 dilution in PBS) for 24 hours (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Wash with PBS (3 × 2 hours) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 3 × 2 hours)  

4 Whole-Embryo Live Neuron Labeling  
4.1 Incubation with NeuroTrace 500 (or similar) at 1:1000 dilution in PBS for 24 hours (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Wash with PBS (3 × 2 hours) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 3 × 2 hours)  

5 Dehydration  
5.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 2 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.6 Incubation with 100% methanol overnight (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

6.1 Incubation with freshly prepared iDISCO+ clearing solution (200 mL DCM, 100 mL MeOH, 1.5 mL 30% H2O2) for 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

7.3 Incubation with 100% BB/DBP (1:1 vol/vol) for 48 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)

8.1 Mount embryo in 100% BB/DBP in a custom imaging chamber

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: rat anti-mouse CD45 (1:200), rat anti-mouse F4/80 (1:200) in labeling buffer (1% serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% Tween-20 (PBST), 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: goat anti-rat Alexa Fluor 647 and goat anti-rat Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500 each) in labeling buffer for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBST, 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 1 hour)  

2 Decalcification and Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with decalcification solution (0.5 M EDTA, pH 8.0 in PBS) for 48 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Wash with PBS, 3 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with delipidation solution (20% methanol, 10% DMSO in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Tissue Clearing  
3.1 Incubation with BoneClear solution (40% glycerol, 20% ethylene glycol, 40% PBS with 1% Tween-20) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with BoneClear solution (50% glycerol, 25% ethylene glycol, 25% PBS with 1% Tween-20) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with final BoneClear solution (60% glycerol, 30% ethylene glycol, 10% PBS with 1% Tween-20) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

4 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
4.1 Incubation with RI matching solution (80% glycerol, 20% PBS with 1% Tween-20, RI ~1.47) for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

5 Mounting and Imaging  
5.1 Mount sample in RI-matched chamber with coverslip spacer compatible with light-sheet microscopy.  
5.2 Image using light-sheet fluorescence microscope with 488 nm and 640 nm excitation lasers.

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin/IB4-Alexa Fluor 647, Osterix (Osx)-GFP, Collagen IV-Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for hard tissues like bone, allowing for effective optical clearing while preserving native fluorescence and antigenicity. It balances demineralization and refractive index (RI) matching to maintain structural integrity of trabecular bone, marrow cavity, and intraosseous vasculature. The selected labeling strategy enables multiplex visualization: IB4 labels the luminal surface of blood vessels, Osx-GFP labels osteoprogenitor/osteoblast lineage cells, and Collagen IV highlights basement membranes of vessels and bone matrix. These fluorophores are compatible with BoneClear’s processing conditions and exhibit minimal photobleaching.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Optical Clearing  
1.1 Incubation with decalcification solution (10% EDTA in PBS, pH 7.4) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours,更换一次溶液)  
1.2 Wash with PBS for 3 × 1 hour to remove EDTA. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  
1.3 Incubation with permeabilization solution (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% donkey serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Osterix (1:200), anti-Collagen IV (Alexa Fluor 488 conjugated, 1:400) in labeling buffer (1% serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
2.2 Wash with PBS + 0.1% Tween-20 for 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
2.3 Incubation with secondary antibody: anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) for Osterix if not directly labeled, or proceed if Osx-GFP is endogenously expressed. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
2.4 Final wash with PBS + 0.1% Tween-20 for 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  

3 Lipid Clearing  
3.1 Incubation with BoneClear-L1 (20% glycerol, 2.5% urea, 10% DMSO in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with BoneClear-L2 (40% glycerol, 5% urea, 20% DMSO in PBS) for 48 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with BoneClear-L3 (60% glycerol, 10% urea, 30% DMSO in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 72 hours)  

4 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
4.1 Incubation with BoneClear-R1 (80% glycerol, 10% urea, RI = 1.46) for 48 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with BoneClear-R2 (90% glycerol, 10% urea, RI = 1.48) for 72 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 72 hours)  

5 Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Mount sample in RI-matched imaging chamber using BoneClear-R2 solution.  
5.2 Store at 4 °C in dark if imaging is not immediate. (Time: up to 2 weeks)  
5.3 For light-sheet or confocal imaging, use objectives compatible with high RI (e.g., glycerol-immersion objectives).

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + TH (酪氨酸羟化酶), CD31 + Lectin]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for clearing mineralized tissues such as bone and teeth, effectively decalcifying while preserving soft tissue morphology and fluorescent signals. It allows deep penetration and is compatible with multiple immunolabeling strategies. The labeling strategy uses β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) to label all neurons, TH to identify sympathetic innervation, and CD31 with Lectin to label vasculature, enabling multiplexed 3D visualization of neural and vascular structures within the tooth.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Pre-treatment  
1.1 Incubation with 0.5 M EDTA (pH 8.0) for decalcification. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours, with solution change every 24 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100 (PBSTx) for 3 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Blocking with 10% normal goat serum (NGS) in PBSTx for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-β-III Tubulin (1:500), anti-TH (1:200), and anti-CD31 (1:200) in PBSTx with 3% NGS for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
2.3 Wash with PBSTx for 5 × 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 hours total)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488 anti-mouse (1:1000), Alexa Fluor 594 anti-rabbit (1:1000), and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated Lectin (IB4, 1:200) in PBSTx with 3% NGS for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Brn3a (POU4F1)+Alexa Fluor 488, Brn3b (POU4F2)+Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is highly suitable for adult mouse eye tissue due to its excellent preservation of fluorescent proteins and immunolabeling, compatibility with methanol-based immunostaining, and efficient clearing of pigmented tissues like the retina. It allows deep penetration of antibodies and is particularly effective after corneal removal, which facilitates reagent diffusion. The selected labeling strategy uses two distinct Alexa Fluor dyes targeting Brn3a and Brn3b, which are specific and well-established transcription factors for retinal ganglion cell (RGC) identification. The spectral separation of Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 ensures minimal crosstalk and high-resolution dual labeling.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Brn3a (1:500) and anti-Brn3b (1:500) in labeling buffer (3% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBST), 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:1000 each) in labeling buffer for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBST, 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H2O2 in methanol (1 volume 30% H2O2 to 19 volumes methanol) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with DCM for an additional 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with dibenzyl ether (DBE) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with fresh DBE for 3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
5.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (100% DBE) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with fresh 100% DBE for imaging compatibility. (Temperature: RT, Time: overnight)  

6 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Mount sample in a glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber using 100% DBE. (Temperature: RT)  
6.2 Store in the dark at RT if long-term preservation is needed. (Temperature: RT)  
6.3 Image using light-sheet or confocal microscopy with appropriate excitation/emission filters for Alexa Fluor 488 and Alexa Fluor 647.

**Chosen Method:** ScaleS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD8+Alexa Fluor 488, CD3+Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** ScaleS is a sorbitol-based aqueous clearing method that preserves fluorescence well, especially for Alexa Fluor dyes, and is particularly suitable for pigmented tissues like human skin. It effectively reduces melanin autofluorescence through its high urea and detergent content. The method is compatible with immunolabeled tissues and allows high-resolution 3D imaging. The dual labeling of CD8 and CD3 enables distinction between total T cells (CD3+) and cytotoxic T cells (CD8+), while DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for spatial orientation.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Immunolabeling (if not already performed)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-CD8 (1:200) and anti-CD3 (1:200) in labeling buffer (1% BSA, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100 (3 × 1 hour). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500 each) in labeling buffer for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100 (3 × 1 hour). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 dilution in PBS) for nuclear staining for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours)  

2 ScaleS Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with ScaleS-1 solution (4 M urea, 10% glycerol, 10% DMSO, 1% Triton X-100 in 0.1 M PBS, pH 7.4) for pigment removal and tissue clearing. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Wash with ScaleS-W1 solution (4 M urea, 10% glycerol, 10% DMSO in 0.1 M PBS, pH 7.4) (3 × 12 hours). (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 3 × 12 hours)  

3 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
3.1 Incubation with ScaleS-R1 solution (4 M urea, 25% w/v sorbitol, 50% glycerol in 0.01 M PBS, pH 7.4) for initial RI matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with ScaleS-R2 solution (4 M urea, 40% w/v sorbitol, 60% glycerol in 0.01 M PBS, pH 7.4) for final RI matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

4 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
4.1 Mount the cleared tissue in a chamber filled with ScaleS-R2 solution for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.  
4.2 Image using a light-sheet microscope or high-penetration confocal microscope with appropriate filter sets for Alexa Fluor 488, Alexa Fluor 647, and DAPI.
